analysis.name: Ainash Childebayeva
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This was definitely one of the harder anthropology classes, especially bc I had no genetics background. She lectures very quickly, & I got points off for unimportant stuff, but she's knowledgeable. You can tell she cares more about her research than teaching. Admirable professor but not an easy class - check prior syllabi before registering.

had her for INB-337. All she does is read off the slides, no emotion, no care, nothing interesting in teaching style. She's showed up late to her own class so many times. As of right now she's been late more than on time. Class is boring and she's intentionally vague on assignments.

Lots of reading (~2 scientific papers by the start of each class). Lectures were often too fast to make time for class discussion and student lectures which were unproductive in my opinion. Very disorganized, most assignments had no rubric or clear guidelines and instructions would be changed at the last minute. Was hard to discern what she wanted.

The courseload was very heavy, office hours were often cancelled. Had to read 2 scientific research papers and a textbook chapter by every class, had a 5,000-word research paper due at end of the semester and 2 exams worth 30% of the grade. Found it hard to keep up with slides in lecture due to the speed of her lectures and lack of explaining.

NEVER take this class or anything with this teacher. She does not know what she's doing and will make you stress over the class until the last-minute. Not sure why there are random positive reviews here.

analysis.name: Alfonso Cuevas
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 48 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Do not take his course. You learn nothing. There is no curve for all his courses. Lecture is a mess. There is quiz after every lecture. The quiz is not relevant to what he said. He is happy to see students make mistakes in exam and then he would say "I made a trick on that question and many of you were wrong." The worst professor I have ever seen.

Taking a class with Cuevas is like hiking up a mountain with a man on your back who smashes your knees with a hammer every 1000 steps and then blames you for having your knees in front of his hammer. He accused a large portion of the class of cheating because they used a technique for convolution that Cuevas couldn't do. He grades very hard.

Dr. Cuevas is very respectable as an engineer. However, his teaching is not the best.   He relies heavily on the textbook, fails to clearly explain examples, and has exams that are much more difficult than they need to be. Often, it is better to just read the textbook rather than attend lecture. Too bad there's pop quizzes.

was rude when i asked for help on a problem and dismissed me. proceeded to help a student on same problem right after. TAs grade harsh on lab reports, had to chase them down for feedback. does not post lectures & thinks that benefits students in their learning.seems like i got the short end of the stick with him but he made 411 wayy too complicated

Cuevas isn't a horrible guy, so I almost feel bad writing a bad review, but the truth is he is a bad teacher. He is super knowledgeable but horrible at conveying it. While I think people exaggerate on how hard exams are (they arent bad + he's nice with partial), he doesnt teach well enough to prepare you for them, and he can be very condescending

analysis.name: Elizabeth Adams
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 44 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: This class is a simple but engaging VAPA that Dr. Adams structured to be easy. The class is beyond manageable and has little to no workload as long as you pay attention to the lectures, do the readings, and study a bit for the weekly quizzes. There were no exams in the class, and instead of a final, there is a fun final project. Highly Recommended!

I'd die for Lizzy. If you didnt like her you probably thought you could get away with doing nothing, which is just plain lazy and you only have yourself to blame. Loved her lectures, she's so funny. Have to buy tophat for attendance. No tests, just weekly quizzes with 2 drops and a final project. Loved this class so much, it was really interesting.

I fell ill and had to drop.  The nature of the course is fast paced but I love the way she has the course structured and once I understood the flow it got so much easier.  It takes time to learn another language but the way she teaches does make it really fun. I plan to take her class again.

One of my favorite classes I've taken at UT I'm a classics minor but I feel like even if you don't know anything about classics it's very accessible. Dr. Adams pairs the readings and movies so well and it is just such an interesting class. I'm also not a big horror movie person but still loved it, definitely recommend. Also not too much work!

Dr. Adam's is a lively and compassionate professor, who clearly understands her class is a VAPA that's not meant to be hard or time consuming. Graded mainly by participation in class and 2-ish weekly reading assignments that are chill. Quizzes every Friday that are specific, but no tricks and are pulled straight from lecture. Super chill class!

analysis.name: Anthony Conway
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 29 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment:
Prof: 

Conway is the best professor out of the many subpar ones in UT math. His teaching: show/tell/apply format.

Class:

Exams based on HW QB. HW:10 problems weekly. Attendance is not required. Great online notes.

Ad. Notes:

UT shows a grading curve with a few C's, D's, and F's. Those are students who do not show up at all, or skip every exam.

Don't take this course (at least w/ this professor) unless you are knowledgeable in notation and proofs. I took this after multiple stats and upper division math courses, and I'm so lost. He rarely goes step-by-step. Tests are representative of hw, but are still difficult if you don't memorize every proof. Professor is clearly knowledgeable though.

Fall 2025. Lowest 3 HW and lowest midterm get dropped. Midterms and final are multiple-choice and based on HW. Discussions are for extra practice, not mandatory. Super easy if you've taken calc before and still very doable if you haven't. In lecture, I like how he proved why everything makes sense. Overall great guy, definitely take him!

Best math course I've had in my life. I've taken Calc AB and BC in high school, but felt like I needed a refresher. I love how he explains things and I genuinely wanted to go to every lecture. He proves how everything makes sense there was really no memorization needed. He drops the lowest midterm and lowest few homeworks. Super cool and funny guy.

Probably best professor I'll ever have. Went to almost every office hour and enjoyed every moment talking to this Swiss guy. Could tell he's very passionate about math and answered questions about anything. Explained concepts in a way that proved everything he taught but no proofs. Clear class outline and almost no work to be done. Wish he did 408D

analysis.name: Aaron Zimmerman
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Physics at UT in general will be difficult, keep that in mind. With that being said, Professor Zimmerman is who you want to take if you're trying to actually learn physics while maintaining a high GPA. Very engaging and useful lectures. Extremely beneficial extra credit for just showing up to class. Office hours are also unmatched. My favorite prof

Best prof I've ever had. Lectures were amazing as he taught physics 2 in the most digestible way possible. If you can do HWs, you will be fine on the exam. +5 points on final grade was offered just for doing InstaPolls for completion. Don't worry about taking the class in community college; take physics 2 with Zimmerman and you will thank me

Lectures are always engaging and material is taught with clarity. Be sure to attend every lecture for up to 5% extra credit on the final, also helps you not get behind. Discussion sections are unnecessary & late but required to attend. Make sure to make an equation sheet for the exam- its very clutch. Very fair professor, 10/10.

He is amazing! He made attendance for extra 5 percent of the total grades which makes the total grade to 105. Keep attending the class and stay in touch with him, and don't hesitate to reach out if you have any questions, and you will get a satisfying grade in this his class! This class is worth being taken with him!!!

Professor Zimmerman was great at lecturing and was able to effectively teach all the material. However, I didn't like that the 3rd test took identical questions from the homework which isn't an accurate representation of performance (just memorizing).The discussion sections were mid, but the timing was horrible.

analysis.name: Ari Adut
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Adut is kind, approachable, and a very skilled lecturer. Attendance isn't mandatory BUT coming to class helps a ton, especially if you do not do the readings. Three tests count for 100% of your grade but they are straightforward.This class is a breeze as long as you pay attention, take notes, and go to the review sessions.

This class was probably the easiest class I have taken in university, although it can be boring at times. Dr. Adut is a very kind person, so the class felt very relaxed. I would definitely take again.

Prof Adut is very knowledgable/passionate about what he teaches. Attendance isn't mandatory, but if you show up and take good notes then you will do quite well on his tests. The course was made up of 3 written exams, no final.

Honestly, I don't advocate skipping class but if you were to only show up to the review and memorized it, you'd pass with a B. No joke. Don't bother buying the book, NEVER miss review day, but don't buy the book.

Dr. Adut was a great professor and lecturer, wanting his students to constantly participate. Attendance isn't mandatory, but if you skip class you will miss all of the information on the exams. Don't bother buying the books, I never needed to read them because Dr. Adut was so good at explaining the information. Take this class!

review_highlights.comment: The class content is fairly easy and gives some extra credit. Implemented a restroom policy because it is a "disruption" when people get up.

Half of the class is think-pair-share. Little structure and no concrete understanding of crucial topics that need to be taught, and not talked about.

GOAT, she wants u to succeed. be prepared to write/study and ur good. Quizzes are random, be there for attendence (though not mandatory). Recommend using NoteBook LM or Quizzify to study as its content heavy. Feedback is specific, use it to improve and exams depend a lot on slides. Overall, great professor, would take again :)

Dr. Garcia is actually amazing. She was one of my first professors at UT, and she made the class so engaging and helpful! Not to mention, she was very funny. She cares a lot about her students and actually puts effort into making sure you understand the concepts. Take her!
I just put the previous rating and I meant to give her 5 stars! LOL shes great

CFD is an extremely hard subject but Prof. Bisetti is obviously an expert and is amazing at teaching it. Overall, hard class but amazing teacher.
Get ready to work in this class. The topic he teaches is difficult, but he makes the content even more complicated. Very strict and has no compassion for his students.

Dr. Bisetti is a fantastic professor. His understanding of and enthusiasm for the topic are unmatched, and he is extremely helpful if you seek guidance outside of class. The course is very difficult, but this is the nature of the subject. I think Bisetti does a good job of making it manageable without losing rigor.
Good luck in this class. It will take up all of your waking and sleeping hours

analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 40 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Clinical psych with Bradbury is one of the best classes in the psych major. TAKE IT. Her lectures are super interesting and easy to understand and readings aren't too heavy. Quizzes could sometimes be hyper-specific but as an online asynch course I get that. She was very nice and helpful over email too!

EASY A. Take this class if you need a UGS class! Amazing professor who is super understanding and laid back. Very few not hard assignment. Laid back about due dates and can miss about 10 classes without it effecting your grade. Genuinely a good person to talk to and have as a recommendation.

I really hated how this class was formatted. We had quizzes almost every other day, and the material itself wasn't hard but rather the amount of readings and lectures she provided was too much to do in a short amount of time. Each quiz was spaced out 2-3 days. Dr. Bradbury herself is fine, lectures tend to be repetitive and unnecessarily long.

I love Dr. Bradbury! Her lecture were so informative of the material covered and she also offered so much advice in life, like how to stay positive and optimistic. Class was graded on 1 quiz per week on the lecture material and there were 2 video projects.

Not a psych major, took this class cause online/async/easy and it was. But writing this RMP because Dr. B is genuinely such a kind soul, sometimes her positivity helped me during the semester for other things. I wish I had her optimism and positivity...

He clearly loves what he teaches. His lectures are funny at times but always engaging. If you do the readings and pay attention to the lectures you should do fine on his written tests.

I loved Professor Brower, he's genuine and sweet and very respectful of student opinions. Class is very lecture heavy with some discussion involved. He's very passionate about the topic. Main grade comes from 3 exams which are just an essay question, and he never gives out 100s but I also don't know anybody that scored lower than an 85 so.

Great instructor and very well organized. He teaches practical knowledge and designs the homework and exams to be complementary. Nice person. Very helpful. Optional field trip and visit to core facilities. Cares about students.

analysis.name: Catherine Pratt
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I attended class religiously at the beginning and had lots of good notes at the start of the semester, the last two months of the fall semester I stopped going to lectures. My notes from the beginning of the semester were enough to complete basically all the written assignments and online quizzes. Easy A. The lectures were cool.

She has a very clear structure to her class which makes staying up to date easy if you do your part.  She is so passionate about her subject and it makes the lectures so engaging.  I really can't say enough good things about her and her course.
I loved the material and she is very passionate about her subject.  She has a very clear structure for how her class runs and it is easy to keep up is you do the reading and pay attention in lecture.

Prof. Pratt is very knowledgeable and kind. I would recommend going to lectures to get the content you need for weekly quizzes, though they can be a little dull. The assignments were generally easy and interesting. Textbook isn't necessarily required but can be helpful as a source for the final project. I enjoyed this class! Good for a VAPA credit.

You can tell Dr. Pratt has a genuine passion for what she teaches. The class is not hard at all if you go to her lectures (I recommend you do; they are not uploaded & contain specific facts that will be on the quizzes). The TA grades everything, is super nice, and holds weekly SI sessions that help. I would recommend if you need an easy VAPA.

review_highlights.comment: In Dr. Cheadle's defense, I think this is a really hard class to make interesting. Fortunately, homework and tests are straightforward and you get a lot of time to do them.

he's really nice, but his lectures are actually so boring and pointless. attendance is technically mandatory, but it wasn't consistently recorded. he just reads off the slides, and i feel like it's a very textbook and TA dependent class, not too hard if you teach it to yourself, but just be aware that you need to lock in and u cant depend on prof

He was not willing to work with students and didn't take accountability. He would show up late to class every day. The review classes had no planning. A really boring lecturer who manages to get sidetracked every 5 minutes. Definitely would not take him again!

Very nice guy, lectures could be kind of boring sometimes but concepts overall not hard. Reading the textbook and making sure you understand it is essential to the class. As someone with zero stats experience I found this class pretty fun.
Professor Cheadle is very nice and accommodating. Course lectures were a bit boring, but course content was not difficult and overall the class was easy for a stats course.

analysis.name: Christopher  McClellan
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: Risk Management made simple. Lots of industry experience as he actually still works and just comes into UT to teach this one class one semester a year. No textbook, no homework and yet this is the class I learn the most in. Worth the 8am start.

This class is only available at 8 am, but he made waking up at 8 am manageable. He is very knowledgeable and a great lecturer. He makes an effort to get to connect with his students and answers emails pretty quickly. He only grades on 3 exams, which is difficult, but as long as you study and memorize the terms, you should be fine.

Prof McClellan is easily one of my favorite profs at UT. He cares deeply about his students' success in his class and makes everything very simple. No textbook, no homework, just 3 exams that you will easily ace if you attend class. He brought everyone breakfast tacos one morning just because. That's the kind of prof McClellan is.

I have never been inspired to wake up for an 8 am until I took this class. The lectures are easy to follow, entertaining, and pertain to real life. He is kind, funny and makes waking up early worth it. Tests are based off stuff in the class so going makes a huge impact on your grade. 10/10 would take again.

Professor McClellan was an amazing professor. He genuinely cared about his students and you could tell he loved what he was teaching, if I could take this class again I would. Only downside is that its an 8 am class but I looked forward to going everytime.

review_highlights.comment: This class got so much harder this semester. Long tophat homeworks, insane amount of reading, lectures are rushed, and exams worth 70% of your grade that are graded extremely harshly by TA's. Way too much work and stress for a VAPA. Very hard to get an A.

I agree that Dr. Curtis is very knowledgeable about mythology but the readings are just a killing. I stopped reading all together and just took detailed notes of his lectures, I mean word for word of what he was saying. He gives assignments with all possible questions and I would just memorize the answers and my essays. Too much work for LAC credit

He recently changed the format of the class. You will have to memorize 200-300 words for each exam. Exams are every other Monday, so your Sundays will have to be dedicated to studying. There's so much homework that is lengthy and difficult, and his powerpoints are useless. I have a 3.9 GPA and this is the hardest, worst class I have taken at UT.

Good class to meet a flag if you need one! 4 tests for 80% and cumulative tophat for 80% of the final grade. Tests (which were directly from worksheets he posts for every lecture) consist of MC (20%), short answer (30%), and one essay (50%). Attendance isn't mandatory but he goes into detail in the lecture that you wouldn't get if you skipped.

Everything is based on the lectures, so if you don't go you're going to fail regardless of whether you read the textbook or not. The TA was beyond obnoxious and rude - thought she knew everything. I had high hopes for Curtis, but he wasn't very responsive nor did he seem to care about his students grades.

He will scare you into studying about 3 times what you need to know for exams, but will set you straight during exam reviews.

Pretty easy overall. Just go over the powerpoints.

Moser is an alright professor, sometimes the modules can be very dry and he stumbles on his words often. The class really wasn't that bad; as long as you keep up with the module videos and read the class google docs before a test, you will be fine. The people saying this is the hardest class they have taken haven't taken a STEM course at UT.

analysis.name: Michael Sailors
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 97 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Super easy VAPA if you just do the work. About 1, 5 question quiz a week and all the answers can be found word for word in the previous lecture. Majority of your grade comes from Cerego Homework which is so easy as long as you just do it. You are required to go to two jazz concerts a semester and write a 500 word paper but its graded super easy.

Cerego is a bit annoying but easy to complete. Lectures are 15- 30-ish minutes have 6-8 instapolls and there's like 6 per module and 4 modules per week. great guy, DO CEREGO AND LISTENING QUIZZES. Those will TANK your grade if you forget. Easy class jsut keep up

Honestly ended up finding the content very interesting, despite not really enjoying jazz prior to taking this class. Now, I really can appreciate jazz whenever I hear it! The lectures are great and interesting, and the Cerego sets are totally manageable as long as you don't start late. Really easy class that I really enjoyed.

Dr. Sailors was a great professor and made jazz fun and exciting. The part of going to concerts for a grade and writing about them was fun. Make sure you show up to every class for your instapolls there's a lot (100, graded for 90). Overall the class was very enjoyable.

Girl. Just take this class. You don't need to love jazz, but it's definitely an easy class. That said, it does come with work but it's nothing that should be giving you a headache. Only thing that may be bothersome to some people is to actually go out to a concert. I went to the free UT Jazz Combo nights at Mozarts and loved it.

analysis.name: Michael Pyrcz
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The course lacks clear structure and often emphasizes methods that feel less relevant than modern approaches. Topics are covered too quickly, and explanations to questions can be unclear or superficial. Assignments focus mainly on adjusting parameters rather than demonstrating deeper understanding

He says he cares about his students but all he cares about is himself and his advancement towards I don't know what goals. Egocentric and hidden agendas. Do not trust him 
Quirky, strange, scolds you and is passive aggressive. Do not believe what you see.
His mind is a mess.

I took the Subsurface Machine Learning course in Fall 2025. Although this is 3rd ML class I am taking in graduate level, I learned tons of new things. He has the best slides ever. He also provides interactive dashboards for playing around and understanding concepts intuitively.
He is a good and considerate Professor!

Dr. Pyrcz is a nice professor who will gladly listen to your concerns and questions. The only thing is that his class is hard to understand if you do not have a background in data science since he goes very fast through his lectures and does not relate it back to why it is practical to learn this stuff. Grading is easy and midterms are not hard.

analysis.name: Matthew Morris
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 67 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Morris is straightforward with his expectations, also very understanding. I am introverted so I was nervous starting out, but his teaching style has made it not so scary. He does grade hard on the written work and not so hard on the speeches (very generous). Dry humor and monotone delivery can make lectures boring, but I would recommend.

soooo boring. He also grades most things out of 50 so a few points off and youre already at an A-. Apparently his grading isn't as bad as the other profs though. Lectures aren't relevant, textbook is unneccessary, but overall haven't had to put too much effort in either. Exams are online open note

Almost everyone gets an A-, but actually take his feedback and he will grade easier.  The TA grades harder than him on written assignments, but he grades really easily on speeches.  He is really nice and easy to talk to.  Class is easy and you can just do other work on your laptop.  Most of the grade comes from the capstone, so work on that early.

He's not a bad professor; however, for what this class is, he grades unnecessarily hard, and gives so so much busy work. The capstone project at the end of the semester ends up being 40-50 pages long and is due during finals week. Why..

You will probably get an A- in this class, but if you can, there are just so many better options for professors.

Funny guy, Boring Lecture. Use AI for grammar quizzes and online tests to make sure you get 100s. Then for every other assignment, you will get an A- no matter what. If you're lucky, everything will average out to a 94. Also, in the syllabus, there are easter eggs of things you should submit pictures of to get extra credit.

analysis.name: Robert Newberry
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 48 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: this man is the goat. I hope this dude wakes up in the morning knowing that this world is a better place with him in it. actually helps you learn stuff, gives very very fair tests, and he's just him in general. I hope bro has an ice cold pillow on both sides every night

Newberry was an amazing professor! Ochem is a hard class, but he made it almost "easy" to succeed. Use the old exams and hw's to study, bc the exam structures are identical. GO TO OFFICE HOURS (John's were amazing) they help sm with really breaking down the material. Also, dw abt the final being worth a lot, if you study you WILL do well! TAKE HIM!

My favorite prof ever! Lectures were very helpful, I really recommend going to every lecture you can- it's better in person imo. 3 exams but he drops one, and he tells you exactly how each exam will be/the type of questions, you know exactly what to study for- he never tricks you. Lots of hw/quizzes get dropped too, but each prepares you for exams.

Dr. Newberry is an excellent professor who actually makes Ochem interesting and simple to understand! His class is structured extremely well, and he provides plenty of resources outside of lectures to get your questions answered and help prepare you for the exams. One thing I will say is that I wish he did more practice questions during lectures!

By far one of the most enjoyable and one of my fav profs at UT. Newberry takes difficult material and breaks it down during lecture in a way that really helps you understand the underlying concepts behind reactions. Exams are all very fair and structured identically to the practice exams that have video explanations. Wish he was teaching OCHEM2

analysis.name: Nicolas Reyes
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 102 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Had some of the best reviews for a calc prof but his switch from online exams to in person broke this class. Quizzes are two questions completely free response and weighted almost identically to the midterms. They are super difficult and they are NOT curved. I finished 408C with a 98 and am struggling to do well on his quizzes.

The professor described the quiz on proofs of reductions as “easy,” many students who don't work with this material found it quite challenging. The topic was not clearly explained during the TA discussion, which made the quiz harder to prepare. I would not be surprised if the scores were curved. lectures are sporadic and are not clear.

Reyes style of teaching, syllabus, and just general vibes from him have changed. Maybe something having to do with new math department guidelines as he mentioned on our first day. The main issues are homework not correlating to lectures, discussions being overly hard, and just in general no synchronization between the many parts of the course.

This class feels completely inconsistent compared to last semester. Previously, exams were online and the course structure reflected that format. This semester, exams were suddenly moved to fully in-person, which felt like a major shift without adequate adjustment in teaching or preparation. Expectations changed, but the support did not.

I had high hopes for this class, but overall it was one of the most frustrating academic experiences I've had. The transition from online to fully in-person came halfway through the year with no clear explanation or advance warning. That change made planning around other classes and responsibilities much more difficult.

analysis.name: Nathan Stone
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Stone is a hilarious and interesting guy, this class is definitely tougher than other ugs but he makes it easier by giving lots of feedback and being very forgiving. he siad he'd cut back on readings this semester but everything that was required was immensely interesting and his experiences made the class very enjoyable

lots of reading, some difficult essays to write, but Dr. Stone is very caring and always gave detailed feedback, and guided class discussions when necessary. this class is a bit more work than other ugs, but Dr. Stone isn't a harsh grader. i feel like i learned a lot in this class, so i would recommend to anyone genuinely interested in the subject

Professor Stone is a great Spanish professor. He was one of the most inspirational professors I've had in Spanish as he actually made me want to put in extra effort to learn. This class does move really fast, I felt like we never had time to fully talk about grammar topics so be prepared for that. Do your work and talk to him, he's awesome

Dr. Stone is a very nice and funny guy, and his class was relatively easy; lenient and willing to work with you. A lot of assignments both inside and outside of class, but normal for a language class at UT. My only complaint is that sometimes lectures can feel very random, and at times I've left lectures not knowing what I should've taken away.

Stone is a very inspiring Spanish professor who cares about his students. He is extremely accommodating and laid-back, but he is still extremely knowledgeable about Spanish and doesn't reward laziness. He is very accommodating, too.

analysis.name: Nicole Butterbaugh
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment:
The most impressive part of this class is how simple material was turned into an unnecessarily harsh and mind-numbing course. Feedback didn't improve grades, studying didn't help exams, and missing class meant penalties with no leniency. 

The course could have been more manageable and engaging. Frustrating and poorly handled, I hope she eases up.

Do not take her if you have any other option. To say the least, the assignments were odd, with poor instructions, and poor explanations when you asked for clarification.  The only thing you could do for a test was pray, most of the topics on the tests we never covered. And the group project, all I can say is good luck.

Do NOT take this class. I thought it wasnt going to be that bad but it is. The lectures are so boring and there is SO much work. The tests are hard and she is not the nicest. Seriously take any other class. Especially if you know you already have a busy semester!

The material was easy to learn, and although the assignments did not have the clearest instructions, they were also pretty straightforward. When asking questions for help, she wasn't the most helpful or nicest, but she did her job I guess.
Rudest professor I've ever had. How do you teach a communications class but lack all communication and leadership skills?

analysis.name: Sean Neagle
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: AMAZING professor. One of my favorite classes I've ever taken (I'm a STEM major btw, so definitely not up my usual alley). Lectures were very engaging and genuinely interesting. 90% of your grade is based on the test, very easy if you attend lectures and pay attention. Reading does not affect your grade at all so don't bother.

I had this professor for my first year at UT Austin First, if you want to be successful in his class PAY attention . The three exams make up 90% of your grade so if you fall behind then your grade is pretty much cooked. However his gradings are fair. The test is based on lecture notes, no suprises. Genuinely good teacher, cares about his class

He's alright as a teacher. His 318 was a solid intro class. I like that he fostered discussions rather than yapping at us. I just don't like the fact that the entire class is based on three in-class essay exams because if you mess up one like I did, you're simply cooked.

analysis.name: Alison Norman
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 162 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Just another typical UT CS professor. She cares more about whether her students are cheating or not then if they are understanding the material. Projects are hard, but not impossible if you give up on all of your social life. Test are easier than projects, but a lot of people don't study much because of the extremely long projects. Just work hard.

She cannot help much with the projects.  Tests are overly hard, made a day or so before giving them.  No clear grading rubric.  Homework is not checked, maybe waiting over a month for project grades, and you will go into tests not really knowing where you stand if you really grasp the concept.  Professor covers way too much information between test

If I could rate any lower, I would. The group projects are unnecessarily time-consuming and quite literally take a consistent daily effort of 4-5 hours. The tests always nitpick on the smallest detail mentioned on the slides. Dr. Norman is a nice person but that doesn't help the fact that her class is literally a full-time job. PintOS is just a no.

One of the worst professors at UT, not because of her teaching, but because of her grading system. The grading system is designed to make you fail. Also, lectures are pretty much useless as all the learning is done in pre-lecture videos (can take 1-2 hours). Projects are difficult and very time consuming, expect about 30-40 hours per week.

Norman is super nice and a great lecturer. She always asks if anyone has any questions at every opportunity. The reason the class is so difficult is 1) There is A LOT of material you have to know 2) The projects are LONG. 40 hours a week long. My only critique is her tests are garbage. Reviewing past tests is A MUST to understand grading criteria.

analysis.name: Natalie Czimskey
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 72 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I LOVED taking Dr.Czimskey's class. She also has the "Longhorn Friday" where, if ALL class wears burnt orange on Friday, she will bring either treats next class or add extra points. She will also allow you to give burnt orange items to classmates before class. She is very funny during lecture and you have access to all ppt. on Canva.WILL take again

She is amazing as always, phonetics content is very overwhelming at first but makes sure her students fully grasp the info. Her and her TA are very easy to reach outside of class and will help you in anyways they can. She makes sure we get the printed out version of the lectures and I think it helps a lot more than typing it out on a computer!

sweetest professor ever! I look forward to her classes every week. Easy to get in contact with, inclusive with all students, explains material in a way that's easy to understand. Love going to office hours and just chatting with her! Would definitely take any and all of her classes again.

EXTREMELY caring and accessible prof. Attendance isn't mandatory. All tests are online and not monitored (she respects our privacy and trusts students not to cheat). I am not an SLHS major, but she made the class fun. Also, an optional final to replace the lowest test grade. Only con is that there's very few assignments outside of the tests.

Great option to take as a science core class, even if you aren't an SLH major. Dr. Czimskey is funny, engaging, and is truly passionate about her field. Make sure to take notes in class as the slides don't cover everything you need to know. Very helpful in office hours if any guidance is needed.

analysis.name: Mina Ogando-Lavin
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Don't skip class, because if you do you won't know what vocab she's quizzing you on in the next class. There is a homework assignment before every single class, but they are super easy. Her classes are very relaxed, and as long as you're speaking spanish she really doesn't care what you're talking about. She just sets you loose to chat all class.

Mina's a great professor, does her best to keep the class engaged and is very nice. The class itself was relatively chill, and you'll pass as long as you stay on top of your work. An A is very much possible if you study.

Condescending, rude. Have to buy a $150 workbook she wrote which you barely use. Grading isnt the best, besides exams and quizzes, some assignments are graded purely on how she feels about you. I could've gotten an A since my exam/quiz/homework grades were high, but I left with an A- because she felt like I wasnt a good student? Make it make sense!

I learned SO much in this class. It was a super organized/structured class, which I loved. There were a lot of assignments, but this kept me on track. I wouldn't say it's difficult to get a good grade in this class. I would turn in things late and Prof. Ogando was so accommodating. I would love to take another class with Prof. Ogando.

Sometimes she would make me feel dumb in class, and the way that the grammar rules are explained are very hazy. You have to rely on the homework to decipher what grammar rules you're learning in class, because it's very applied in the classroom. She has a lot of energy but doesn't facilitate the best learning environment

analysis.name: Shannon O'Brien
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 95 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Lets just throw together 2 tests worth most of your grade while giving a study guide each with 300 terms then calling it a day. The tests are written as if they're open note and with 300+ terms in each test, pray youre lucky and get easy ones, every mistake is costly and getting 2-3 more wrong is a letter grade difference. Terrible grading system

Anything you heard before Fall 2025 about this class IT HAS CHANGED!!! Tests are honorlock and you are expected to know over 300+ vocab terms for each test. In retrospect if you have the time every week to listen to 10 lecture vids each being 45 min you should be okay in the class but If you're looking for an easy A+ I wouldn't take this class.

She's funny... But that's all I really got. The each test is 27% of your grade. Involves memorizing over 300 words, CLOSED BOOK/NOTE. In my opinion, the exams seem to be formatted like they're open book/note (like they were previously), but the percentage it takes up in the class does not reflect the increased difficulty for students.
Tests are implemented so students suffer and make sure your grade stays down. Interesting lectures ig

Uses honorlock. Optional prerecorded lectures. Very light workload. For exams, lots of terms to memorize. If you watch all the lecture videos (3 hrs/wk) and pay attention, you'll do fine on exams. Little EC/No curve. Answers emails quickly (same with TAs)

analysis.name: Yukie Okada
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I took business Japanese with Okada Sensei, and although the content was challenging at times, she tries her best to help us understand. She is always very kind, has helpful office hours, and explains stuff in English when Japanese is difficult. Attendance is important and there are daily quizzes, but they aren't hard to study for. I recommend!

Okada Sensei is a very kind and understanding professor. She helped me ease back into Japanese after an 8-month hiatus and really pushed me to develop my speaking and listening skills. Her class is difficult, but if you really make an effort, it feels more like a fun challenge than anything else.

-1% off your final grade for every absence (3 dropped), there are lectures every day!! 3 late = 1 absence, even a second late will be counted!! Ridiculous, as if missing the daily quiz wasn't already a penalty don't take her there are way better professors

analysis.name: Diana Orozco-Lapray
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. O was such an amazing professor. At first, the exams can seem very daunting and the lectures seem fast paced. However, you get used to it and her lectures are very engaging. There are many extra credit opportunities and a chance to replace your lowest exam grade. Dr. O is so kind and understanding, and most of all deeply knowledgeable. TAKE HER

Dr.O is an amazing professor! Her class is one of the few that I made sure I attended despite her not taking attendance most days. Her lectures were engaging, fun, and interesting. Your grade is exam heavy, but she offers extra credit at the end of the year. Exams were tough but mostly everything is covered in lecture.

This professor is AMAZING. She is kind, loving, and treats her students like her own kids. Her class is normally paced, and the lab is one of my favorite things I've done in college. If you have the opportunity to, TAKE HER. SHE IS BEYOND INCREDIBLE!!!!

She is a very knowledgeable and kind professor. Her class is attendance optional. Test material comes entirely from lectures/recording. Other assignments are weekly quizzes/written assignments/activity. No test review but easy to study for just review notes/lecture recordings. She is very approachable for questions or office hours. I recommend her.

I loved Dr. O's class! So much wonderful info and very relevant to the world. She hasn't taught 313 in a while, so the class is still changing. 3-4 Exams + Lab portion with 2 easy papers! Lab grade is separate. Tests are open-note + online, but I would study for them. I learned a lot in this class! She wants you to do well! Incredibly knowledgeable

analysis.name: Ryosuke Okuno
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This professor is dismissive, unapproachable, and unsupportive. He rarely helps, lets his ego dominate, and speaks negatively about students behind their backs. Even though I earned an A, I would not recommend taking his class.
Lectures are disorganized and difficult to follow. He is unapproachable and often impatient when students ask questions during office hours, despite putting on a forced, insincere smile.
Barely learned anything. Lectures were messy and unprepared, and most of the time it was hard to tell what he was even trying to teach. Worst professor I have ever had.

analysis.name: Shannon O'Brien
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 113 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: I LOVED Shannon's class. Great intro professor, makes it interesting for all the non-majors. Very clear on grading, tells you exactly what to study on the tests. As long as you take good notes in class, do the assignments (super easy), and read the textbook, it's incredibly easy to get an A. Also, she's super helpful in office hours and very kind.

Dr. O'Brien is a cool and funny teacher. This class isn't hard. Just don't overthink her tests. She really doesn't try to trick you. I would recommend using quizlet to study! Go to her office hours. She's super chill and easy to talk to. I overall enjoyed this class and she made this subject intresting. Lastly, you don't have a final! Great teacher

ALL reviews before fall 25 are INVALID. The class changed and now has HonorLock proctored and closed note exams. There are only TWO exams for the whole semester each with about 400 terms. You can study for days, and still do bad on the exams, if you don't memorize every single term. Such a horrible class that you unfortunately have to take for CORE

Yk that scene from mean girls when she's writing in the book screaming and crying. That's me with this course. Exams require honorlock and you can't use any notes, despite being able to use them on assignments and quizzes. I'd rather she say we can't use notes on anything because why have I been writing stuff down just to not use them on exams???

The lectures are long, only to be followed by 5-10 question assignments that often have nothing to do with her lectures. Taking notes is close to pointless and time consuming. Midterm and final questions are pulled from a random test bank, so be prepared to memorize literally 300 terms, only to get a random 50. Tests are hard but assignments arent.

analysis.name: Youjeong Oh
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Oh is very smart, but not a good teacher. She also can make an lecture 2x longer than it should be, and 4x more dull. Her attendance policy is very strict, so don't miss any class or your grade will suffer immensely. She did not post a grade the entire semester. Her grading system is also very opaque, which makes it difficult to succeed.

Dropped this class during sylly week. Extremely rigid policies: only one excused absence, no exceptions, plus strict rules on tardiness and screen use. For a 9AM class, this felt out of touch. She framed the course as “easy” because there were no closed-note exams. I wouldn't recommend her unless you need the class to graduate.

I thought this class was a free A, but the final caused my grade to drop to a B+. Graded on attendance, 2 reaction papers, and the final, which is a take-home. I believe the average for the final was around 60%. Most of the time, lectures are boring unless you are interested in South Korean history. I struggled to stay awake for this class.

If you are a cns student looking for an easy foreign culture class DO NOT take this course. They completely screwed us over on the final exam paper. The average was a 18.6 out of 30. Attendance was mandatory every day and there is a separate participation portion so you have to be active in class. Worst class I have taken by far.

This professor takes absolutely no care in the world about her students. The grading system is horrible and she does not care about whether students pass or not. The lectures are long and grueling and she expects you to retain information while consistently talking in the same tone and not making the lecture engaging at all.

analysis.name: Pauline Turner Strong
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Strong is phenomenal and cares about all of her students. She's a great resource to learn about various programs and specialties, and is always willing to help. She's also a very knowledgeable lecturer. The class is completely discussion-based, so come with readings done. There's a lot of reading, but that's to be expected of an honors class.

Dr. Strong was a great professor, and the workload was manageable. There was quite a bit of reading, but the required papers are easy to write. The class is heavily discussion based, so it's important to be in class and jump into the conversation. Overall, it was a great class, and I recommend the professor!
I loved all the exposure she provided to the world of Museums.

there wasn't an option for it, but i took her for ANT 302. she was an extremely good professor in my opinion. she has a really good way of tying anthropological concepts to current issues. my favorite class this semester, easily. great discussions

Professor Strong is one who genuinely cares for her students and their well-being. She is extremely knowledgeable on a variety of topics and only assigned 4 essays and 4 group projects. I definetley believe that your success in this class will depend on who the TA is. Be prepared to read; I suggest buying audio books. Attendance matters.

analysis.name: John Osborn
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: Everything (including some exams) is collaborative, essays are not bad, and the content is very manageable. If you can look at definitions/theorems and apply them, you can do the proofs in this class. He's a nice guy but particular about notation and formalities. Be respectful and you'll be fine. Probably the easiest class in the department.

GOAT! Tests are identical to assigned study problems (or similar methods to solve). 6 quizzes, 2 dropped. GO TO DISCUSSION!! HELPS A LOT FOR PREPARING FOR TESTS AND QUIZZES. No graded homework, but they were useful as practice for exams. 

I personally didn't think he was the best lecturer, but he makes the class easy if you put in a little effort.

Gives you almost, if not the exact questions that will be on the midterm. Midterms are five questions and he gives you 12 to study, which is extremely manageable. TA was fantastic and explained solutions very clearly. Lecture is a little theory heavy, but solutions to every homework are posted in a timely manner. Take him if you want an A.

Lectures are useless, but TA sections are GREAT. I didn't go to any lectures beyond the first week of class.

Prof gives a study guide before every exam, and the problems on the exam will typically be drawn straight from the study guide.

class is not an easy A but it is obtainable if you do not make mistakes, miss readings, homework, or presentations. You will have to teach yourself a lot .You will have to treat this class as a regular required class so be wary with how many other classes you are taking. He does offer extra credit opportunities and you will learn a lot in the end.

analysis.name: Tasha Philpot

review_highlights.comment: Tests are really difficult. If you show up to class and take all the pop quizzes, and do decently on the tests you can achieve a B. Class average  B, highest grade on last test  90

Do not take her. She is rude and a horrible professor. She shoves her political agenda down your throat. Professor Philpot is everything wrong with college professors in 2018. DO NOT TAKE HER. YOU WILL THANK ME LATER.

DON'T DO IT. There is an excessive amount of reading (2 books and multiple research papers) that MUST be done before each class b/c there are random pop quizzes. Her exams are equally excessive and worded for the purpose of confusing you. Philpot is also extremely rude, sarcastic, & unwilling to help her students in anyway so don't bother asking ?s

This wasn't a government class. It was a room where she could rant about racism in the media. I learned everything about stereotypes in every genre of multimedia. Didn't learn a single thing about government. Her exams were subjective multiple choice and she was rude to students who wanted to state their opinion. We ended up appealing our grades.

Dr. Philpot is a wonderful professor. Her exams are both lecture and reading based, all multiple choice. Her classes are interesting and important to attend if you want to do well. If you aren't willing to do the bare minimum in her class, just don't take it. Any negative reviews are mostly personal, not indicative of her as a professor at all.

analysis.name: Pamela Elias
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 26 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: If you ever have the chance to take Pam as your professor, please do!!!! I just completed my first semester at the UT Austin, and she was without a doubt my favorite professor of the entire semester. Pam is so energetic, and she teaches the material in a way that helps you understand no matter what your math background is. She is the absolute best!

My GOAT. She gives you test reviews for the midterms and the final that match the test exactly and you get a one page cheat sheet (front and back). Attendance isn't required but the daily homeworks match what she does in class so it's best if you go. TAs are very helpful and reachable. Easiest class ever if you listen in lecture and put the work in

I loved Pam, she is sweet,kind,& smart. She truly loves teaching, and you can tell. Attendance is not required (but you should definitely go because it helps a lot!). She builds in no-class days before and after holidays. Her office hours (along with the TA) are helpful. No matter how much math you have going in,she'll make sure you understand.

She always has opportunities outside of class to meet with her if you need extra help. What is on the exams is clearly communicated by word or the Canvas reviews.

Just one of the nicest people ever, super fun and easy math class that is good for education/UTeach. Tests were easy, projects were fun. Awesome professor, and very good teacher too. Material was easy, but she is a great explainer of things. GOAT level professor, can't recommend enough

analysis.name: David Quintanilla
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly

review_highlights.comment: Quintanilla is an amazing prof!!! He has super clear lectures and is such a cool and laid back guy. He really cares about his students and wants you to succeed. I would take him again if I could!

Prof Quintanilla is the best lecturer I've ever had. He makes every complex law topic easy to understand. TAKE HIM IN PERSON!!!! and always go to class, it's not mandatory, but participation is part of your grade and really all you need to do well in this class is take good notes during lectures. One of the few classes I actually loved going to!

Prof Q. is very passionate about teaching, and that passion shows in his lectures. He made the online class engaging and explained complex topics in a practical manner. He rewards your participation - by answering questions and attending lectures, the assignments and exams are very doable. Enjoyed the class a lot; he taught very useful concepts!

TAKE THIS PROF! GO TO CLASS! Prof Q is so amazing. This class changed my life no joke. You MUST go to lecture to do well on tests (which can be somewhat tricky but not horrible). Homeworks & group proj are easy. Review sessions are incredibly beneficial. Prof Q is incredibly engaging, passionate, & caring. I looked forward to class every day.

Business law sounds like it would be boring, but he makes it exciting and shows how useful it is for everyday life. He makes lectures engaging, interesting, and memorable. As a CS major, this class felt like a breath of fresh air. Definitely one of my favorite professors at UT. Just make sure to keep up with the readings and participate in class.

analysis.name: Emily Que
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 27 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She's nice, but the lectures are super hard to follow. she doesn't like to explain her work when "teaching" her lectures. If you didn't take AP/dual chem in high school, you'll be lost. For one of the exams, she made it too long and despite most of us not finishing, she didn't give us a curve despite acknowledging that the test was too long.

Dr. Que is extremely hard to follow in lectures. She doesn't completely work out problems and expects us to follow unfinished messy work. She jumps from topic to topic with confusing explanations, does not simplify any concepts. Tests are too long, which she acknowledges but does not change. Can only understand material by teaching yourself.

Can't even solve her own questions, even relying on students to help her. When she make mistakes (pretty often), she just smiles through it and laughs it off. Embarrassing for her honestly. Lectures are essentially pointless because she just reads off of the slides without ever explaining anything. Might as well be a biology major and take Laude.

Dr. Que is talented in her work and is very nice; however, this does not translate to her skills as a teacher. Her lectures are hard to follow, and at times she will skip certain skills, as it may take too long to teach, or be stuck on information that won't be on the exam. No curve, her exams WILL be long. You will NEED DC Chem or AP Chem to live.

Que is the worst professor I had. First time teaching gen chem and it shows. Exams are long, heavy weight, no curve, rushed. Lectures are reading slides, messy work, and disorganized explanations that confuse instead of help. She makes mistakes and relies on students to correct her. If you lacked strong high school chem, this class is a struggle.

analysis.name: Robert Quigley
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: Quigley is a great lecturer and is very knowledgeable in the field of journalism, as he spent many years working as an editor and a few years as a reporter. His approach to the class is very hands-on, having groups go through the reporting process step by step. Overall, it was a fun class, and if you want to be a reporter, it will be useful!

Quigley is an amazing professor and a gem of UT. Assignments are really straightforward as long as you follow the rubric. He also invited alumni like Pulitzer winners and reporters to give unique Q&As. There is an overarching group project with a low-stakes presentation at the end, but it's easily manageable unless you're stuck with an awful group.

Had Quigley for 301F and it was a great experience! The whole class is basically step-by-step instructions of the journalistic process with a short, low-stakes presentation at the end. He also gets some very interesting and accomplished people to give guest lectures. Overall, Quigley wants the best for his students and creates a solid foundation.

For his first time teaching 301, Professor Quigley did amazing. The homework and group projects were easy to complete and content was well taught and easy to understand, especially if you have a journalism background. Quigley is funny and kind and wants the best for his students. Choose your group wisely, you'll be working with them all semester.

You can tell he really loves his job and especially journalism. There are two big projects but they are fun to do. There were multiple guest speakers which were pretty boring. There are multiple opportunities to get a good grade. Just go to class and do your work and you will do fine.

analysis.name: Qiang Liu
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: Really easy CS Honors class for grades, and while he covers important info, he doesn't seem to care about teaching so the class feels like a drag sometimes. TA Ziyi is the goat though, he's most of the reason the grades are so good cause Prof. Liu just comes in, lectures exactly till the class cutoff time, and then is the first one out of class.
Took ML2 Hon and was a great class. HW and exams were directly related to course content and were similar to practice problems. Lectures were good as well.
For ML2-H, he is extremely knowledgeable and has good lectures and homeworks. It is also almost impossible not to get an A.
Super easy class if you need a tech elective. Class was just basic HTML/CSS. Does take attendance on random days but gives lots of extra credit to make up for it. Great guy.

analysis.name: Quoc Nguyen

Nguyen is honestly the sweetest professor I've ever had. He truly cares about his students and treats us like his own kids. Dr Nguyen is truly a once in a lifetime professor who genuinely cares about his students. Quoc is genuinely a good and caring professor but the class itself is very hard with the final being the hardest exam by far.

analysis.name: Emily Quigley

review_highlights.comment: Quigley is absolutely my all time favorite professor at UT. She is one of the most kind and understanding professors here. Prof Quigley was one of the best professors I ever had. She truly cares so much about her students and helps them with everything to succeed in journalism. She was always avaliable to help. Participation is also a huge part of this class.
Professor Quigley is great. She gives great feedback and really cares about student's success. If you go to her office hours, you will get an easy A. One of my favorite professors at UT.

chose professor Quigley as your reporting words teacher. She's my favorite professor at UT by far and truly wants you to succeed. She's chill and laid back but also pushes you to be the best. She's someone you can go to for more than just class and understands reporting words is difficult so she's awesome
EQ is amazing. My writing improved so much because her feedback is so detailed. She is also a cool person overall. Labs are fun. Take her if you can!!!

analysis.name: Michelann Quimby
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Avoid taking this class if you can. The majority of lectures devolve into her chatting with a few students about her politics. Constantly tries to push her own agenda, and asks loaded questions on canvas. Doesn't seem to have a very strong background in computer science and most issues discussed are generic tech issues. Lenient on late submissions.

Took her for HDF340. While her lectures are politically charged, she encouraged open discussion and was very honest with her own experiences. She constantly stressed the importance of mental health days and rest. Dr. Quimby has been one of the best professors I've ever had at UT. She is GREAT, and she makes this class so interesting. analysis.name: Laura de Castro Quaglia

Took this course online over the summer and was extremely easy. Not much homework and very few quizzes which is all your grade is accumulated with.

analysis.name: Peter English

Class was graded off of 6 projects and 2 exams (tons of EC tho). Exams were difficult (mostly theory that was covered in slides) but graded very leniently. Projects (choice of matlab or python) were time consuming but covered really cool topics. Lectures that didn't involve linear algebra were pretty good, but the ones that did were a struggle.

analysis.name: Qianqian Li
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment:

Can't miss more than 7 classes w/o failing but it's a QR code so...

analysis.name: Sahil Ravgotra

I thoroughly enjoy Prof. Ravgotra's class. The material is really technical and math-heavy, he's very good at breaking it down and connecting it to economic examples, which makes the class much easier to understand. If you put in the effort, you'll learn a lot from this course.

I really liked Prof. Ravgotra's class. He explains things clearly and answers questions in a way that actually makes sense. You can tell he cares about us understanding the material. Homework and quizzes kept me on track. Sometimes a bit fast, but overall a great class.

analysis.name: Richard Taylor

This class was actually so easy. I did the readings and the async lectures before every class, and the ICA's were a breeze. Also does not budge on policies.

analysis.name: Stephen Slota

Very chill professor ocasionally says funny stuff. Very easy class mixes with i302 at times.

This class formed great friendships for me in the HDO major! It was the perfect introduction to HDO, but I can understand that if you don't get a good group, it could be a terrible class. Dr. Wuster focuses on making sure each individual student receives the education they want.

You can make up absences by doing extra assignments, it was an okay class lots of group assignments but still liked it and learned a decent amount. more busy work than i thought though, felt like a high school class. he's not very interesting and kind of hard to hold a conversation with but a good person and wants the best for his students.

analysis.name: Stephen Trejo

Professor Trejo's lectures are amazing, the speed and way in which he explains things make it very easy to understand complex subjects. Also the course is super light work, only 3 quizzes and 3 exams.

Trent is the best!! Take this class!!!
