analysis.name: Delgerjargal Uvsh
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I took Dr. Uvsh's UGS about corruption. From the start, the rubric for the class was clear and grading was very chill. There are readings weekly but you lowkey don't *have* to do them to do well 😅. Overall, Dr. Uvsh is very nice and lectures are informative and relevant. She also responds to emails quickly. The TA, Vahan, was also great.

She was a super sweet professor who was always available for questions. She gave you a lot of creative freedom which I appreciated and allowed you to research what you were interested in. There was only one mid-term and it was super fair. Additionally the TA was super sweet and helpful. Overall she was a great professor.

Assigned a lot of readings, can do perfectly fine without doing them. Took feedback mid-semester and immediately applied it, reduced readings. Midterm exam was easy, have access to all slides and notes. Great class for the UGS credit and easy A.
There were a lot of readings but not super necessary to do. The only exam is open note, open PowerPoint. Most things can be completed pretty quickly, and she is flexible with deadlines.

Dr. Uvsh was very caring. She did a good job at creating an engaging curriculum. It is helpful to do your notes on the slides she posts for lecture. She made the class structured but not too stressful.

analysis.name: Sean Upshaw
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Super kind, positive, and laid back guy! If you're not great with computer stuff the assignments can be a little hard, but he's such a chill grader that you just have to focus on getting them turned in on time. He's also very understanding if you email him about certain circumstances. Very glad I took this class with Upshaw, highly recommend.

guys trust, take this class. Professor Upshaw is super kind and this class is genuinely the most enjoyable class I've ever taken. The work is very simple and just follow the tutorials in the textbook and that's it. The books have videos embedded so actual reading is minimal. Pretty self paced but you do have to manage your time.
Very kind. He grades easy and has interesting material. Would take his class again.

For ADV 378: Shawn facilitated so many great discussions and had awesome guest lectures and I learned so much about Black advertising. Most lectures were straight from book material which was sometimes hard to focus on, but I feel like the greatest part of this course was the in-class conversations. He was so kind and truly cared about the course.

He graded very easily (I'm pretty sure everyone made an A) and the content was very interesting and easy to understand because of how he structured the course. He would go over the textbook readings in class by formatting the important details into a PowerPoint. He also had some guest speakers who were all great to listen to!

analysis.name: Ulrich Mueller
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Mueller is such a nice professor! Exams are based on lecture and are relatively straight forward. Attendance isn't mandatory but all the exam content is from the lectures so it helps to go. He offers lecture outlines and practice exams. He really wants to help your grade, so I def recommend him! Discussions are chill as long as you talk once.

love dr. mueller. he outlined everything on the exams early and was receptive to feedback. he truly cares about students as it showed he wanted us to succeed. his exams are not hard as long as you study. evolution is def a very interesting topics as is my fav class at ut so far. his exams gave cushion and room to do bad on the quizzes later.

Dr. Mueller is a great professor and truly wants to help you learn. We had two exams in the first half of the class. Study the lecture handouts because all the answers you need are there. Attendance is mandatory for discussion, but show up because it will help your grade. I recommend taking Mueller & Mats for INB 370!

His lectures were very straightforward. He provided a real-life example of almost every concept he taught. He provides a lecture outline that is where 90% of the test questions come from. Discussion is mandatory, but it helps with the reading questions on the test. There are only two grades for this half of the semester, and they are two exams.

Amazing professor! Attendance is not required for lecture, but is required for discussion. Exams are very very easy with multiple choice questions and True/False. He gives out lecture outlines and as long as you study those (know them by heart), you should get an A in his portion of evolution.

analysis.name: Luis Urrieta
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This class is strange. Required to go off campus for field studies as well as you have autonomy to create your own field study, which can turn out to be  annoying as it is highly time consuming at times. You have to go to every class, sick or not in order to do well in this class as well as he isn't very available outside of class. Glad its over!!

Qualitative Inquiry into Education for Social Change; Professor Urrietta was a fantastic lecturer and discussion facilitator. You have to attend class and participate, but I found the course content very interesting and easy to engage with. He gives you autonomy in defining your field observation project which can turn out to be a lot of fun!

Took this as a 5 week summer class and it was A LOT. So much reading! 7 papers due. 10 volunteer hours & 2 outdoor walks in 100+ degrees. Miserable. Lecture heavy with mandatory participation. Learned a lot but felt as if there was an agenda being pushed. Glad it's over.

analysis.name: Arban Uka
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Inspirational the right word to describe him. He makes students wanna do something more with their life. Amazing lecturers definitely yes. He always brings up interesting facts + engages students to give their opinion, even if the topic is not that hot (like differential equations). Would take again though I've graduated.

very smart and hardworking. very fair evaluation. always ready to help students. a bit messy and always busy (cause he finds time for everyone). kind and polite to extreme. sometimes hard to follow his genius track of thoughts :( . Still among best profs ive ever had
He details the math step by step, always.

analysis.name: Thomas Wiseman
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 138 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I took his social economics class and he just makes it way harder than it needs to be. He wants you to write and memorize the exact same sentences he tells in class with the EXACT SAME WORDS. If you don't use the same word even if you get the right answer, he will give you 0/1 for the question, not even 0.5/1. The most nitpicky professor I ever had

exams are short yet the majority of your grade. no partial credit. no extra credit. lectures are unhelpful. lots of r coding even though its not really relevant to the exams. have to teach yourself everything. textbook is very confusing

DO THE EXTRA CREDIT. Unclear on what the assignments are going to be graded on. Very nitpicky on midterms and paragraph responses are graded harshly with 0 feedback given unless you email him. Cool dude I guess, lectures are just recaps of the notes that you have to do yourself before class. Not a good elective if you want to learn something useful

Wiseman is terrible. One of the worst professors I have had. He makes his tests impossible and if you miss 2 questions you are already in B range. His B+ range is only 88-90, which is ridiculous. Class is 100% memorization no learning involved. Absolute waste of time, and a gpa tanker of a class. find an easier elective.

2nd class with him,& he shouldn't be a stats professor! He's a chill guy and kinda funny, but tests dont allow for patial credit, and the textbook was so incredibly convoluted, meanwhile he'll spend a whole lecture talking abt german v-1 bombs hitting london in ww2 (it's stats), but still weird.
Class is doable if you take hws super seriously + SI

analysis.name: Jason Urban
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Jason gives great feedback and is a fair grader. You can tell that he takes his work seriously and is truly passionate about what he does. I cannot recommend his class enough!

He is great! He gives really specific and helpful feedback to everyones work, and built a polite atmosphere in the online classroom. The class critique process is always so fun and helpful, and I have produce a lot of works Im proud with for my portfolio. Although the workload I can be a bit overwhelming sometimes, but all projects are fun.

I cannot stress enough how much I loved taking a litho class with Jason, he explained everything clearly and gave thorough demos. He does expect you to have good attendance and to actually work during class but it's worth it in order to understand everything that's taught. Definitely take a print class with him if you can!

He is one of the best professor I ever had! He is Inspirational, reasonable, friendly, caring, approachable, and very helpful. He always give clear guidelines when introducing projects. During discussions, he give you comments that can make you go further and want to go further.
nice funny smart cool guy. would recommend. Advice: don't be slovenly.

analysis.name: Victor Eijkhout
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: coe prof that doesn't know how to work canvas. quizzes given out whenever he feels like it. hw is announced randomly in class with limited instructions, yet is graded extremely harsh. prof does not know how to lecture, just mumbles his inner monologue in class. prof is also slightly childish/hard to approach without a getting a sarcastic response.
be careful with his dark magic. Overall, this is a horrible class that I wanted to drop out since day one, but I had no other options to choose.

Initially the course was easy then the content became much more difficult. Lectures were provided online in case students wanted to review them. The final project was one of the more challenging projects I have ever completed, but it was also very interesting. I really like him as a professor and his textbook is great. Would take again! :)
Hard to understand, very old school, and not a good lecturer

Steep learning curve (for me at least) which meant putting in a lot of work outside of class. Lectures and lecture slides are uploaded, and textbook is provided by him, otherwise the course and its structure were confusing

analysis.name: Vaibhav Bahadur
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Bahadur's lectures were very good. His exams are fair but comprise most of the grade. They are generally very similar to the samples he gives. Fall 2024 he provided extra credit to those that attended the final few lectures. He asks tough conceptual questions on his midterms, be prepared. Homework is generally much harder than any exam.
Awesome, teacher would take this college class again.

Boring lectures to help prepare with the lab. Occasional quizzes and a short exam. Doesn't really help prep for lab. Overall, not super necessary or detrimental to doing well in the lab portion of the course.

His class was very disorganized. He would quiz over material learned in class that day, giving us no time to study or ask questions, and the midterm was not a good representation of the class material. He also canceled office hours every week. Lectures were boring and low effort. Heat Transfer lab is also a lot of work in general so fair warning.
He is very good i would take him 1000 times.

analysis.name: Volker  Bromm
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Genuinely easiest A of my life, attendance is taken via instapolls & midterm reviews are pretty similar to homeworks and reviews. Exams weigh only 20% of the grade, it's mostly 4 homeworks (easy). The professor understands most of the students have little to no knowledge about astronomy so he caters to that, nothing too difficult to understand.

Weekly quizzes were pretty easy. The lectures are really fast and I didn't actually learn much, but I could gather enough to do the projects and quizzes. The HWs were a bit confusing but his OH were helpful. Super easy grading on the group projects, you present to him in his office and submit a super short paper. Wish I learned more. Good blowoff.

Super knowledgeable, passionate, kind, and willing to help if you need it or just want to discuss astronomy in general. Works hard to make sure the class isn't stressful grade wise and gives intriguing lectures.
Very easy class, would take again. Accent is a little strong but he cares about the subject. 2 very easy exams, most of the grade is based off of 4 easy homeworks.

Very knowledgeable professor. His lectures are very interesting and you can tell he's passionate about what he's teaching. Weekly easy quizzes and 3-4 problem sets for the entire semester that are not hard at all. No midterms or final , replaced by two fairly simple group projects.

analysis.name: Sara Villanueva
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: DO NOT TAKE HER SHE IS A JOKE!!! She mostly reads directly off the slides and is very rude to students. She barely engages with the class and doesn't explain the material well. She claims she cares about students, but it doesn't show. The tests feel random and don't relate to lectures. Overall, the class is disorganized and frustrating.

I'm not sure what happened to her. Had her for another class and she was okay but this class she was just awful. Her lectures were not only incredibly dense but also super boring and she tested on random and minor details. Also not at all accommodating. If you miss a test good luck trying to get a retake. I had to basically harass student services.

just no. she doesn't seem to care about her students success and so rude in person. in terms of the class itself, very interesting but all she does is read through the slides and doesn't add anything to it. if you ask her a question, she either doesn't know the answer to it or expects you to answer it on your own. Also, she tends to ghost emails!

Professor was okay. Since the online class was just watching prerecorded lectures, there is not much I can say about her personally. You can work ahead in this class which is a good thing, but the order of the canvas material was out of order so when I worked ahead, the info required for the quiz was not under that week which messed me up.

I expected the worst. In reality, I found myself in the easiest class on my schedule. There are weekly quizzes due at 11:59 pm on Fridays, a four-part deep dive assignment, and three case studies. Everything was manageable. I did some parts early too, so there were weeks when I didn't even have to look at the course. The textbook was not needed.

analysis.name: Etienne Vouga
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I also had him for CS395T Physical Simulation. He is hands down the best CS professor I've had. His lectures are engaging and clear. His classes are also some of the hardest I've ever taken, with lots of tough but rewarding projects. But if you put in the effort, he is a pretty lenient grader. He does open-ended final projects in his classes.

I really wanted to like this class due to my interest in competitive programming and preparing for coding interviews. The exam structure is extremely harsh with no partial credit (even though the syllabus says so) making it significantly easy to get a 0. The class is also mostly Turing students making it easy to get imposter syndrome.
Find the bug, and do at least two leetcode problems a week. Did not quite like the amount of work for a 1 hour class.

All around amazing class. Lectures are clear, interesting and informative. Vouga is always available on Discord to answer questions. He's also just a really nice person and very easy to talk to. The content is hard but there's tons of support available. Projects are hard but fun and super rewarding. Lecture quizzes can be tricky but there's no exam

Dr. Vouga is a great guy he really enhances the UT CS Deparment by contributing his time and free energy towards the serious algorithms and data structures education of undergraduates. In guiding students through this curriculum everyone learns and benefits for graduate and career outcomes and some find a life long passion!

analysis.name: Vincent Viviani
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 56 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: One of the best professors I've ever had in this school. Funny, friendly, energetic, kind, and helpful. Very straightforward rubric after standardization. All learning objectives are given and explained before exams, even if you didn't learn anything well, the supporting materials are great to help you out. Also gave bonus at the end of semester.

Very funny guy, and the accent isn't bad. Exams are extremely easy; there is no final. The one quiz per unit is also very easy. Easily the best gen chem 1 professor right now, since most other professors have quizzes every class. I showed up only for tests, since the material on Canvas is enough to learn. However, Prof. Viviani is a great lecturer.

Great professor! I must admit I fell asleep during most lectures (but still ended with an A!) Either way he is really funny and does cool experiments - plus generous with extra credit (+3% to your overall ending grade!). Gen chem 1 is light and taking it with Vivani is chill

Lectures are great and there are tons of review resources for the tests, including practice tests that are almost the exact same as the actual test. He's also super funny and does a bunch of experiments in the class. Definitely recommend him for gen chem 1!!!!
Very kind and his lectures were fun. The class is easy as long as you keep up with the material throughout each unit and he also offers extra credit. Definitely recommend!

analysis.name: Viranga Perera
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 102 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Worst class I've ever taken. He overcomplicates topics which makes them seem harder than they actually are. Doesn't give partial credit back despite some past reviews saying he does. Use the homework to study, but expect to teach most of this class to yourself. I also never took physics before this which I think put me at a disadvantage

His summer course is fast paced, but his lectures are great and he makes sure that students understand the content before moving on. There's a decent amount of hw, but it helps to solidify understanding and to prepare for the exams. Course organization is solid and the teaching team is active on Ed. This is likely the easiest UT physics gets.

It's a lab and the lab is one of the worst designed pieces of education conceived. Its all stats and uncertainty. the whole point of physics is that its not engineering, its ideal, but this class is 5% doing physics concepts and 95% propagating uncertainty. Doesn't make a lick of sense. Perera is great though

Perera is an amazing lecturer, and his class is clearly structured and easy. The midterms are multiple choice and similar in difficulty to homework. If there are bad questions, Perera will drop them to ensure the exams result in grades that reflect the knowledge of the material.

The class is a basic introduction to engineering physics. The topics taught are the same as high school physics with a few changes. Dr. Perera wants his students to succeed and has designed his course so that most students will get A's. Homework will take a bit of time, but it isn't too hard; exams are just like the homework. Best UT Physics Prof!

analysis.name: Vincent Vanderheijden
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 28 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I loved this professor! He is incredibly patient, helpful, and kind to those confused, and he makes sure to challenge students (some cold-calling, but pretty typical for language course). There's a good amount of daily homework, but again, typical of language course. He's also extremely easy to talk to and creates a fun atmosphere in his class.

The professor is extremely passive-aggressive in class and gets annoyed when someone asks questions about the material or grammar that derails from his lesson plan. He aims to give homework that should take 2 hours maximum but takes almost 3-4 hours each day, as if we don't have other homework for other courses. I would never take this class again.

Like Vanderheijden as a person but this class was ROUGH. The scavenger hunt for homework, most of my class felt lost the entire semester. He seemed to blame us for not understanding the concepts instead of spending time making sure we understood the concepts. It felt like by the last week of the semester our class size had dropped by 1/3.

This class was the worst. Hours of homework, difficult quizzes and assignments.  And to top it off, he's a bad teacher!  You learn nothing in this class, and then he gets mad at you for not knowing what's going on. Even if you try to ask him for help/go to office hours, he says he's busy. Once he told me it's not his job to teach me. Like sir?

I hate learning new languages, so I needed something easy to do in 2 semesters... don't do what I did if I could have, I would have dropped the class. That being said, if you have to take him, (don't), stay on top of the themas, DO NOT fall behind!! Prof will notice, and your grades will hurt for it. If you put the work in you'll get the grade

analysis.name: Shawn Williams
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 29 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Incredibly easy class, especially if you have already taken Calc AB or BC. Neither the lectures nor the discussion sections are mandatory to attend. The worksheets and homework are MUCH harder than the exams, and the exams are similar to the reviews. Some extra credit is available for the group mini projects. Final is optional, overall great class!

His lectures are boring but he's good at explaining the topic at hand. There is A LOT of homework- do not attempt to do the homework the day of, i recommend at least 3 days to complete the HW. 2 mini projects that are not too difficult, but choose partners carefully.
 Overall, he's a good teacher and cares for his student's comprehension of calc

This guy is awesome! Didn't take calc in high school, and Dr. Willaims explains concepts in a way that's so easy to understand. Exams are copies of the reviews. Worksheets and Mini Projects are tedious but extremely doable. Homework and exams are graded leniently. TAKE THIS WITH HIM!!!

Makes calculus 3 very digestible. Exams are very straightforward and solely apply the concepts you learn in basic equations. AFAIK does not record lectures but does upload his work online, so attendance is recommended heavily. Weekly homework can be difficult and not follow his methods of solving (it's also harder than the corresponding exam).

Great professor and really cares for students. His homework is really close to exams, and his reviews before exams are very very helpful. Lectures do get posted and he is very easy to access outside of class, for office hours, etc. He is very accommodating of student circumstances and really wants students to develop a love for math.

analysis.name: Wei Xuexin
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This class changed my life. Yes, it's very math heavy BUT he is so fair in grading, homework and exams. The exams were open note and I thought were a fair representation of the course material. OH and rvw sessions were beneficial too. You can tell he cares for his students, he's also knowledgable in the field. deff take it, not a hard class at all.

Took class after seeing previous reviews, but unfortunately prof has significantly changed class structure. Lectures difficult to navigate. Exams are no longer take-home writeups, now difficult. Quite lenient on grading is only good thing but still low exam scores due to hard concepts. Very hard class now, take another neuro class to fulfill degree

He makes simple concepts somehow impossible to understand. Lectures are difficult to follow. Despite being a neuro class, this course covers strictly math concepts. Exams are difficult since he thinks he explains concepts much better than he actually does while the entire class stays confused.

Professor is not good at explaining concepts. Even though this is technically a neuro class, it's a ton of math which he expects you to already know the fundamentals of. He password protects lectures and files, making it a pain to access them and download to write notes alongside lecture.

I had no computational/math background so there was much new (but useful) material about understanding computational modeling of neural systems but he explained very comprehensively! Dr.Wei and the TA sessions were clear on exam content and helpful for preparing. He took student feedback and made availability for students outside of OH if needed.

analysis.name: Haiqing Xu
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Sad to see the lack of engagement from the class- his humor is underrated! This class was very content packed which made it hard to process and remember everything for the tests. Good news is that they were not cumulative! Lab component isn't something to stress out about. I did every assignment the night it was due and got a 97+ on all of them.

Course is graded 65% lecture, 35% lab. Lectures are long but he tells you what specific concepts will be on midterms and quizzes (makes for easy studying). His accent really isn't that bad, just pay attention. Lab section consists of a couple papers, nothing crazy difficult just time-consuming. Be sure to get assignments in on time.

If I could rate him zero I would.
The topics themselves aren't difficult - but he makes everything overcomplicated. I self-taught using the textbook
His accent is rlly difficult to understand and he does a lot of (unnecessary) work that's not on the slides
Doesn't really care about students and scheduled the final way before the examination period

Surprised by this rating. I thought he was fantastic. Lectures are fine. His accent is over blown imo however could just be me. Super nice guy very accommodating. I thought this class was fairly easy math was lite and essays were fine. Would be surprised if he's isn't the easiest metric teacher. 10/10

Professor Xu has a very heavy accent that is difficult to understand, and the course is very very lecture heavy. As a result, I don't feel like I learned anything. I paid a lot of money to hire a private tutor, and I feel like that was the only reason I didn't flunk the class. Would not recommend.

analysis.name: Xuan Ho
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: A lot of assigned material (readings + film) outside of class, but they were all interesting, albeit the readings can get dense. Class is discussion heavy, so make sure you come prepared. Low-stakes weekly response essays to assigned material, group presentation, and final essay (focus on this). Overall super fun and informative class.

I took her film class to receive a flag I needed, she was very pretentious and condescending. The course isn't well structured and consists of watching several films repeatedly and discecting scenes in class. 70% of the course was taken up by group presentations. High work load and there is 1 paper worth 30% of your grade, the reading is nonsense

Yes it's a little intense for a lower-division class but I had fun and never thought that the assignments were too hard. Easy 2-page film reviews that once you get the formula down you can just repeat every week and she gave me 10/10 on almost every one. Just like watching films before you sign up for a film class (I saw that problem in my class).

The class consists of almost weekly 2 paged double-spaced papers that analyze assigned movies, but that's it. You WILL be paired up with a partner where you need to lead the discussion, but only once. Readings are practically unintelligible- and she knows this. The only bad thing was the strict attendance policy. 3 absences then letter grade drop.

analysis.name: Fangzhou Xia
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: His lectures are very boring, and you won't learn anything. Quizzes became more about memorization of homework problems than actual learning. If you can self-study well or have some preexisting knowledge, you will be fine. Otherwise, try to take it with someone else. However, he does give lots of partial credit on the midterms and final.

Bad lecturer. If you can stomach self-studying entirely, you will be fine. Quizzes are directly from textbook problems, and tests are similar to, but harder. The problem is, you don't learn much, if any, dynamics fundamentals/intuition, you just end up memorizing textbook problems. If you want to actually learn dynamics, look elsewhere.

Terrible lecturer, excellent one-on-one. Go to office hours, read the textbook, and put in the effort of learning on your own, and you'll be ok. Despite the terrible lectures, he is a very kind person who is willing to explain the material and help you. Genuinely cares about the success of his students.

Lectures are pretty pointless. He teaches straight out the textbook. First two exams werent bad and he does a decent enough job of telling you general problems on tests. But, the final was awful. Had an entire problem that was never taught in class and genuinely no one knew how to do.

Weekly homework with a quiz during discussion. The quiz was a homework problem with different numbers. There were 2 tests and a final. These questions were picked from the textbook, so it was pretty easy to practice for them. All things are graded with generous partial credit. He adapted his teaching to help the class. Very nice guy as well.

analysis.name: Xiaofen Hamilton
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She changed the project guidelines every week and treated students poorly. She also said things like "we should fail children with disabilities who don't meet standards" and "ladies weigh yourself every day and never gain weight." She was confusing, outdated, and none of the students respected her after 3 weeks. Choose the other professors!!

I hated this class. The only day Dr. Hamilton taught an informative class was the day she was observed by higher-ups. Your grade comes from teaching a PE lesson as well as weekly discussion posts and a midterm+final. Strict 0 absence policy or you fail. Don't waste your time in this class, you won't learn anything.

Absolutely awful. Just the worst in every way. Made statements such as:
1. "Students are either normal or disabled."
2. "If a student can't meet the PE Standards for any reason, they should be failed."
3. "Weigh yourself every day and don't eat if you don't need to."
Harassed multiple students after classes for their disabilities and identities.

If you have the possibility to take a different professor for EDC 314, do it! Professor Hamilton not only was slow and repetitive during lectures, but constantly contradicted herself and treated the students like children instead of adults learning to become teachers. The TAs were the only saving grace for this class.

Fitness For Life is such an easy class. You don't need to buy the textbook its basically useless. There is no exams. You just need to write for majority of the class and you have revisions to get a 100. Her lectures are pretty boring and will make you stand up and do stuff in class but just do homework or something else to keep yourself busy.

analysis.name: Mindy Xiaolan
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: One of the worst classes I've taken. Xiaolan's nice, but she gives you the same randomly assigned group for all of the cases throughout the semester, and you don't get to switch groups at all, regardless of how many people complain about issues they've had with their groups. Other profs let you pick groups/switch. Would not take again.

The contents for this class are difficult as is, and although the professor is very nice, keeping up with her lectures was hard.
