Highly recommend taking this class and getting to know Akash!

By far my favorite class I've taken. Half the grade is participation and the tests are heavily curved. If you show up and participate you are almost guaranteed an A. He's extremely smart and has great real world experiences, and he really cares about his students. No better class to learn about what is going on in markets AND how to talk about them

Great class to learn about markets and keep up to date. There are 2 exams that are pretty difficult but the class gets curved to a 3.6 anyways so it doesn't matter as long as you get within the average (~65). His class emphasizes participation so show up and try to contribute as much as possible its worth 30% of your grade. Overall, great professor

Great professor and lectures, sensible content to address markets from different perspective (and each week has a market lecture too). Exams aren't too hard, it's like 2/3 general understanding from lectures and readings and then 1/3 hard/nitpicky questions "to make a curve." If you listen in class, a day's studying probably enough.

Akash is an excellent professor who is incredibly knowledgeable about the subject matter. If you really want to learn about markets, you'll absolutely love this course. The tests are tough, but the class is heavily curved. He's one of my favorite professors I've had at McCombs. Just show up, participate, and you'll do well.

analysis.name: Amanda Koltz
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Koltz and Wolf, along with the teaching team were nice and knowledgeable. The class itself wasn't bad, it's mainly memorization-based and exams are heavily graded. However, the class was harder than what I had expected it to be. There are a few projects that the TAs grade strictly on, and exams are a mix of MC and FRQ. Content is interesting!

Dr. Koltz and Dr. Wolf were great lecturers! The content was mostly memorization and the exams were not too difficult. The exams did take a long time to be graded and there are outside projects that are easy but you do have to still do them. Very interesting class and content overall and both professors were kind and understanding.

The content of this class is not TOO difficult, but the course structure is set up a lot harder than it needs to be. Grades are almost completely based on exams, and each exam is graded atleast a month after it's taken. Grades aren't posted until LAST minute. They mentioned a curve, didn't apply it. So stressful not knowing how you're doing.

Dr. Koltz was a great lecturer, and she and Dr. Wolf made sure to cover everything needed for each exam! It's mostly memorization, but as long as you stay on top of the content it's manageable. The discussion projects are also a good grade boost, just make sure to actually try on them.

I personally did not enjoy this class, I felt that the lectures weren't that intriguing. The grades are hidden throughout the semester so you can't see how you stand in the class, and assignments can take 2-3 weeks to return to you. At least there's no final. If you really like ecology then this class might be for you, but it wasn't for me.

analysis.name: Amrita Kaur
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 110 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: read all of this. I'll start by saying she is an amazing teacher, just not a good professor. She's really fun in class, but she loves handing out zeros on her homework assignments, which is hard to come back from. I enjoyed the class before we were given back our homework grades (1 month after submitting!), but she was not helpful after that.

I personally enjoyed the HWs even though they were challenging because they were quite enjoyable to code up. However, I feel like most of my effort went into doing good style and docstrings. Sometimes we don't know about certain style requirements until after it was graded, especially at the end unless you asked the TAs. Final was hard, but curved

Professor Kaur has really good lectures. The programming assignments are long and you can lose a lot of points because of poor style (especially at the semester start), but since there's so much lecture/feedback form extra credit it's easy to get full credit. Tests are really hard and worth a ton but there are practice tests posted, so study a lot!

Professor Kaur is a great teacher, and her lectures are engaging and informative. The tests are difficult, but are often heavily curved. The TAs are helpful, but their grading can be inconsistent. If you attend lectures, study, and don't use AI to generate your code, you will do well. Beware of using outside material, because it's an automatic zero

Pretty good professor. Lectures and weekly assignments are engaging and interesting. Weekly assignments are graded harshly but there's a ton of extra credit so its not hard to offset the tough grading. If you do the practice tests she gives you its not hard to get 90+ on exams. If you did UIL CS this course will be extremely easy for you.

analysis.name: Amy Liu
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 35 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Great UGS to take! The topic of the course was interesting and engaging. Dr. Liu is very kind and a good lecturer. The weekly quizzes are exactly what is covered in lecture, so if you take notes they will be very easy. There are multiple in-class essays, but they are pretty straightforward to prepare for and write. Gave extra points at the end.

Easiest UGS ever, the only negative thing was at 8am. Attendance is not mandatory, but quizzes are based on lectures which are not accessible outside of class so...you miss out a lot if you don't attend. My TA Meiying Xu was the sweetest person ever and I got 100s on all essays that I personally thought were very mid when I wrote them.

Dr. Amy Liu was a very good lecturer that kept her students entertained and intrigued throughout classes. The weekly discussion sections were also a great time to go over lecture materials and the quizzes often got content directly from the lectures so if you paid attention you were fine. She was very generous with her grading and often gave 100s.

Dr. Liu is an amazing professor! I took this class for the credit, but the content she covers is honestly really interesting. Write down what she says WORD FOR WORD during the lectures, because the quizzes are fully based on what she says. My TA graded a bit hard on the first essay, but after that you'll figure out her expectations for the essays.

Great UGS! Lectures and class content were extremely interesting, and weekly quizzes were almost rote what was taught in class.  Dr. Liu is also wonderful. She brought us breakfast burritos and pineapple bread to sweeten the 8 AM once! You will need to write 4 essays in class, but follow the rubric and you will be fine. No quiz makeups, but drops.

analysis.name: Amy Thompson
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Easy class with clear grading expectations. Make sure to put effort into the weekly discussion posts, show up to section meetings, and go to most lectures because attendance is taken randomly. I wasn't super interested in this class but Professor Thompson did a good job teaching and I would definitely recommend her if you need to take this class.

One of the best classes I've taken. Only thing you have to worry about is your participation grade in the discussion sections since they weigh heavy. Most of the class work is made up weekly DBs over the topic of the week. Exams (2 total) are easy if you follow the review provided.  Keep track of deadlines, attend class and you should be fine.

Sweetest prof and truly cares about what she teaches + she's pretty quick to respond outside of class. There are short participation assignments at the end of lecture once in a while and the exams are really easy if you prepare (class Avg. ~90). Around 10 EC opportunities, each worth 0.5 pts for a max of 2.5 pts on your overall grade.

The professor is a great lecturer, and the class is pretty easy. Not a lot of homework, just reading and discussions. The worst part is that she takes attendance on random dates, so you really want to go to every lecture, and the discussion sections feel a bit useless to me. Overall, though, really good professor and class, 8.5/10
Very sweet, engaging lectures, comprehensive, kind. Reasonable with grading and assignments. This was a very good intro GRG class.

analysis.name: Amanda Hager
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 127 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Hager is the best professor I had during my freshman year. There is a extra credit opportunity that is worth 1 % added to your final course grade by using Piazza frequently. On the last day of class, she gave us 2 points on our final exam just by showing up. She is an amazing lecture and really nice. There is HW due every week. I love her!!!!!!

Amanda is by far the best professor in the math department. She is so nice and cares so much for her students. Her exams are not hard at all if you attend class and do your homework. Exams are quest based with a few free response questions. I took her for M305G AND M408N and it was a great experience. She's amazing.

Dr. Hager is the most involved professor I had during my time at UT. She is absolutely rooting for students to get an A in her class and makes it very possible to do so. Attendance is required once every week or so for the in person assignments, but I'd say to go as often as you can because she'll give hw answers in lecture!

She is my unicorn. Her lectures were always well prepared and easy to follow. I always felt comfortable asking my questions in class, and she was also accessible outside of class. I genuinely believe she cared about me, and she graded a lot of work with individualized comments, which I appreciated.

hager gives a lot of resources throughout the year (hw, textbook questions, in class practice, test reviews) for you to succeed. would recommend going to class as much as possible for proper understanding of the material. pretty content heavy after midterm 2, but doable if you keep up with hw and do the final exan review. overall, def recommend!!

analysis.name: Amy Howard
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She's very caring! There are three exams (40%) that are fill-in-the-blank. The rest of the class is composed of daily discussion boards at the end of lectures, a few in-class assignments, and a few outside-of-class papers. They are great buffers to the hard exams. If you put in the work, you will succeed (don't rely on the study guide, though).

She has been one of the kindest professors I've had. While the material can be challenging, if you pay attention and study, you will be fine. You can tell that she cares a lot about each student and wants to see everyone succeed, so utilize office hours if you need! She is also funny and very relatable, which makes class enjoyable.

She is super sweet and kind, as well as funny and relatable!! Class consists of 3 exams, the final one being cumulative; it's a lot of information given to you in lectures, so study well because the exams are the majority of the grade. There will be extra credit, I suggest doing all of them.

analysis.name: Amy Meeks
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Meeks is a very good intro teacher; the class is very lecture-heavy, and you have to pay attention to succeed on the tests. She offers a lot of extra credit, but there is a lot of McGraw-Hill.

Dr. Meek is the sweetest lady ever! She treats her students like they're her children in a way. Anyways...she is very EASY! Tests are basically just like her powerpoints so reading the book is not really necessary but it does help. It was an easy A for me. I would reccomend her!
Had plenty of time to take notes by hand. She's adorable, and grades fairly. Show up, take notes, and you'll be sure to get an A+. Ended up with a 100 in the class.  Loved her.

I love all things psychology and I couldn't handle this class, it was so boring. You just went to class and filled in powerpoint slides she would give you, you also have to use a laptop because she goes way to quickly to take by hand. Her lectures go along with the book so if you don't go to class you can use that. She gives a lot of extra credit.

She was a  nice lady. The book is not necessary as the exams are mainly based off her PowerPoints. They're very straight-forward, so as long as you pay attention and read your notes a couple of times, you should EASILY get an A. Only issue about her is that her lectures usually ended late. She gives extra credit for papers and perfect attendance.

analysis.name: Amy Bryan
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Bryan is fantastic. She really cares about her students, wants to see them succeed, and will provide them with resources if they put in the effort. She's difficult to reach online due to her busy schedule, so find her in person if you ever need anything. She's one of the best faculty members I've had the chance to interact with on this campus.

Dr. Bryan manages to cram so much information into a semester that it's a wonder she maintains such clarity & distinction in her lectures. Attendance is taken randomly, but usually occurred once a week or so. Would definitely recommend attending all classes. Very kind, very willing to work with you if something is going on, & loves her students!

Child Development: Prof Bryan was very knowledgable and helpful, in my opinion. Class was extremely easy and interesting. 4 exams, no final unless you missed an exam with valid excuse. Takes attendance on random days for extra points on final grade. There's also a separate lab that I really enjoyed! Consists of just 2 observation assignments

Class is very easy and fair. Assignments are not too complicated. Not hard to get an A as long as you pay attention to her lectures. The tests were mostly from lecture, not book. She made the material very interesting and overall a great class. I'm taking her again next semester!

analysis.name: Alfred Tuley
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 44 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: His class is super chill & he's really funny. I would mention that he does tend to skim through topics and talk about it kinda vaguely. Most of your learning needed to pass the class and test is based off of the resources in canvas, not his lectures. quiz every week, tests are a little hard but with use of resources its easy. tons of extra credit.

Best professor at UT so far. He makes chemistry accessible to all. Highly recommend his office hours to get advice for quizzes and exams. He offers so many resources from himself and the chem dept. He is funny, caring, and devoted to his students. Studying lectures, quizzes, learning modules, and practice problems/exams are all necessary.

The class is not that difficult, and it can be interesting if you pay attention and put effort into the class. There are many resources provided to help learn and review for exams, which are very easy if you do them. Dr. Tuley explains concepts well in lecture and is very friendly. This class is very easy to do well in if you put in the effort.

tuley is objectively a good professor, his lecture style was just hard to follow personally. however he definitely cares and wants us all to succeed! just beware when you get to acids and bases, tuley isn't that great at explaining the more advanced topics and breaking it down easily. but overall he's a good professor #ilyalfredtuley

Dr. Tuley is a really caring and genuine guy. This class was difficult but you have the opportunity to earn up to 30 points of extra credit and retake two of the exams as your optional final. I went to office hours once a week and felt much more confident on the material afterward. He'll basically do the hw with you which sets you up for quizzes.

analysis.name: Eman  Alasadi
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 60 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Truly an outstanding professor. She goes above and beyond to support her students and provides an exceptional amount of resources to help you succeed. She is deeply invested in making sure students actually understand the material and is always willing to spend extra time explaining concepts. PChem could use slightly more rigor, but she's great

Professor Eman was the best chemistry professor ever!! She is super sweet and wants everyone to succeed. She offered 2 makeup exams at the end of the semester that will replace your lowest two exams. She is hilarious and lectures were always engaging. You do have to study and put in some time/work, but all the material is accessible and organized.

The best professor I've ever had. She gives out: extra credit, participation quizzes, practice questions, multiple practice exams for each unit, cheat sheets, FAQ's, annotated lectures, her YT channel and transcripts, a STUDY SCHEDULE, and keys to go with everything I just mentioned. Hilarious, laid back but caring. Exam grading is clear. TAKE HER.

I LOVE Professor Eman, she is so knowledgeable, respected, inspirational, and just overall an amazing professor. I learned so much from her class and was actually able to retain what I learned. She offers lots of extra credit which is also a plus. I recommend that everyone whether you are a science major or not take a class with her!

Professor Eman is THE GOAT. I don't enjoy chemistry at all, but his class actually made it bearable for me. The class is extremely well structured, has tons of resources, extra credit, but most importantly, the professor truly cares about each and every one of her students. If you have the chance to take a class with her, you should 100% do it.

analysis.name: Benjamin Allison
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: DO NOT TAKE HIM! I have NEVER struggled in a class like this before as a straight A student. He gives 50 min exams where we have to write an essay, 3 additional paragraphs and analyze 3 documents by hand. I studied so hard only to fail due to lack of time. VERY strict about small details and makes the class incredibly hard to do well in.

Would not recommend this class to anyone who cares about their GPA. No form of exam prep, heavy reading material, no consideration for working students, not enough time on exams and condescending about grading. Majority of the class did poorly on the exam so we'll see how the next one goes. Avoid at all costs!
I thought I was the only one the reviews are spot on. Nightmare class.
No exam review and very vague on what will be on the exam.

analysis.name: Alberto Ghibellini
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Ghibellini is incredibly kind and creates an extremely warm and welcoming class, though his first year at UT showed—lectures were surface‑level, monotone, and often behind schedule. The readings themselves were valuable, the grading is easy, and he's very laid‑back. Again, great person, but unfortunately class time did not aid in understanding.

Dr. Ghibellini was great! Very kind and caring! I definitely recommend taking his class. There is a lot of reading for the class, but he spends the whole class time explaining the readings. The only grades in the class are attendance, one midterm, and one final so study for these exams (they aren't overly difficult though).

Very laid back and knowledgeable, good at discussing philosophical basis for governmental texts and structures. All of the grade was attendance, one midterm and an oral final so be sure to not fall behind on content, but there was no busywork.

analysis.name: Andres Almazan
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The GOAT. We heard from leaders with remarkable careers (former CEO of Southwest, CFO of Walmart, ByteDance exec, etc.). His dry humor and thoughtful questions make sessions engaging. He even hosted karaoke at his house :). He genuinely cares about his students and pushes them to uphold professionalism, think critically, and communicate clearly.

Overall, class was really easy and virtually a free A (although some people take an A-). I think what is frustrating is the class is very ambiguously graded, but as long as you show up and speak 1-2 times in class, you will be fine. Midterm and Final were fairly easy - just GPT the books.Almazan can be rude at times to students, but he means well.

Lectures are super interesting bc they have guest speakers. The test are based on books that are long af. They def require you to do research on them (don't really have to read) but reading is the safer choice. Overall, 1 essay and 1 final exam and really just based on if you know what was in the books or not. Attendance required but prof is cool.

This is a great class to hear from seasoned professionals across various industries. The class itself is graded on participation and tests are over 3 books you are assigned to read. The books are interesting and the tests aren't too bad either, just make sure to stay on top of the readings!

Lyceum was a semester-long set of seminars with guest speakers from various business professions. Exams were over 3 books that we were assigned, but otherwise the class wasn't much of a time commitment.

analysis.name: Ann Thijs
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 133 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Lecture and homework seemed so easy but the passing rate for each test was always super low! Tests were not an accurate representation of what was taught in lecture which makes it completely hard to perform well. I learn a great deal but did not get a complementary grade for all of the work I put in.

The wording on her tests is extremely difficult to understand. Everyone had to ask what the questions meant during the tests. I wish I wouldn't have taken her class. Also in class participation is 75% accuracy, so getting a one hundred is gonna be some work.

Dr. Thijs is a nice person but shes not a good lecturer. She fumbles her words, says um a lot, her sentences are incomplete because she pauses between words, and she goes through the powerpoints too fast. She was disappointed with our exam average and blamed it on us for not trying harder instead of asking what she was doing wrong.
Avoid her at all cost. Does not know how to teach and her test are nonsense. Good luck :)

To start it is a flipped classroom with a pre-recorded lecture that you watch on your own time Monday, then regular in person lecture Wednesday and Friday. I loved Dr. Thijs! Previously I took this course w/ a different professor and q-dropped bc of his demeanor, but Dr. Thijs is the sweetest. She looks out for her students and makes sure they pass

analysis.name: Anita Latham
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 182 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Latham is the nicest professor ever. She always asked all of us how our day was, "Too much for a Monday (her catchphrase)"? She lectures over the main ideas, not so much the details. But that's Biology. We have to read! If you don't like to read, I'd suggest you take another Bio prof. Overall, you'll enjoy being her class. She's great.

Don't make the same mistake I did. I devoted all my energy to past material and it cost me. The final is mostly cellular respiration, photosynthesis, energy/enzymes, and biotechnology. Focus mostly on these topics! The final is alright. The thing that makes it different from past exams is that it's mostly application. In conclusion, study 3 weeks!

Dr. Latham is so funny and nice. I love the fact that she's the only professor that asks us often how our day was. Don't go to her office hours. She say's that the CA's are better than her. Go to CSS! They don't gave you the answers but make you think. This prepares you greatly for the test. All in all, her test can be challenging. So, study alot!!

DONT take this 1st semester if you can avoid it!!! Keep track of due dates b/c they aren't consistently on one day and for example Latham will say it's due in 5 days when its due in 2 days. Just check canvas, youll be good. For exams learn the ws objectives like the back of your hand, know discussion ws and you can get an A. She gives candy!!!!!!

I love Dr. Latham and her whole team of TA, CA! Came with little biology background but succeeded in this course thanks to how amazing she is. She's so caring, funny, and an amazing lecturer. I have hard time focus during class and it was fast paced too, but there is recorded video lectures that is super helpful! SHES THE MOST CARING PROFESSOR EVER

analysis.name: Ann Johns
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 163 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Dr. John's is good at conveying important information through her lectures, and as long as you show up and do the readings it's easy to get a good grade. That being said, on an interpersonal level, Dr. John's is extremely rude and condescending, shaming students in public for silly reasons. Also, this class is almost purely memorizing, not learning

Super unwilling to talk to students and insanely rude/condescending, few extra credit opportunities, your grade mostly depends on three tests, and the grading is very subjective to the TA. For a VAPA, save your time, I studied more for these tests than my other major tests.

Dr. Johns enjoys feeding off the souls of miserable people. Never had a pleasant conversation with her. Don't ask questions, she will yell at you. Not chill. There are 3 tests, at 20% each. You have to give information on 10 pieces (date, artist, where, context, medium, etc, out of a pool of 50) and then write a full essay in 50 min.

Prof Johns is SO passive-aggressive to her students and belittles them in announcements and class when asked questions. She knows her content but has no joy in interacting with students. Tests consist of 10 ID questions (out of 50+ artworks) and a 25-minute, 3-page essay in case you want to get a good score. DO NOT TAKE

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!!! Lots of memorization, harsh grading, you must be very specific on tests, or else you will get 0 points. Have to know upwards of 300+ things per test, including readings every week. do not be fooled by the grade distribution!!!!!!!!!!!

analysis.name: Lee Ann Kahlor
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 130 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: My favourite professor this semester. Shes very sweet and understanding with her students. I feel bad, however, because a lot of students take her for granted. She gives great lectures and although they may not be mandatory, I regret not going when I should have. Its not an easy A unless you make an effort knowing the topics covered in this class

Look I love Dr. Kahlor. She's one of my favorite profs I've had here because she's so funny, likeable and reallllyy loves to hear from her students. However, the minimum for an A is a 94 which is crazy to me. I've made low A's on all the exams and am at a 93.6 right now even though I'm doing good in the class? Now I have to try to take the final

Fun, but beware of the reading. They are long and WILL be referenced on exams. Everything is open book, but you cannot just skim and get away with it. Take extensive notes on the lectures, too - they reference the embedded videos on the exams. Grading can take a minute to get back, and those chapter quizzes are on a 10-minute timer (so be fast!)

Kahlor was amazing! I'm an engineering student who needed the soc/behav science credit, and I have no regrets. 

What I did that helped a lot (and not saying you should) is I completed a lot of the modules way before they were due at the beginning of the semester, so later (when other classes got tougher) I didn't have to worry about ADV.
I took this class for my social and behavioral science core. Im an RTF major so I wanted something easy and this WAS easy. Take it. You won't regret it.

analysis.name: Anne Finley
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Prof Finley is probably one of the best professors I've taken at UT. She is super approachable, caring and wants to help her students learn. She is also really smart. GO TO OFFICE HOURS trust me it'll help. Make sure to come to class bc that is important. Her lectures can be long but as long as you come to class and take notes, you'll be good.

Professor Finley is very caring and genuinely wants her students to learn as much as they can. She definitely appreciates participation in class and during office hours so try to do that as much as you can and you should be fine. For tests, use the unit notes to study and make sure you understand the mechanics of all of the concepts.

Professor Finley was great! This was her first semester teaching and her sections did better than others. She really cares that students understand what's going on and takes a lot of time out of her day to help you. I would def take her again and there was a curve.

Prof Finley really cares about her students and values learning over grades. The course material is difficult, but she does a good job on explaining and is always willing to meet outside of class time. TAKE HER! She is the best.
Hard class, but Professor Finley did a good job of explaining the course material, and all reading are given to you without having to buy a textbook

analysis.name: Dananjaya Appulage
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Took Dr. Dan at ACC for Chem 2 Lab. He's very kind, wants you to succeed. Thick accent and speaks fast, so his lab lectures are a little hard to understand, but he is a generous grader. He will try his best to help direct you to the correct answer and even lets you redo work. Be cautious taking him for lecture, might be hard to understand content.

They removed my rating before, but I stand by what I said. This was the worst science professor I have ever had in 3 separate countries. He was rude, homophobic, spoke constantly and handed out papers during active exams, and treated his students as less than. 
This man shouldn't teach.

I went to every class. I aced every online quiz due to 2 attempts, and I aced every homework assignment. I stayed for 1:1s. I went to tutoring. I did group work nothing worked. I found the professor to be really hard to understand with his thick accent, but equally hard to understand his concepts when he broke it down and that becomes your problem.

I wish professor Dan used the board more. He is super chill and understanding but just goes through the course contents on the presentation. At the end of the semester, the presentation wasn't working and when he taught on the board, it was so much more informative. Great professor overall. Easy to get As if you invest enough time.

He cares about his students, offers flexible schedules, and inspires us to do our best. He shares his experiences, gives helpful advice and encourages questions if we don't understand. He's available during office hours and is passionate about learning. I'm glad I took chemistry with him. Amazing professor!

analysis.name: Brendan Apfeld
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Awesome Professor. Chill, young dude. Does not grade hard. If you actually do the assignments then you can expect an easy A in this class. There are 2 multi choice tests and a paper at the end of the semester. The paper is only 4 pages tho! I got a 90 and an 80 on the tests with only a few hours of studying for each. And a 95 on the paper.

Apfeld's class is fairly easy, though the tests are more difficult than you might expect. He makes occasional jokes and his videos that he plays during lectures are generally very entertaining, though the lectures themselves are sometimes boring. Attendance is not mandatory though your alternative is the most boring set of books put to print.

Took a risk taking a first-time teacher and it paid off. Very fair exams, fun assignments and great teacher. Glad I took him. Only con is the textbook sucks, but he said he hates it and won't use it again. The exams are fairly lectured based, but he puts the powerpoints online so its not life or death if you miss some classes!

I LOVED Apfeld! He really wants his students to do well. It's 25% midterm & 25% final (both curved), 25% a paper (he'll give you 100 if you check all the boxes he's looking for), and 25% a series of community engagement things (5 for 5% each). I was nervous about it but I was really glad he made us do them. He's a great guy and a good teacher!

I took a chance on Professor Apfeld. This was his first time teaching a college class so he had no reviews or anything. That said, this is a very talented young dude and a great teacher. Readings are long, but study (memorize) the lecture slides HARD for every quiz and test and you can get fairly easy 100's. It's April and I have a 99.3 average.

analysis.name: Jamie Aprile
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 29 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Completely unrealistic expectations! This is an Intro course and half or more of the students are non-majors and she expects everyone to memorize the what, where, when and significance of EVERY SINGLE artifact, building, and sculpture we have EVER SEEN in class or in the book. Absolutely ridiculous! This is like an UD Art History class! Do not take

She does read off a paper but that's because she is telling you the stories of mythology. If you think she is rambling then you aren't paying attention. It's not too much, but you have to write down EVERYTHING! Then reguritate it on the test and you will get an A. Sometimes I would have to read the book for discussion post but it was easy enough.

Very poor teacher. Reads off a sheet for the entire 50 min and mumbles her sentences. Worst of all, when I had her she designed her tests so that no one could finish (not even on purpose). She's new and I think she got flustered and didn't know how to conduct the class during those 4 days we missed because of the weather. AVOID

She is ridiculously passionate. Honestly, it really is a TON of information in only THREE tests, so there's a ton of studying needed for each test. That being said, people grumble about it being super hard, BUT it really isn't If you take decent lecture notes a ton of those too!) and read the SUMMARIES online, NOT the book. Study SMART. Easy A.

She was a really good professor. After a few classes though, the class (which comprised of 9 students) figured that we have to ask questions because she literally can talk non-stop for an hour straight. She used power points for her slide so there is at least some visual aids in the class. There will be a lot of reading though.

analysis.name: Aquasia Shaw
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment:
(-) Seems like a cool person ig but that's all I can say
(+) Terrible at letting us know if class was in-person or zoom. Bad at giving instructions for in-class assignments & knocked off points for instructions she never gave. Never posted slides or study guides despite exams being lecture heavy. Same as last years reviews, just overall, bad.

Worst class I have taken. It is EXTREMELY unorganized, does not follow the syllabus, gives major assignments with hardly any guidance, horrible communication, and tough grading. She never posted lecture slides. Not to mention she threw a dry erase marker across the room at a student for whispering with no previous warning. Awful class.

I feel bad giving her a poor rating, but I feel like there were a lot of things wrong with her class and teaching style. She didn't really teach us anything. She was more of a facilitator for our group projects while grading us unreasonably hard and giving little to no instruction. I feel like with time, she'll get better, but 355 was a disaster.

such a hard grader and her feedback makes 0 sense. She will take off 10+ points off of a paper for the SMALLEST thing and papers are a large percentage of your grade. assignments had absolutely no criteria or guidance. VERY political and I was afraid to speak out for the opposite position because she would've taken it out against me and my grade.

She is really disorganized and you really don't know your grade in the class until the end of the semester. The class does not follow the syllabus. She threw us into assignments and projects with little to no guidance and she grades harshly. Not a mean lady like the other comment claims, just really disorganized.

analysis.name: Arjun Sobnack
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 28 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Sobnack doesn't know what he's doing at all, ever. If he's as good at rock climbing as he is at teaching, he's a subpar climber at best. It is possible to do well because of the generous curve, especially if you've taken Calc BC before. He is so creative, he can make even the easiest topic seem impossible.

Sobnack does have super hard tests/quiz, mainly b/c he uses odd symbols and sometimes Q's are more theoretical than hard calculations (lot of proofs, Q's don't use numbers but symbols instead) You might be shocked by the first quiz, but literally trust the curve and you'll likely be ok. This class WILL make you smarter & I appreciate in retrospect.

Nice guy, but unable to communicate his knowledge of math to students. He kinda fixed this and started a curve (60->90). No recorded lectures. Practice sets weren't provided until the night before a quiz/exam, and often came w/o solutions & were unreflective of the exam. Homework is unreflective of exam. Graded only by tests, quizzes, and homework.

VERY difficult class to stay motivated in; NOT recommended if you're new to Calc 2. Very DIY w/ resources beyond lecture. It's you, Quest, & the textbook. Exam Qs are hard to understand & impossible to solve in time. Exams: 3 FRQs with 2-4 parts each. If you miss one, the next may be impossible. Nice Prof. Avoid or commit to a life of uncertainty.

chill guy but makes me want to kms so bad. genuinely got diddled by every quiz/test in this class. the in class examples are like not too bad but then the quiz and tests have GENIUNELY been dug out of the deepest depths of his bootyhole. he meekly chuckles and tries to be helpful. silly guy but AT WHAT COST. he also rock climbs which is pretty tuff

analysis.name: Arielle Woznica
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: One of my favorite classes I've ever taken! She's a great lecturer and the material is interesting itself. Course is a bit more self driven because the grade is mostly exam heavy and homework/instapoll is completion, but she provides a lot of help if you seek it and she is constantly available. Exams are fair, and she offers a bit of extra credit.

Really great professor, it's obvious she's very passionate about cell biology and as long as you keep up with the material throughout the semester you will do fine. Super knowledgable and very approachable outside class. There's a big emphasis on designing experiments that demonstrate cellular processes so the class isn't just brute memorization

Taught cell biology in a cool way. You need to go to class to do well, attendance isn't "mandatory" but it probably is in order to be prepared for exams. Very accessible outside of class and was always willing to explain things in class and not make you feel silly.

analysis.name: Arianna Avalle
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Avalle had been my all time favorite professor. Throughout the semester, she not only wanted me to succeed, but she went out of her way to make sure that I understood the material. She was very reachable outside of class and during office hours. I cannot say enough nice things about her. Often, she brought homemade treats to class.

I noticed that one of the reviews stated that Professor Avalle “tries too hard to be liked”. This is actually a positive! Professor Avalle goes out of her way to get to know the needs and ambitions of each individual student. She always tries to form a bond with each of her students and it is evident that she deeply cares!

I would definitely take intro to Italian with Arianna again if given the chance, she is such a kind professor and understanding! You can tell she has a passion for what she does, I really enjoyed this class despite having zero previous Italian knowledge. I found that the class flowed nicely and modules were easy to follow! 10/10 recommend beginners

analysis.name: Arvind  Ravikumar
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Worst Prof Ive had so far. Super unprofessional, did not release a guide to our on paper coding midterm until TWO DAYS before it, so we had no idea what to expect. Kept saying he would release solutions to final guide and NEVER DID. failed to prepare us for HW so AI was a must even though it was 'forbidden'. I maybe got an A but I learned nothing.

The professor is knowledgeable in the subject and is kind to students. However, the class focusses so much on the math and the theory behind numerical methods that when it comes time to do real problems it often seems impossible to accomplish by oneself. Homework at the beginning of the course easily took 4 hours each week however lighten later.

Lectures do not help you with the homework or tests. He spends much more time explaining the intricacies of numerical methods than teaching you how to translate word problems to coding problems, which is really what the tests are about. He doesnt teach coding well, but expects everyone to know how to do it, then he is surprised when no one does.

analysis.name: Arturo Jimenez
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Arturo was a good professor. He kept the class engaged and did his best to encourage student participation. Students sometimes won't answer, and it'll make the atmosphere awkward at times, but other than that, as long as you have a good TA, you should be good. Be sure you take this class seriously and make work you're proud of.

Arturo is an okay professor! His lectures are often surface-level but sometimes he goes more in depth on some interesting industry topics like film festivals etc. He often seemed uninterested in teaching the class and like he hated it LOL but this class definitely does teach you vital things to go into film production. Just wish he dived deeper :/

Professor Jimenez is my favorite professor I've had so far! His lectures were so informative and helpful to get an intro understanding of the industry. 
He is so passionate about film, which might be his only flaw. It seems like he expects everyone to be as passionate as he is, which is understandable since he's teaching hundreds of film students.

Prof. Jimenez is extremely passionate about the film industry, sometimes to a fault. Lectures are informative and fun, but he will get verbally upset if students do not engage with his lecture/answer questions often enough. The 3 film projects are tough to organize but are graded fairly, and the TA's give lots of incredible feedback on your work.

analysis.name: Arcelia Hernandez
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I would NOT recommend taking this class with Dr. Hernandez. The course felt very unorganized, and I received low grades without clear feedback or explanation. While she was kind and created a safe space, the grading felt unfair and unclear, which made the experience frustrating and discouraging.

Unfortunately, she had a bad experience with a past student and mentioned it repeatedly during many of our class meetings. That made it seem like she doesn't trust any of her students. Lots of assignments due in a 3-hour course that already requires 10-15 hours per week of fieldwork. Future students deserve a better time

If you can take any other professor do it. She is condescending and treats her students like children. She has a ton of assignments and her grading system is confusing. She spends most of the class time telling random anecdotes and the rest of it is just spent watching videos. There's no reason to show up to class but if you don't she'll fail you.

Says she cares about her students but doesn't at all. Horrible grader, if you go against what she says or her opinion you are always wrong. Would never take her again if I had to. The whole reason I why I had a horrible senior year and why I wouldn't recommend people to be an education major at UT Austin

analysis.name: ATILA NOVOSELAC
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Only thing I disliked about the class was the enormous 1" = 1' model we had to make, which cost like $100 (divided by 5 people). Other than that, the class was chill and easy with cool speakers.

Professor Novoselac is an outstanding introduction to architectural engineering. He is extremely knowledgeable, friendly, understanding, and very approachable. The guest lecture panels throughout the course were especially useful. One time, when our projects were accidentally thrown away by a janitor, he even bought the entire class Ferrero Rocher!

Professor Novoselac is a very nice person, and he tried to help all of us navigate the beginnings of ARE. The guest lecturers were interesting. Sometimes the material was disorganized. The group project took a long time to complete, so think ahead for that. Very nice beginning to Architectural Engineering for me!

This is a great guy. Super chill and easiest class I've taken. Tests are all open book/open note, project 1 was a little tedious but everything else was super easy. Even though this class was really chill, I think I got a lot out of the guest speakers. Take advantage of the opportunity to learn in this class!!

Lectures included guest speakers who has slides we would take notes on. Notes would be turned in at the end of the year (I love that he made us take notes because I could not tell you one thing a presenter said from the top of my head but it was useful ArchE stuff). Group project was somewhat hard, but office hours helped and buy materials aheaddd.

analysis.name: Lucy Atkinson
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: They fell kind of behind so felt like everything was pushed back at last second but outside of that the professor is nice but this class was just a class I decided to take outside of my major so any grade I may have gotten because of that is on me.

The sweetest professor ever, take this class!!! Her class is so laid back and chill. Assignments are simple and easy, projects are also very straightforward. This class is a relief and I actually learned a lot.
0 extra credit. Will give an A- if 0.1 decimals off an A

As an engineering major, this was a nice class. laid back, discussion based. Just do your part in group projects and keep up with assignments. Dr. Atkinson (who prefers Lucy) is witty and engaging with her lectures. Breath of fresh air.

This class was really interesting and her class is extremely well-organized. As long as you actually read the textbook and take good notes, you will be okay. Consistent effort is key to succeeding this class.

analysis.name: Athanasio Papalexandrou
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 61 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: The prof is great but the older reviews exaggerate how easy the class is- you need to work for an A. Lectures are recorded & there are mandatory labs w/ weekly response papers (completion grade). TAs grade the first exam harshly, and you need to rewatch the lectures and pay attention to catch the details they want you to mention on exams

Definitely not as easy as the previous reviews have claimed, but the class was doable. T/F and MCQs felt like random trivia questions at times, but the writing portions were easy as long as you keep up with lectures and discussion sessions. Grading varies by TA, mine graded harshly initially but became more lenient as the semester progressed.

You can tell he really cares about what he teaches, he's passionate and that makes lectures interesting. There is a lot of reading needed for the class and the lab but it's very manageable if you're good at writing. The workload is light! I very much recommend the class, you don't need to go to the lectures as long as you watch them online.

Took two semesters of his art history classes. Easy grading; wrote a terrible-quality paper and still got a B on it. Incredibly kind and genuinely wants to get to know his students. Very thick accent that is both endearing and a bit hard to understand. He is super passionate about the subject, which helps if you are not interested in art.

Such a cute prof. Kind of funny, referred to Augustus of Prima Porta as incredibly sexy. Was absent one day, and came to office hours once and he spent the entire time going over the presentation. Caring prof. Greek accent takes a while to get used to. ATTEND LECTURES!!! Grading is P/F for lab questions and from tests. No final either.

analysis.name: Wang Atlas
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Overall this was a really great class. Prof posts all of his slides with the concepts very clearly described. Wasn't the best lecturer imo but going to lecture isn't necessary to gain a lot from the class. Homeworks and final project took a lot of time, but overall were worth it.

Professor Wang is a true legend and perhaps the smartest person I've ever encountered. 

Unlike many professors who just read textbooks, he teaches effortlessly from his vast knowledge. He's engaging, incredibly kind, and adaptable, always happy to take questions and meet student needs. 

Such a pity UT cannot keep him teaching longer!

Besides the fact that he is one of the best researchers in his field, Prof. Wang is also a great teacher! He has very well-organized lectures and is a grandmaster describing the intuition of the material.
Lectures are fun. The class is not all that difficult, but Prof. Wang does go in depth in lectures and is very willing to dive deep into specific things the class asks.

analysis.name: Nigel Atkinson
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Do not take Atkinson. His lectures are so convoluted that you can easily get confused even if you already understand the material from the textbook. You have to decipher what his tests are asking and you probably won't pass unless you memorize the whole book or have his old exams. Thankfully I had a wonderful TA so that's the only reason I passed.

Neuroepigenetics- This is a hard class but if you do the homework and the study guides (which are basically the tests), an A is very achievable. He is very knowledgeable but a little hard to understand, will clarify when asked. We had 2 group poster projects that are worth as much as the test, and are easy to get an A for if you follow the rubric.

Hard class. If you can read for yourself and understand the material, you can get an A. The tests are difficult. He doesn't add anything to his lectures, so it is almost pointless to go; it'd be better to just spend that time reading the book. Half of the test question are from old homeworks/old tests and the other half are new.

CONS:
The epigenetics class was: VERY DISORGANIZED, had no clear rubric/expectations, and the grades were returned WEEKS later. It is PROJECT HEAVY ( 4 presentations and a Wikipedia article). 
PROS:
He grades presentations/ article relative to others/yourself/ and level of effort. The practice exams ARE the exams (still hard though). An A is doable

He is a nice guy, but his lectures are painfully boring. His tests are difficult, and he writes them aiming for a 70-72 average. He does not curve or use plus/ minus grading. The class was disorganized and the expectations were unclear. You pretty much learn from your book and TA. I consider myself a strong bio student, but struggled in this class.

analysis.name: Lucinda Atkinson
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Her lectures are really helpful and easy to understand. She is engaging and gives you bonus questions that are super easy if you came to class!

Dr. Lucy is the BEST! She makes the lectures interesting and provides plenty of in-class extra credit. You do have to read the books for the tests, but luckily they're pretty interesting. She really enjoys discussions too, sometimes we would get so busy discussing in class that we would end up having to cut information off of the tests!

This class was okay. It definitely was not hard by any means but i will say there is a lot of work you need to do. Each module takes an hour to two hours to complete so it definitely sucked doing those but most of the stuff is things you will see on the exam. I read the textbook sometimes but mostly never and still got an A.

I loved this class and i loved her as a professor. She makes the class fun and easy to understand. Also the tests were easy as long as you read your notes and sometimes textbook. Attendance not mandatory but the bonus questions were based on class lectures. it was an easy A.

I'm not a business major, was thrown into this class (since another was cancelled 2 days before classes started) but could not be happier. She really kept this class interesting and fun, and gave plenty of opportunities to succeed. Read the book, take good notes, and you'll get an A+, and you'll actually enjoy yourself. Favorite professor so far!

analysis.name: Rowland Atiase
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Atiase is by far my least favorite professor I have ever taken. His sarcastic attempts at humor seem to demean students more often than encourage or amuse them. You come to class to copy down verbal notes which could be posted online instead. Homework is explained, in a confusing, hard to understand manner, leaving you to learn on your own.

This class consists of you doing a ton of reading and written homework/handouts before class (at least 2 hrs for each "lecture"), coming to class to copy notes verbatim that he won't post online, and then getting called on to answer the questions you did before class without a good explanation. You have to teach yourself--just avoid altogether

Don't do it! Claims that he doesn't give us busy work, but that is all he gives us. Teaches too fast, and has the audacity to call exams "parties". He is a very smart guy, as he's worked at some very high up companies in the world, but teaching just isn't his thing. Avoid him at all costs please, unless you are feeling like a risk-taker.

Prof Atiase may not be my favorite professor ever, but he definitely is not as bad as the other reviews here make him out to be. There is a lot of written homework due before each class, but it is completion and he just wants you to attempt it before actually seeing the solutions in class. Tests are very similar to the review problems which is nice

Homework structure supports memorization, not learning. Lectures are worthless fill-in-the-blank notes that he reads from. He either assigns busy work or problems that he has not prepared you to complete. Hard to understand due to accent. Only reason I did okay was bc his test was near identical to the review. Lots of wasted time in class. ACC 312H

analysis.name: Florence Atiase
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The class itself is pretty tough and not just because of the subject matter. It's how she grades. I really wish I took this class with a different professor! Avoid, if you can.
Sometimes hard to understand and hard to follow in lectures. Also, very uninteresting to listen to because of the way she teaches
Her class was very difficult but she did a great job of making difficult material more easy to understand.
A very good professor, helpful, good explanations.

analysis.name: August Shi
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Useless lectures, self-taught course/no guidance, unclear project requirements, no announcements on canvas, expected to check Piazza to do well/pass, harder projects than other profs, unreasonable expectations, not understanding/flexible, no Test reviews, unorganized exams, doesn't use IDE, unlear answers to questions, taught like a grad course.

This Prof has useless lectures and is not understanding at all. He doesn't have practice exams and doesn't send out announcements that are crucial to passing assignments/the class.The lack of coordination among the professor and their TAs has negative consequences on students' grades. Take a different professor if you can.
The best faculty I've ever met.

He's definitely knowledgeable and speaks with coherence and confidence, but I found that I had to do a lot of learning after lectures to comprehend the concepts. Granted, that could be an issue on my part. Workload was manageable, but there would be 0 feedback left on assignments, which was odd. Advice: watch Coding With John and Bro Code!!

Definitely take Nando over him
-Next to no review material for exams, only one previous exam. Actual exam was way harder, ~70 avg no curve
-Tests and projects are much harder than other profs
-No in class test review or exam prep guidance
-Useless lectures, don't help with projects, just end up self studying 
Overall way harder than it should be

analysis.name: Javier Auyero
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 82 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Javier is HILARIOUS and so knowledgable. He explains things incredibly elegantly in a way that's super easy to understand. Pop quizzes can sneak up on you, but if you listen, he usually gives the answers in lecture. There's a lot of reading, but you can get by just using his explanations. Definitely one of the coolest professors ever.
This class was super intensive and not as easy or a blow-off class. You seriously have to put in work. ALOT of reading and be ready(and beware) for POP quizzes.

Very interesting (albeit boring) class and the prof was great. Attendance during main lecture isn't mandatory, TA sessions (required, but chill). Quizzes were light (gives answers in class usually), reading was so long and boring but you can get away w/ not reading (goes over in class),and essays were long but light. better than other ugs - easy A.

He is amazing, I will always recommend. You have 2 papers and like 4/5 quizzes, lowest one is dropped. He gives you all the answers before the quiz. Show up to every lecture and you will be fine. He is so amazing and funny. The best class I had all semester. TA meetings seem a bit useless but it was nice getting to know them. Overall, take Javier.

Attendance is only mandatory for discussion sections. Very generous and understanding to students. I didn't actually read because he would always go over the answers and readings for the quizzes (he was discussing maybe changing that, but he may not). Very easy and interesting UGS. More controversial topics but if you're into sociology I say do it!

analysis.name: Aurora Wallace
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She's a new professor at UT but friendly. Lectures are straightforward. Homeworks are short. She offers plenty of support if you're confused. Participation work is required on Mondays, but she gives makeups for it. Exams closely follow the practice materials and HW, though they can get tricky—especially the final. Highly recommend!

Really great experience taking her for Probability 1. Explains everything very clearly and tests are pretty easy as long as you are familiar with the material. Gives a lot of really good prep material for the tests too.

The course content itself is incredibly easy. If you get stuck, she is very helpful over email/office hours. I did very well on the HWs and midterms, but I just barely got an A bc of the final, which is weighted 30%. In-class activities once a week for a participation grade. Handwriting is a bit difficult to read at times.
Really great and caring professor. Good lecturer as well, although attendance wasn't mandatory — take if you can.

analysis.name: Celest Austin
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She is SOOO nice. Got super lucky with registering for her class for Fall 2024. Individual exams are 45% with the rest of the grade being group exams, group work, and instapoll. IMO the groups were big enough so that at least a few ppl could be on top of things, and even though the exams were hard, they weren't weighed heavily + small curves!

She is such an amazing teacher and lecturer. She breaks down every concept completely from scratch so that everything is very digestible and easy to understand, and you can tell she genuinely cares about her students understanding the material by the quality of her explanations and slides.

Dr Austin is so kind and a great lecturer. She's so smart and passionate about physiology and teaching. She makes it attainable to know the material and understand it. The way she did group homework assignments was helpful and group exams were extremely helpful as well. She's so accessible outside of class as well as her TA's and they're so helpful

Dr. Austin was awesome. She encouraged us to truly understand physiology by forming connections rather than simply memorizing facts. Most of our grade was derived from group assignments (weekly homework, iClicker, group exams). As much as I dreaded physiology entering the class, I left with a love of the subject and a deeper understanding as well.

Dr. Austin is THE BEST. Study for exams by using HER lecture and exam review slides, explaining the concepts to yourself, as well as doing the practice problems for math-related topics/questions. She has learning objectives from another prof which you can do for extra practice but you should mostly focus on her slides and you'll be fine.

analysis.name: Jennifer Austin
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I loved Austin as a professor and she made the class more intriguing and forced you to be involved. Charismatic and light personality and brough positive vibes into every lecture. Take her for any class that you can because if you mess up, she is very generous and tells you exactly where you went wrong. Avg/easy HW and Exam difficulty, long HW's.

A very nice professor. The homeworks are insanely difficult, but she has tons of documents available to help with the homework. The tests are exactly like the test reviews and she is very helpful in getting people prepared for the tests. She doesn't explain some of the in depth concepts the best, but you at least understand how to do the problems.

One of the few amazing teachers at the ut math department, She breaks down complex proof topics into easy to understand lectures and practice problems. Tests were not too bad if you studied for them, and did the review problems. A lot of extra credit was given if you participated in class problems and presentation problems, definitely a must take.

Dr. Austin is really nice and creates an environment where you can focus on learning without worrying about your grade. Her guidance is great, and she is a must take professor to enjoy your intro to proofs class. Overall 100% recommend taking her.

This review is for M 175T, Being You in Mathematics. It is indeed rather boring. However, I cannot deny that it is applicable to math majors, even pure math majors. Take this class to get your ethics flag done and perhaps learn a bit more about the major in the process.

analysis.name: Andrew Augustin
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Media and Technology. Very interesting class! Learned so much about level design and the art that goes into making 2-d games in Unity. Definitely great for beginners such as myself. It was a lot of work but! It was fun work and not agonizing work, very simple and got a 100 in the class, very easy grading too.

I don't want to be biased, but honestly professor Augustin is the best teacher that I have had in my entire life. He goes above and beyond not only for his work and projects, but also for his students. He is always watching out for you and may come off as having high expectations, but genuinely its because he cares.

Design&Interactivity is focused on creating a character, an environment, and then making a game based off of that in Unity. I never attended the in person sessions (class was held once a week online) and despite taking that blow to my grade, still ended with an A. As long as you try you'll do great. Prof Augustin himself is super cool and laidback!

Love Professor Augustin! He makes it clear that you will get a good grade as long as you try your best, and he is super understanding when you have other things going on. He's also generally very cool and funny. I'm taking another one of his classes next semester because he was so nice to be around.

analysis.name: Audrey Duarte
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment:
*This rating is for PSY 332S*
 I was very optimistic about taking Neuroscience of Sleep; however, Professor Duarte was extremely condescending when I asked for feedback. She had daily quizzes over readings, and you had only 5 minutes to answer the question in full paragraph form, which had to have extremely proper grammar that made sense to her.

I did really well in Psychopharmacology with Duarte but not because of any help she provided. Her lectures are really interesting and the topic is fascinating, but Duarte doesn't provide ANY resources to study except for in class slide shows. I  passed with an A+ by making hundreds of flashcards for each test covering every sentence on every slide.

I found her class harder than expected- it definitely requires studying to do well. There were 2 lectures a week (which were fairly dense), but she was very willing to help out outside of class hours with more than just the class, which i appreciated. She's a good professor and knows what she's doing- just make sure you put the time in the class.

She is really smart but just doesn't know how to teach a class. The only assignments in the class was a paper and a few in class quizzes with one question. The tests are like trying to win trivia. No emphasis on what you need to know, and she tests very randomly. It is a strange combination of neuroscience, history, etymology, and geography.

Grade is based primarily on 4 exams. While you can drop one exam from your final grade, her exams are very difficult. She is very lecture heavy and so you need to be prepared to be a good note taker as her slides aren't sufficient and she doesn't record her lectures. Took a huge chunk of study time and effort. I wouldn't take her again.

analysis.name: Michael Aubrey
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I don't think Dr. Aubrey should be teaching Gen Chem 2. His quizzes are hard and you can't study for them because he puts a harder version of the example that you have never seen, he makes mistakes that have to be corrected by students. He doesn't explain things during lecture and expects us to know a lot (we are 2nd semester first-year students).

This class is recommended for the chemistry major/honors track and so most of us thought we had to take it, but you do not have to! Dr. Aubrey is one of those guys that are just way too smart to be teaching intro to gen chem. Because he is so smart he does not explain nor teach very well. He is not a good teacher, but he is nice, I don't recommend.

Lectures are hard to follow and are frequently focused on interesting but ultimately irrelevant applications or details of course content, making tests and quizzes very difficult. The textbooks are the best way to learn the test/quiz relevant material. He's kind and clearly very knowledgeable about the content, but doesn't convey it well.

Prof. Aubrey is new at teaching this class and pretty bad at it so far. His quizzes are inconsistent, difficult, and have had lots of mistakes. He does not explain things at all and assumes we should know everything. This is Gen Chem 2 for chem majors and makes me want to change my major. :(

For his materials chemistry course his test reviews did not actually prepare us for what would be on the tests. Topics would be on there we hadn't even really covered. He seems like he knows what he is talking about and is very knowledgeable, just not the best at preparing us for exams and thus our grades kind of took a hit because of this.

analysis.name: Andrei Straumanis
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 916 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: During my three years at UT-Austin I had always enjoyed my professors and excelled in their classes... that was until I made the regrettable mistake of registering for a course with this egotistical man who has the nerve to call himself a 'professor.' You can throw all sanity and well-being out the window if you plan to be a student of his. Don't.
Grades tough and tends to lose his bike.

Dr. Straumanis fails to understand that everyone learns differently because he is so set on his way. POGIL works great when BALANCED with a traditional lecture. POGIL is meant to reinforce ideas, not cause mental breakdowns every week due to unfair quizzes. Quizzes dont accurately represent material and have unreasonable time constraints.

Two words: F.U STRAUMANIS! This class was insanely hard, no help from the professor and quizzes were 5 minutes in length while it took this wannabe marine biologist 20 to explain the whole thing. No reviews for exams and you sure bet the exams were hard! Lots of fun to fail every test!

One I asked him a question during class because I was confused. The answer I received was "I think you are confused about something deeper, I am going to go help other students that need me." Instead of answering my questions he just left. He has no office hours, you are teaching yourself. Absolutely don't take his class if you want to learn.

analysis.name: Audrey Shaffer
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Shaffer is very kind, and is a very good professor. She gives very specific feedback, and provides extra credit. She's also willing to work with every student. Attendance is mandatory, but it makes up a big chunk of your grade and is easy points. She's amazing, I love her. My speaking has improved a lot because of this class.

Prof Shaffer is a professor that really only wants to see you do good. Understands all the pop culture references and is really respectful to all her students. Can have a good laugh while still being productive and will answer any questions you have. Class is not difficult, but it is time consuming.I do recommend mainly due to Prof Shaffer.

This class helped me (mostly) get over my fear of public speaking! Prof Shaffer was very kind and encouraging to all of her students and allowed us to give speeches based on our actual interests instead of just boring assigned topics. If you're going to take this class, make sure you get Prof Shaffer as your instructor.

I wish I could stay in this class forever. I loved Prof Shaffer so much. She cares for her students like no other professor I've had, and her feedback was always helpful. This is an amazing class that I think everyone should take (and definitely try to take it with Audrey Shaffer)!

analysis.name: Audrey Blood
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Audrey made me fall in love with printmaking. Truly the perfect professor for intro to print. Jumping between four types of printmaking in one semester seemed overwhelming in my head, but audrey and our TA noah made it so doable and fun. She is so knowledgeable about processes, concepts, and history of print. You must take print if she's teaching!

I love Audrey. She is incredibly well prepared always and organized. Is knowledgeable about almost all printmaking but especially Intaglio and papermaking. She gives fantastic support, feedback, and suggestions (artists, films, books, poems, research, etc.) Her class discussions were so insightful and fun. Such a wonderfully kind educator as well.
Loved this class!! Audrey is so nice and is so helpful. She definitely helped me with my drawing skills. I would recommend any art class given by her.

analysis.name: Ashley Matheny
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
