review_highlights.comment: Dr Matheny is the sweetest professor and really cares about her students. She tells you pretty much exactly what is on the exams. Two midterms and a semester project, easy peasy. She moves due dates if she feels her students are too busy. Great lecturer as well, definitely recommend!

Dr. Matheny is an incredible professor! I thoroughly enjoyed taking her Intro to Hydro course. Although I got a B, I would absolutely take another class with her, as my B was due to my own personal issues. She was very helpful and understanding, and her lectures were entertaining even online. You can tell she is very passionate and knowledgeable.

Dr. Matheny is a great professor. She is easy to listen to, and makes her lectures interesting. The class isn't super hard, as long as you pay attention during lecture. Assignments were always graded quickly and fairly, and she is super accommodating if you need anything. Would definitely recommend taking any of her class, she is such a gem!

I loved this course and Dr. Matheny. She worked with students to make sure that everything was fair, assignments were graded within a week (usually within a few days), and she is just such a fun person. Definitely one of my absolute favorite professors. You can really tell that she cares about her students over grading

Amazing lecturer and always ready to help everyone understand anything, inside or outside of the classroom. Gives lots of examples for 'real life' career/scientist skills. Creates a community feeling around projects and research! Would definitely take her class again!

analysis.name: Astrid Runggaldier
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 26 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I accidentally took an upper-division art history class as a freshman, so this class was a bit tough for me. Dr. Runggaldier is pretty vague in her directions and I received some pretty poor grades because of misinterpretations. She uses lecture slides but they don't have text on them, just photos, so it's not really helpful for exam reviewing.

She obviously is very knowledgeable in her field; her class is reading, and lecture heavy. The majority of your grade is dependent on a multi-part project throughout the semester, and if you are not accustomed to writing for art it can be a learning curve, if you are thinking about this class for your VAPA I would recommend something easier.

This professor is a very harsh grader. EOY project is worth so much, but she has never given anybody a 100 on a single section of the project that was submitted (I checked the Canvas median). The tests aren't that hard, but what kills is you are the essays that are apparently "never perfect". Please don't take if you scared of getting a A- or B+.

AMAZING PROF!! Best choice I could have made for first semester VAPA. She cares about student understanding of the material and constantly asks for feedback. Attendance isn't mandatory, but you'll have to attend every lecture and read the textbook to do well. Material is incredibly interesting and she makes lectures engaging. Would take again!

I have never felt so disrespected or afraid of a professor in my entire life. I genuinely dread going to class and facing her wrath and I am a good, dedicated student. I do NOT recommend taking a course with her. She's not blunt, she's demeaning. Does not shy away from humiliating students, so the discussions are usually silent out of pure fear.

analysis.name: Ashley  Moran
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Moran is awesome, very knowledgeable in her field, and cares about her students. Participate in class discussions, as she keeps a very close eye on who talks and uses that to determine participation grades. Tests are short answer questions that aren't hard if you pay attention in class. The readings will help but you don't NEED them to pass.
She is a very caring professor, but the class it pretty content heavy and tests can be tough. You definitely have to do the readings and work hard.
Kindest professor ever! Easy, fair grader and very caring of her students. The content is very interesting and presented in a way that is easy to understand and remember. Would recommend!

One of the best Professors I have ever had. She genuinely cares about the content and her students and is an amazing lecturer. Weekly discussion posts over assigned readings are due every Sunday but are mostly completion grades and cover material discussed in the following lectures. I've never retained so much from a class I loved it!

Professor Moran is a great professor who is extremely knowledgeable about the course content. There are lots of dense readings every week to get through and a weekly reaction discussion post. Lectures can be a bit slow at times, but the course is super interesting and enjoyable. Professor Moran is very helpful and wants you to succeed!

analysis.name: Ashley Farmer
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 25 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Farmer is one of the best professors I have had. She has so much passion and energy for African American history. Lectures were so engaging and insightful. There is a-lot of reading that is assigned, but most of it was interesting and it is helpful to do well in the class. You will learn alot. Put in effort and it will be worth it.

Dr. Farmer is an amazing professor who really just does it for the love of the game. She can be a little bit harsh at times but its always out of love. She is a relatively easy grader and her classes are amazing. I hope i get to take her class again. Only gripe was one of her assignments required use of AI.

I took AFR 360 (black freedom movement) and this was one of my favorite classes, being a math major. She made the class amazing with her genuine personality and being so funny. Lots of reading but she makes sure you succeed if you demonstrate that you're trying. Easy exams and easy papers if you spend at least a few days researching and writing.

Very good professor and class. She lectures very well and profoundly. She knows the material very well, and it is easy to succeed. Instapolls, short in-class assignments, and a couple tests make up the grade. I wish she gave us more material to study with for the tests, but not really necessary.

My favorite professor I took this past semester! Dr. Farmer is an amazing teacher, and her enthusiasm made waking up early completely worth it! She's a fantastic storyteller, and she's able to help students realize the importance of learning from history. Attend class, take detailed notes, and study before quizzes/tests - you will do great!

analysis.name: Ashley Coleman Taylor
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Taylor was very organized and clear on her expectations. Was graded on 4 short papers (1 page or so), a video, and a reply video. As long as you read the assignment in detail and hit each point, you will succeed.

Dr. Coleman Taylor is an exemplary educator. She embodies a pedagogical ethos that is in alignment with the intersectional feminist theory she teaches. She treats students as people first, which can be rare to find at the university level. Her feedback is insightful and she challenges you to always dig deeper. You will leave class a different you.

THE BEST PROFESSOR IVE EVER HAD! It was an honor to be taught by Dr. Coleman Taylor. She teaches a thought-provoking, inclusive curriculum that expands upon typical cis, white, male narratives She is also incredibly knowledgeable, often invites amazing guest speakers, and truly cares about her students. I highly recommend her classes.
Very little details or feedback and she doesn't keep up with grades so you never know where you stand in the class. I was scared to speak up in class because she could be very condescending.

analysis.name: Ash D'Harcourt
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This class was fun and engaging. The way Prof Ash structured and paced the course was intuitive and low-stakes, allowing you to focus on the content without stressing about your grade. Grading was very fair, and the TAs consistently provided helpful feedback.
rtf308 is so easy and the TAs are pretty lenient on grading!! be prepared to write essays but other than that its a great vapa

This class was low stress and taught in a way that made it a great intro to going to college. The lectures were all genuinely amusing, and the asynchronous format was really accommodating. The exams were open note and easy as long as you took good notes from the lectures, and the grading criteria for the writing assignments was incredibly clear.

I loved Ash's class! Ten out of ten - one of the sweetest profs I've had at UT. There were at least 10x during the semester that I laughed out loud at a joke they cracked during lecture. Super entertaining to listen to and the lectures were pre-recorded which was great for my full schedule. You can tell they really care about their students.

I love Ash!! Such an incredible professor who really cares about their students. They were always super responsive to emails and there were at least 10x during the semester that I laughed out loud at something funny they said in the lecture. TAKE ASH'S CLASS!! It's asynchronous online, so watch the pre-recorded lectures whenever in the week.

analysis.name: Luis Aviles
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: I took his beginner level (6week long) Spanish course and was forced to pay 62$ for a program to do work that wasn't even graded. Yet he expected everyone to finish (literally) 12 assignments every day. His lectures were unfocused, and I spent most of my time in breakout rooms w peers. Despite him saying he cared it was abundantly clear he didn't.

The quizzes were a little tricky but he really offers a lot of content to study for both exams and quizzes, and makes class really fun to go to. He engages with each student and genuinely cares for each person's wellbeing. Most fun I've had taking a class in college for a long time, and I will miss this prof

I took SPN 314 with Prof Aviles in summer 2021, and I really enjoyed it. He is super enthusiastic and helpful, and he really cares about the students' learning. There was a lot of homework because it was a summer class, but it wasn't too challenging. Overall, it was a great course and I highly recommend taking it with Prof Aviles!

analysis.name: Kiril Avramov
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Avramov is one of the best professors I have taken at this school. This class is interesting at times but can often be boring and he kept everyone engaged. There is a lot of reading but quizzes and tests are open note/book so you don't have to do it all the time, but it helps. Other assignments are short discussion posts. Take this class!

Avramov is one of the greats! Engaging lectures, fascinating material, really genuine guy. My only critique is that the class allows students to succeed without learning the material. Ex- tests are online, hw only covers part of the reading. Bc of this, his class ended up on the back-burner. I wish he demanded more, bc I know I had more to give!

Professor Avramov is super awesome, the lectures are very engaging and this class is super relevant to current events. Discussions are lively and students are super welcomed to share their opinions. Would hundred percent recommend for everyone to take it - one of my favorite classes and professors here at UT!

Dr. Avramov is definitely one of the best professors at UT!! He is the most caring and passionate professor I've had. Cares more about the students actually learning than the grades. There were three exams and two discussions a month based on readings. However, he is pretty lenient and doesn't want to add stress to his students. Take his class

He was one of the best professors I have ever had in college. He is so passionate about these topics that he is teaching which makes it so enjoyable to go to class and learn. Even though it is a big lecture class, he makes an effort to get to know all of his students. Great experience. I am taking another one of his classes next semester.

analysis.name: Avi Blitz

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Blitz is one of the best professors I've ever had, hands down. He will go out of his way to help you, and he cares tremendously for his students. Loved the atmosphere of his class. I am shocked to see that others claim to have not liked his class: I have a feeling they weren't expecting Hebrew to be so difficult. Take him, you'll learn so much!

Avi is an absolute GEM of a professor. His classroom feels like home. He's so kind and welcoming, and he TAILORS THE CLASS MATERIAL TO THE CLASS based on our interests in subject material. He's also accessible out of class at Schulchan Ivrit or by email. He will improve your Hebrew drastically, and you'll have fun learning!

he grades really tough on homeworks (i got a lot of 60s) and there's hw everyday + weekly quizzes. good at teaching, supportive but sometimes unsympathetic (or has too high expectations of how easily we can retain words). accessible through groupme or text, not email. class discussions sometimes became anti-Palestine which was uncomfortable

I would definitely not recommend. This professor demonstrates a lack of care for his students and total apathy about the subject im interested in. A very poor experience I give 0 as a score if I coyld

analysis.name: Avigail Noy

It is reading heavy and discussion based so make sure to read or at least skim. No tests however there are 4 written assignments and weekly journals, but so far they have not given me any issue and 2 of the papers are only 2 pages long.

Took Arabic Lit. Highly difficult class yet rewarding -- you learn a lot! Readings are super difficult. Noy's lectures are amazing and she is easy to reach outside of class and understanding. PLEASE CONTRIBUTE IN THIS CLASS. It's small and discussion based, don't take it if you're not ready to talk. DO THE READINGS, she likes to see effort!

I took her arabian nights class, and really loved it. the class is interesting, and Noy is very knowledgeable. she is a hard grader, however, and sometimes frustratingly so -- a few times i thought about throwing my computer out the window. LOTS of reading. too much. not burdensome, though. overall, id recommend for people interested.

analysis.name: Ronen Avraham
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Uses Socratic method to a fault, basically to have students teach for him. Grades are completely arbitrary and he provides no feedback. Not approachable.
Prof. Avraham is really sweet and loves torts.  He explains a lot of things at a level even a 5 year old could understand. Some other readings were hard to understand.  Overall, highly recommended.
Avraham is funny and makes class enjoyable.  I had him for Torts. He really covers everything he wants you to know during class, so don't miss class!

analysis.name: Axel Turnquist

With a current RMP score of 1.9 and difficulty of 4.6, UT should find another use for him immediately.

This professor is a RED FLAG!!! Avoid this professor at all cost. He lack the ability to teach at all, he does not explain concepts, nor does he actually provide resources. Unless you are trying to drop out of college, DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR. Genuinely might be the worst professor at UT Austin

This is hands down the worst professor I have ever had. He rants about concepts that won't be on the homework or exams for the entirety of class and then grades everything like it's a dissertation. If you think you can teach yourself an upperclass math go ahead - but it will not be fun. He isn't mean, just a terrible professor. UT please fire him.

Regardless of what other reviews say, his grading is NOT lenient. His tests will not match the material and if you want a chance at passing you must read the textbook (which again, is almost as bad as his lectures). 
My grade is wildly different from my peers who took other professors. This seriously needs to be addressed by the Math Department

I thought I was always good at math. I easily surpassed the A grade in every class I took, until I got to this class. This class was a pain. Very theory heavy, and if you don't like that, do NOT take him. His exams are not for people who like applying math, and solving equations.

analysis.name: Marcelo Azambuja

review_highlights.comment: As others have mentioned, Dr. Azambuja works full-time at TxDOT and teaches on the side... but he should probably just stick with TxDOT. He's a pretty unengaging lecturer and is very monotone. The project management material is pretty easy, but his engineering economics lectures are almost unbearable. Exams were straightforward and fair, though.

I went to maybe 6 classes over the course of the semester because it genuinely pained me to listen to this man speak for more than an hour. The content is relatively easy and can be self-taught. I recommend going to the classes before exams because he will talk about what will be tested. Study for tests with hw problems and examples from slides.

If you want a professor that cant teach and will lie to your face and say that he will curve the class but doesn't, Azambuja is the one! All jokes aside, worst teacher I've ever had. All he does is read off the slides with the most monotone voice ever. Doesn't upload slides before class so a lot of ppl skip. All exam avgs were under 75. Good luck.

Honestly one of the worst professors I've ever had, he will not work with you and clearly does not care about the class whatsoever. There's no practice tests so you only have 2 MAYBE 3 homeworks to actually use to study, most of which don't really correlate to the test whatsoever. The most nothingburger class that shouldn't have been difficult.

Worst professor ive ever taken at UT. Nice guy but this man cant teach to save his life. The course itself is easy and the material is light but his exam averages r also very low compared to other PM classes. Doesnt upload slides before class so a lot of people dont go. All he does is read off pwpt slides. Wouldnt take him bc hes a bad teacher.

analysis.name: Dewi Azizah
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style

review_highlights.comment: She's a great and well-intentioned person, but I felt like her lack of organization put me at a disadvantage at times, which I didn't feel was made up for with extra credit. Professor Dewi has been one of my favorite professors on campus. This is a presentation-based class where you will give speeches, typically 1-2 per month. Don't listen to the bad reviews, she's a really kind professor and wants all of her students to pass the class. She is lenient with assignments and understands that we all have busy schedules. This class improved my presentation skills and was also a lot of fun.
She is not a good professor at all. She is completely unorganized, has absolutely no reason for giving the grades that she does, and she does not seem to care about her students

analysis.name: Flávio Azevedo
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Flavio is awesome; genuinely cares about students. Class itself consists of readings which can be long and pretty dense. During lecture, there is A LOT of group discussion. Not hard as long as you do the readings and put in some effort!

Dr. Flavio is a great professor! He really knows his stuff and cares for his students! There were even times he brought cake for all of us! The class isn't difficult! Yes, there is long readings but those can bring you get. 2 drops for it! The midterm isn't that bad since there is a review. You will get to know your classmates! Participate/enjoy it

This grad class is by nature difficult, as a review of cognitive research. Flavio is cool, very laid back. His style is not for everyone (looking at you, A-types), but he makes sure you get what you need out of the class. You are treated as a colleague and beginner researcher, with respect and also support. Your head will explode, but worry not!

Dr. Azevedo is brilliant and you will learn a lot from him. He doesn't really care about grades (it is not really that hard to make an A if you do the right things) but you will care about doing well in his class because you will be inspired to really learn it.

analysis.name: Azfar Moin
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Moin is .. interesting. His lectures are good if you care about the material and he definitely cares about the info he teaches. The class is graded by few things and the criteria are VERY vague. The class itself was fine. the worst part was the TAs. One was RUDE and graded us like grad students though the class is only an intro class.

He's okay. He's funny and likes participation. Lots of reading, but most of it's interesting. Only 1 quiz, 1 paper, 1 midterm, and a final. All essay and short answer. But he gives prompts and choice of words in the test review which he chooses from. It takes work for sure, but it's not impossible. Definitely read & take notes & you'll be okay.
- Only his view is valid - When you ask for help his answers are vague - Rude, criticizes students in class in front of everyone (very unprofessional)
He's an okay professor, he kind of acts like an desi uncle. There is a quiz, a paper, midterm and the final and everything is essay/short answer. Randomly does attendance.

There's a lot of reading but you don't really need to do it to pass the class. I'd recommend doing it and then participating in class discussion; it's an easy way to stand out. The course material is interesting, but Moin expected so little of us that it was hard to care.

analysis.name: Adnan Aziz
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit

analysis.name: Hina Azam

Smart. Knows her stuff. Fantastic choices in readings & a diverse array of them, and very up-to-date on the subjects (unlike some profs who reuse old material to the point of absurdity). Very liberal and will expand your (even if already open) mind.

she ROCKS really funny if youre not a liberal just be warned but she is really funny and is a fair grader. she wants her students to do well. PARTICIPATE it shows her you care and she will fight for you more if she sees that

Omar is a really great guy, and you can tell he cares about his subject a lot. Awapara was a great professor and gave really great lectures. The tests are fairly doable if you pay attention in class and read the assigned readings. You'll also need to do an essay, but it is not that bad.

review_highlights.comment: Genuinely such a nice person, she's one of the kindest professors at UT! Her class is super easy, and even though there are some group projects, it's really doable. This class is super easy, one open note quiz every week and a couple of other assignments here and there. Definitely go to class because there are random attendance checks, and missing too many can add up. Overall really easy class but the professor can be really boring.

Amazing teacher. Very approachable and caring. Open note quizzes and several projects using the UT Library resources. Interesting digital topics during the course. Gives extra credit for early submission in assignments. They can become heavy, starting early is a must.

Professor Gursoy was extremely kind and understanding. She will be lenient with you as long as you talk to her in advance. Extremely easy class. A quiz every week, open note. Two projects. As long as you do your work on time, you will pass.

analysis.name: Ayelet Lushkov

Lots of reading, but you do get to read Game of Thrones a lot in Classics and Modern Fantasy. Essays were rough but debates and discussions were fun.

Professor Ayvaci was a nice guy to say the least, but he had trouble keeping the lectures interesting. Luckily the material is fairly easy and he provides all the slides you need, so if you just read/memorize the slides before the tests and quizzes, you should do fairly well. He definitely knows what he's talking about, but has trouble clarifying.
He should learn that teaching doesnt consist of preparing and showing slides. As a teacher his value should be more than that. Your learning will be mostly limited with your capacity in his class.

Every example is taken directly from the book, and he rarely, if ever, leads the class step-by-step on a block of code, and this is nominally a CODING class. By far the worst MIS professor I've taken thus far at UT. He's just not an effective teacher when the goal is programming knowledge.

He's a nice guy, but not so great of a teacher. I stopped going to class because I couldn't understand his style of teaching and the test was straight from the book anyways. Right before the test I would memorize the powerpoint slides and textbook chapters, and would do ok. Aside from that, the homework assignments and quizzes are really easy!

took his class one semester and found shakespeare completely innacessible, failed it. took it with another prof the next semester and she presented it and breathed a life into it  in such a way that I understood it and enjoy it to this day. made a B.

I took this professor in the mid 1990s, and from these reviews, it sounds like he hasn't changed much.  Terrible instruction.  Abusive to students.  Loves to give Fs.  He certainly knows Shakespeare, it's just a shame he can't teach it.

Great Professor. He is very knowledgeable. If you are pre-law, take his classes. I got into many programs because of his rec letters. He teaches at UT Law. Attendance is mandatory. Two tests: midterm and final. He gives exam reviews for both. Take this class!

Was not familiar with Islam at all coming in but this class is interesting and well structured. Plenty of opportunities for extra credit and easy assignments. Professor Ayoub made it clear that he cared for his students.

analysis.name: Lori Barnes

review_highlights.comment: BA324 is a rough class because the grading is designed to be very specific and nitpicky. However, Professor Barnes does her best to make it enjoyable and genuinely cares for her students. Dr. Barnes is extremely kind and accommodating, but her class is tough. She and her TA are super nitpicky on small details, so make sure to follow the rubrics/examples and ask for clarification. Dr. Barnes is also lenient on regrades since the entire class is pretty subjective, so don't be scared to ask for points back. Pick a good group as well.

BA324 is a challenging course because the grading criteria are very detailed and strict. That said, Professor Barnes makes a real effort to keep the class engaging and clearly cares about her students' success. She also provides thoughtful, helpful feedback when requested. Overall, I would highly recommend taking her class.

LOVE Dr. Barnes!! She makes herself super available to answer any questions about assignments. Honestly a lot of presentations so picking your group wisely matters!! My advice is to always ask her for guidance with any presentation feedback and it will help your next presentation grade because sometimes its tricky to tell what she's looking for!

Dr. Barnes was so entertaining and understanding. Her TA's graded tough, but her assignments and timeframe given were on the easier side and she was super kind and understanding when issues came up. analysis.name: Patrick Badolato

Will say not to get overconfident after first exam, the final is much harder and with no extra credit this time. Wish I had taken more advantage of him

Take this class if you actually want to learn accounting. Classes are very engaging and actually get you to learn instead of just memorize all the boring parts of accounting. Take him! If you want to learn content & gain value from class, you have to take him. analysis.name: William Babler

analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 57 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Very content heavy class, lecture attendance not required and are recorded, don't get behind and study the lecture slides THOROUGHLY (use flashcards), he is very kind but lectures could be scattered and it wasn't clear what would be tested, lab is a bit boring but quizzes and exams aren't too hard, group project is easy too, LOTS of extra credit.

As a result, he rushes through and often doesn't finish lectures, leaving students hanging and completely unprepared for his extremely nitpicky exams.

Babler is a sweet guy, but lectures are him reading off slides and reviewing the content to himself. This is easily one of the hardest classes I've taken, and much harder than the entirety of the MCAT. Take this in your later years where you have time to spare. Write down everything, tiny bullet points with 1-2 words will be on the test.

Generous generous curves and extra credit in lecture and lab. Anatomy has a lot of information to memorize, but you don't have to know anywhere near 100% of every detail to make an A. Realistically you just need to know 70-80% of the material for A, but the class does take up a significant amount time more than your average upper division class.

Prof. Best is an amazing lecturer, and he knows why most students are taking his class, so he makes it as fun and engaging as he can. I would recommend this as a science credit for sure, one of the best classes I've taken here at UT.

Dr. Best is great. Knows students are there for credit, you are still able to get something out of his class if you go every week. There are instapolls in class not for credit and questions for EC every single class so attendance helps your grade.

He knows most people taking this class are not majoring in anything related to astronomy. Still genuinely one of the sweetest, most passionate professors I've ever met. My only regret with this class is not paying attention more during the lecture and choosing to do other class work instead. Every lecture was extremely interesting and engaging.

Best is an amazing professor who is passionate about what he is teaching and genuinely wants to get to know and interact with his students. If you have to join a waitlist for this class, DO IT! I would take this class 1000x over

This is an absolutely diabolical class that will screw up your GPA. Despite being a UGS this class a LOT of work. There were presentations, essays, tests, and a final (not normal for a UGS). analysis.name: Elizabeth Ries

review_highlights.comment: Ries is so sweet, knows a lot about her field, and was just a joy to be in the classroom of! I learned so much about children's literature and had a great time. Definitely take Prof Ries!

Professor Ries cares about student autonomy more than any other professor I've encountered; she will give you a choice about what you want to do at every opportunity. She also gives incredibly detailed feedback. Classes are usually packed with lots of activities, which keeps the environment lively. You'll also do lots of group work

analysis.name: Danielle Berg
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 27 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: TAKE THIS CLASS! Recommended for an easy science credit. Homework is due before every class, but it is very easy and doesn't take much time. The 3 exams are only worth 5% of your grade, and a final project you can do with a group is worth 5% as well. She does Instapolls every class, but you have 4 free skips for the semester.

Straight forward teaching style and makes the topics fairly easy to understand. Lots of homework but each one only counts for a little bit. Pay attention in class because not everything is on the slides but just do the work and you'll be good. Easy and interesting class. some math involved

Prof. Berg was a fun professor. She loves what she does, and you can tell. The class wasn't hard, but you do need to talk to and work with other people a lot. She had some cool expierments from time to time.
easy hw, low stake tests and final project, sometimes the class groupwork was tricky. easy science credit, just have to go to lectures.
Super easy science credit. Daily hw and group assignments all have 3 attempts, tests are pretty easy and open note. Should take!

analysis.name: Amit Bhasin
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I never took the course. He seems like a chill guy, though. I spoke to him a couple of times in person, and he is very knowledgeable about the subject matter he is teaching. I didn't fully follow everything because the class was not related to my major :( I would highly recommend taking any class that he teaches!

He's a great guy I really enjoyed going to class and learning about asphalt lol :). He always listens to the class in terms of making open notes or group quizzes. You can work on homework's in groups and the final exam was open notes. The final was pretty similar to the in person quizzes we took in class. Overall great guy and interesting class.
I took him for design of Bituminous Materials. Very knowledgeable about the subject and gave great lectures where you really do learn a lot. Quizzes are very fair.

A fantastic professor, who genuinely cares about the well-being of his students. In his lectures he gives you important background knowledge and information about the assignments. In every class he promotes curiosity and critical thinking. Although the course load is very heavy with multiple research papers, this course will allow you to grow.

Perhaps my favorite professor at UT, knowledgable, approachable, caring and well-prepared. The project can be a lot of work but is also fun, you learn so much. I would definitely take another class with him.

analysis.name: Venkataraman Bhaskar
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This is a hard class in general, but I would say he is the best professor to take it with. The homework are 10% midterm is 40% and final is 50% of the grade but his curve is the only reason I passed. As long as you show up and take good notes you should have an easier time on the exams. Try to find people to do homework with to help you understand.

High stakes exams (Midterm 40% and Final 50%). No recorded lectures, but lecture notes are posted. Homeworks (10 total, 2 drop) are good practice for the exams. Midterm and Final are curved for fairness for those unable to attend midterm (Final 90%). I would recommend staying on top of the course material as falling behind can easily overwhelm you.

Bhaskar is a smart man which is why it's so easy to get confused when he explains. Watch videos for clarity and DO additional practice problems. There is one midterm worth 40% (avg ~60) and one final worth 50% (avg ~68). I got below average for both exams and got a B so he curves good. DO NOT WAIT LAST MINUTE FOR STUDYING. Keep practicing activley.

The class is very interesting and the problems are fun.... when you are given effective material to work with. Homeworks do not prepare us for exam questions and often take multiple hours to do. I got myself sick once because of how much time it took to do one homework. The material is very interesting, just study as much as you can!

analysis.name: Chandra Bhat
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Bhat is a pretty good professor. His exams are fair, but he underestimates the time it takes to do them which led to a failing class average on the 1st exam. The class only has 2 exams, mid-term is 30%, final is 40% of your grade, homework is 25%, & participation is 5%. He covers how to do the HW well in class and is an understanding prof

He is a great prof! Super nice, cares about students, explains concepts well. However, there is breakdown in grading with the student grader being SUPER harsh and Dr. Bhat did not accept any feedback on that. Material can get confusing, homeworks are easy but the exams are incredibly hard

He really cares about his students. There's are one midterm (30%) and final (40%). He pretty much gave us all the answers to the homework (25%) in class so it is important to attended them all (they are not recorded). He made the exams open notes which helped tremendously. If you understand how to do the homework and you go to class you'll be fine.

Good instructor, worst professor in my life. After class, I asked a calculation question cz I was confused on the concept. He raged because I didn't get the concept. He kept saying "I don't know how you can't get this" over and over. He didn't try to listen to me. I was asking different one first time learning transportation system in my life.

The material itself was super interesting, but Bhat wasn't the best lecturer. His handwriting was sloppy and he went on many different roundabouts that didn't pertain to the content. Any time I contacted him for help on hwk or clarifying grading he would spew off some philosophical nonsense and wouldn't answer my questions

analysis.name: Bjorn Hegelich
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: what he teaches is not on the test
All he does is stand at the front a derive equations. He does not help at all in the way of actually learning the concepts of physics which is what this course is supposed to be about.
Does not use class time effectively. Does not explain the material well. Doesn't even teach whats on the exams.
Definitely the least caring professor at UT. The averages on the tests are a 55. Good luck my friends.
Does not teach, test are extremely hard

analysis.name: Anna Bjurman-Pautz
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Don't let her casual demeanor lure you into thinking the midterm and final will be simple. Expect to put some effort into understanding the concepts bc they aren't always explained well in class. Students asked questions as if the views she was suggesting were her own. They'd debate her, she wouldn't be able to get on track, and we'd get nowhere.

She follows the slides and explains things pretty well until someone asks a question. Then I stop taking notes until she goes back to talking about the slides because any response to a question seems to make her uncomfortable. She pauses a lot while thinking how to respond. She really is a nice woman and very intelligent, though. I'd say, take her.

Human Nature: The teacher is amazingly lenient and super nice. The problem is that she reads DIRECTLY from her slide shows and the class was at 8 in the morning MWF. Her TA was VERY nice and lenient also. There is a midterm (essay answers) and a final (essay) and there are two Response papers and about 10 in class assignments. Hard to pay attention

She is not an  awful professor by any means but does lack the ability to make the lectures engaging and it's common to even find her looking at the clock. Her pauses  between statements give the appearance that she doesn't even know what she's talking about; but that isn't the case because she does in her own capacity. Paying attention is hard.

It's like Einstein said: "if you can't explain it to a 6 year old, you don't fully understand it". She answers questions in a convoluted, round about way and often mixes up her terminology. The book is no help either; nothing is explained in an introductory way, not in lecture or from the book. HW problems are out of the book so its essential

analysis.name: Clayton Bjorland
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I liked this prof. He was very helpful to students, and worked lots of examples in class. Also, I took this class over the summer, so we were moving pretty fast, but I nevers struggled with his pacing. As mentioned by someone else, he does mess up a lot in examples. This can be annoying, because he writes very fast and taking notes is hard enough.

It might have been the class material was easy (math 408M is suppose to be inbetween 408D and 427L) But when I took his class back in spring I remember it being very easy. His lectures were nice in that he'd work examples in class, he sympathized with students and graded very leniently. I'd recommend this professor and I hope I can take him again

He's a good math professor, willing to work with students, accepts questions immediately and tries very hard to reconcile misunderstandings. Has good lectures, organizes very well. Grades haven't come out yet but for the midterms there appears to be quite generous partial credits awarded, not really any curve though.
Constantly messes up while giving examples. His lectures are boring and the only reason you will get a decent grade is  because everybody else does poorly.
I don't attend class at all. but there's really no need to. Just rework all the homework questions before every exam and you'll get an A!

analysis.name: Oyvind Bjoru
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 36 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Best professor ever. I took his Planet Word course, and it was so good that it almost made me switch my major to Linguistics. Very little work and amazing lectures. There's one midterm essay (which you condense and revise for the final) and a short 4-minute presentation, both easy and fun. Lukas Rudzinski, the TA, was also great and very caring.

I had Professor Oyvind for Planet Word and he was extremely passionate about what he teaches. The class itself is an easy A, there's weekly hw quizzes that take about 3 min max, only one essay, and a short presentation for grades. Attendance is mandatory but the class is a super easy A if you spend even a little time on the assignments.

If you need a language credit TAKE NORWEGIAN!! Prof Øyvind is genuinely one of my favorite professors I have ever had. He is incredibly patient, kind, and empathetic and wants you to succeed. He will work with you if you need help and is understanding and flexible with illness/absences. This class is a gpa BOOSTER and the timing MWF 11-1 is ideal.

Prof Øyvind is the best! If you need a lang credit, take Norwegian! He is so thoughtful & patient and just wants you to have a positive experience. Attendance is mandatory, but he is forgiving about sickness. Exams are online/at-home & there are only a few in class quizzes. It's one of the easiest languages for English speakers.

Oyvind is probably the best professor I've had at UT. He's incredibly understanding and cares about his students, but he's also an amazing lecturer. I didn't care about the noir genre, but understanding all the intricacies now has given me a newfound appreciation. I'm taking Norwegian because I just wanna have him as a professor again.

analysis.name: Luke Bishop
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This Spanish class was time-consuming, but very doable. Doing the homework/online work really helps to understand the grammar and vocabulary. Class was enjoyable because we were able to practice talking and applying what we learn from the workbook. Also, Professor Bishop is very patient and helpful when learning new concepts. Really recommend him!

Awesome prof, super fun and great music taste. 610D is the heaviest homework load in the Spanish sequence, but Prof Luke makes it worth it with great, engaging lectures. He's clearly passionate about Spanish and I definitely recommend taking a class with him!

Awesome professor and taught the content really well. Just a super nice guy as well. He gives great feedback and is very approachable. There's homework every day, but if you do it there's no way you won't do well. I really enjoyed being in the class.

This class, as with the Spanish classes at UT, comes with a lot of outside work due to it being a 6 hour credit! He gives great feedback on homework and as long as you put in the effort you will do well in the course! I recommend making quizlets for vocab and using the chapter reviews in the textbook to study for the exams! Participation is vital!

Although the textbook did awful job at explaining the grammar, Luke was great at helping you understand. If you didn't get it he would rephrase his explanations until one stuck. Very helpful office hours.

analysis.name: Daniel Bisett
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Nice guy w an unfortunate grading policy. His class material is engaging, but competitive nature of the final project makes caring about material>grade difficult. Wants you to read his mind and doesn't go by rubrics well. Said he would curve us down. Also asked for good CES survey scores. If the final wasn't a competition he wouldn't have to ask.

Prof Bisett is definitely passionate about marketing and cares for students. But he has inconsistent grading, curves down, and often doesnt follow his own rubric. Tests are easy but the curve down really messes with your grade. He uses AI for slides and tests which make the class feel less personal and is frustrating imo. Wouldnt take again unforch

While this class is interesting and Professor Bisett clearly knows a lot about marketing, the grading scale of this class is one of the worst at UT. He curves the class down and 30% of your grade is dependent on a group project, where he shows clear favoritism and the grading scale is unclear. He also frequently used AI for slides.

OK professor. Easy quizzes and exam. Complete all possible extra credit because he will try to give you the lowest final grade possible. I ended this class with a 91 and received a B freaking plus as a letter grade.. because of his unfair grading policy. The final presentation policy is a nightmare.

While the lectures can be interesting at times, the grading sucks. He wants his students to compete in order to get a good grade in the class. The final project is worth 30% of the grade, and if you are not a finalist, you can only get an 80%!! He also cleary has favorite students!!

analysis.name: David Birdsong
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I literally love this guy. He is so kind and he is very accessible if you miss a quiz or a test. He is extremely knowledgeable and receives questions well. He also does review sessions and goes over your exam 1:1 with you which is reallllyyy useful. The class itself is straightforward and the exams are just like the review.

Joy of French truly was joyful. He cares about the content he is teaching, and it is fun to learn about French curse words, common sayings, and other aspects of the language that typical classes do not teach you. He is passionate and understanding, so this is the 3rd class I have taken with him because he's simply the best. I highly recommend him!
Took for Power of Words UGS. Such a fun class and insanely easy. Professor does tend to go on random tangents/talk about nothing. Very little work and it is hard not to get an A.

Birdsong is a very enthusiastic & fun teacher- gets you excited about what he's teaching. He was not originally supposed to teach 317C, so he did not create the material and tests. Prepared us well w/ handouts, practice quizzes, & told us where to find the study material. Pretty generous with grading. Attendance points are self grading after class

Great class to really learn about pronunciation. He's engaging and fun. Writing recommendation letters for multiple people in class. Cares about your individual progress. He gives practice tests and quizzes. Homework isn't too bad but to do well you want to do it. I definitely recommend him for any french class.

analysis.name: Bindu Viswanathan
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 63 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I enjoyed this classes material but didn't really feel stimulated by the teaching style. There could have been more done to spice up the lectures but they were totally acceptable- at the level of or better than average. She was kind and seemed to care about her students to some degree but I did not have much personal interaction with her.

Dr. V is the GOAT!!!! She is so amazing and super helpful. Whenever I had trouble, I would go to her OH, and she would guide me through the questions/concepts, making it so much easier to understand. She would also check your HW answers during OH, which helped boost my grade sm, and she rounded our grades up at the end. LOVE HERRRRRRRR

Professor is really great at explaining concepts so go to class & OHs. There is extra credit for going to class. Homeworks can be a little difficult, going to OHs def helps. Exam 1 was the hardest because of counting. Exam 2 and 3 are straight forward. Exam 3 is cumulative. Do practice problems and redo homeworks before exams. Go to OH to check hw.
A really fast paced class. She does not post answers to the homework. She doesnt really help you prepare for the tests. She goes really fast through powerpoints in class.

Dr. V is very sweet, but the class itself is boring. Homeworks are not terrible and going to office hours helps. For exams, Exam 1 is the hardest because it has counting. Just do all the practice problems she gives. You can also see what you get wrong on tests and dispute it if you think you were right. Exam 2 and Final were both straightforward.

analysis.name: Joydeep Biswas
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I liked his lectures and also that he would try to create as much student engagement as possible especially on an online class! Cool dude.

Using very old material like ten years ago. 
AI is allowed in the syllabus, but they will report if using AI.

Decent prof. Class was very group project based, but the material was interesting and as long as you do the work you're guaranteed an A. Biswas is kind of judgey if you don't start the assignments before the (mandatory) Friday lab (even though they're due on Monday). Made me realize I didn't want to work in self-driving cars though lol

analysis.name: Bill Wolesensky
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 240 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Literally the best professor I've ever had. He is genuine, caring, and really wants your success. ALWAYS makes time for students, NEVER makes you feel dumb or inadequate for not understanding something. One of the best guys I know. I wish he were my father.
Best teacher ever. Honestly so nice and extremely helpful. This was one of the easiest classes i've ever taken at UT but was also totally enjoyable. 10/10 would recommend

WantEasyA?-dont take him. Although hard, this has been my favorite class so far and I truly believe this class taught me how to (actually)learn. Bill truly cares about his students,is always open to questions,and inspires us to learn to think critically by truly understanding concepts instead of just memorizing. AmazingProfessor+WorthTheCourseRigor

peak professor, highkey goat. very caring and passionate about student success, empowerment, and understanding. 3 exams each with 2 parts, indiv. (60%) and group (40%). very clear and concise explanations of concepts, and easy to approach. very kind and respectful professor. literally best professor ive taken, genuinely kindhearted.

He prefers to move slow and ensure deep understanding of topics. Made me feel encouraged to learn and ask questions which is a first for me at UT. He did assign a lot of homework but often times would drop off sections as he wouldn't get to lecture that content in class. He empowered me as a student and I put effort into his class.

analysis.name: Joshua Blank
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Blank and Henson's class was not nearly as hard as people make it out to be. If you treat the course like an in-person class, meaning you actually watch the lectures, it'll be fine. The two exams are decently challenging and worth 20% each, but not outrageous. Professor Blank is engaging in lecture videos and has a good sense of humor.

Worst class I've ever taken in my life, the sheer amount of work that this class has is abysmal. There is an insane amount of weekly lectures that range from 15-60+ minutes each PLUS all of the work from the online webtext. The professors provide ZERO methods of studying and often contradict themselves for what information will show up on the test

Decent Teacher, HARD CLASS. Exam format is extremely lop sided (1 exam covers 2 months of material) and questions deviate DRASTICALLY from weekly instructions. Also, video instructions are long and 95% unnecessary, but you need to pay attention since the 5% WILL be tested. Overall, not hard class to pass, but HARD to get an A in.

The weekly reading has about 200 comprehension questions + 7-10 lectures a week. It's annoying, and professors aren't helpful, telling you to study everything. Exams are Honorlock and have frequent typos and formatting issues. Might need a thesaurus to understand test questions. only 2 exams worth 40% of grade

This class is not as bad as people are making it out to be but you do need to actually watch the lectures! Lectures will be more helpful over the readings and the readings can be done in abt 15 minutes. Not a class you can breeze through but definitely do able to get an A

analysis.name: Blair Johnson
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Johnson is great at explaining difficult concepts and often presents simpler, clearer methods. Homework is time-consuming and challenging, so be prepared. Exams are structured differently but not bad. Many extra credit opportunities. IMO one of the better fluids professors at UT, would definitely take again. Shoutout TA Alex for being awesome

Anyone who dislikes Prof J just hates when professors expect their students to learn. She is a good teacher, and the class is manageable. It is easy to succeed in her class if you participate in lectures, go to office hours, do the homework etc. Only gripe is all homework assignments were group work which I hated, but overall, I really liked her.

The only way you can do good is by attending office hours where you can receive further info the rest of the class is unaware of. She was not prepared a lot of the time and taught straight from her notes, often making mistakes and not correcting them until the next lecture. Not recommended if not passionate about fluids, as she expects you to be.

Honestly she's my fav prof I've ever taken. I'm not really an outgoing person but she makes sure to get to know her students well and make them feel comfortable. It sounds silly but I was really touched that she remembered my name(which she pronounced properly) and face after I introduced myself once. You can tell she really cares which is nice.

She preaches about mental health but denied our group an extension when we were overloaded. She uploads assignments as announcements (rather than in files), and many of the time are uploaded as word docs instead of pdf. She assigns groups where you have to give a presentation over a scientist and work on weekly homework with that same group.

analysis.name: Cheasequah Blevins
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She essentially reads off the slides, but the course itself is not difficult. You can teach yourself what she skips over. She is friendly and it is better to ask questions in office hours. Grading is nitpicky for minor lab and homework mistakes, points off add up over time. She also gives extra credit for coming to class, that helps.

Nice lady, but this course is heavy for an introductory statistics class. A lot of people thought this class was a breeze because they took AP Stats in high school but if you didn't take it, it's not a walk in the park. Blevins definitely has good material and resources but the quizzes are a lot harder than what she teaches

Super sweet professor, loves giving feedback and regrades, but emails vanish into the void and lectures were insanely long. You can easily self-teach, she posts annotated slides and lets you use cheat sheets. Extra credit is HUGE but only offered if you show up.

Love this professor! She is very clear about what she expects. Your grade is made up of a lot of different things, so exams aren't super stressful. The homework is very tedious though sometimes. Overall, I definitely recommend this course!

Dr. Blevins is a great professor, and she cares about her students. Her lectures are clear and straightforward without being dry. You don't get a lot of time for quizzes, but they aren't too difficult. TAs grade strictly on homework and it's not always apparent what they want you to include. Overall, not a difficult course. Some extra credit given.

analysis.name: Kirk Blazek
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 220 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Wow. What an eye opening experience to the savagery and absolute bonkers max-tier class the Dr. Blazek has created. The homeworks are redundant, tedious, and mind-numbingly difficult. And the tests are really, really hard. Lectures are scrambled up so that even Einstein couldn't figure out what is going on! Pls don't take :(. Save your soul.

Worst professor I have had. Be prepared for lots of homework. He does not show basic respect to any students. When asking questions in class, he gives off an impertinent attitude, answering in a sarcastic and condescending tone. Expect to learn everything by yourself; his notes are illegible, and he barely records his lectures.
very awful professor. doesn't clearly explain concepts and the homework is incredibly redundant and tedious, do not take

Tests do not line up with what he teaches, and he goes SO fast in lectures that it is impossible to follow. Notes are not even helpful because there is no structure to the class. Curses every two seconds. Not sure how he is still a professor at UT with how unprofessional he is.

Blazek has revamped the ECE M340L section to make it incredibly difficult, tedious and not easy to understand. Beware of taking the class as it is not as easy as other sections. Very unfortunate to experience... I cannot emphasize enough how bad my experience has been.

analysis.name: Lauren Blondeau
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 80 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Blondeau breaks statistics down really well. She has plenty of resources for your success in this course. Her class is graded by quizzes (where you can have a 1 page cheat sheet), homework, labs, and a major project that isn't too difficult! She is pretty flexible and understanding and responds to emails pretty quickly too!

The most understanding professor ever. I slept in for the final quiz and told her the truth, and she let me take it during office hours on Zoom. The quizzes are very easy (7-8 questions per quiz, 4 in total). The final project is split into parts where you're given a template to fill out, so you're not lost. She is an angel and a GPA savior

This class is very easy if you've taken AP Statistics in high school. Overall, the material is boring, but Professor Blondeau does a good job organizing the course. The workload is very light, though you should be cautious with quizzes. Even though you're allowed a page of notes, they are graded strictly. Overall, it's a decent class.

There is only 4 quizzes and 1 major project. The reviews she gives are very different from the actual quiz questions. She does allow a page of notes for each quiz, but it's not very helpful. Attendance is not mandatory, but you are graded on Instapolls during class. Try not to fall behind at all and do show up to every lab meeting.

Blondeau is a decent professor, and the project was easy to get a full score on. However, I could not manage to do well on a single quiz this year because of how difficult they were and it sunk my grade because they were weighted heavily. Also the TA was very strict on grading. Lectures were helpful in studying.

analysis.name: Blanca Ramierz
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Don't take this class with her period. TA's were rude & inconsiderate, while the professor read off of a script without expanding on the topics/terms. I didn't learn anything from the lectures since she didn't give time to note anything and didn't post the slides. Attendance via instapolls was the worst

If i can deter you from doing anything during your time at UT it is having this woman as your professor. She takes an intro class way too seriously and has a terrible structure. I have never rated a professor before but something had to be said. She cares more about stopping you from cheating than helping you learn.

The structure of this course is terrible. The professor does not post the slides and gets upset if you try to take pictures of them if you can't write fast enough. Most of the learning will be done through the reading since the lectures are all over the place. The one thing I like about this course is the fact that the textbook is free.

Horrible teacher. She read from a script and did not know her slides at all, Guest lecturers were better than her. Didn't post slides and no extra credit. Cutoff for an A was a 94. She doesn't want you to do well. Exams aren't hard. Papers are graded by TAs, so they decide your grade. I didn't learn anything it was about the level of a hs class.

Professor Ramirez was a great teacher. Her class was very engaging, with interesting topics, and was definitely one of my favorite classes. Although there were few assignments, as long as you studied, you would do great. My TA was also great and very helpful during office hours. Highly recommend this class!

analysis.name: Clarice Blanco
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Excellent professor. She really cares for her students and she really wants to see you improve. Your grade is mostly essays, and she gives a lot of great and helpful feedback as well as having one-on-one sessions for in-depth feedback. I personally don't like writing or anything of that sort, yet this was my favorite class. I would 100% recommend.

Really great profe. She really cares about the students and ensuring that we got the best grade possible. Attendance isn't required but if you attend the classes she unlocks assignments and closes them during that duration.

Her class was essay heavy. But she was really nice about grades. Lets you make them up to a 100!! Take her class!

Genuinely one of the most interesting courses I've taken at UT. Rhetoric of Borders was not only fascinating to learn about but also to write about! This class actually inspired me to become a rhetoric minor:)

Professor Blanco was my favorite teacher this semester! She worked with students one-on-one to help meet our individual needs on our writing assignments and truly cared about each of us. She is the realest professor and I'd recommend her to anyone and everyone who needs to take their rhetoric 306 credit. The best!

analysis.name: Mary E. Blockley
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently

Dr. Booth is very thoughtful and organized. She explains concepts clearly and brings real industry insight into the class. She also regularly asks for and implements student feedback.

Prof Booth's passion for research & teaching is clear in the way she leads lectures & structures the class. Professor Booth is great! Compared to other professors in the iSchool, she is one of the stronger public speakers and consistently comes to class well prepared, she puts thought into each class. TA's are lenient graders and sometimes I would be too lazy to do the full assignment and still get a 100. This is the easiest class I have ever taken in my life.

Such an easy class. I never read the books, or showed up to class and still got an A. As long as you do the canvas assignments online you'll be fine. The book quizzes were one question, no lockdown browser on anything. The only class you wanna pu to is the discussion. Every assignment is so easy. No tests. Highly recommend.

Dr. Bowers was great! I would definitely recommend taking this class with him if you need it. in Spring '25 paper exams were absurdly hard also no curve after avg 58. Exams had such a wild range of topics and the class did jack shit to prepare you for it. He's so kind and adorable!  He gave group quizzes and got rid of Perusalls.  When I emailed him about any slight issue, he gave me a take-home quiz or another way to open Lockdown. analysis.name: Daniel Bonevac

review_highlights.comment: Not too sure why everyone is raving this UGS. The assignments are easy yes, but the TA's grade so harsh for things with no rubric. He's nice but it's a no.

He is a very good lecturer. There are a lot of assignments based on readings, but as long as you do them, you should be fine. Overall, if you put effort into this class, it's not bad at all.

Outstanding lectures, he is genuinely skilled in that regard. Attendance is not mandatory but you will want to attend, every class is like watching a well-produced documentary. analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: They are such an amazing professor! Super kind and welcoming. They provide super insightful lectures as well. Genuinely learned so much but in a fun and interactive way. Would 100% take again. There are exams and a good amount of writing assignments but they're pretty simple! Attendance is not required 100% of the time, but often.

Cizsek is the sweetest; you can tell they care about their students and teaching the material. This class wasn't difficult at all either. Def don't hesitate to take this class if Cizsek is still the professor!

Although I ended with a C (totally on me because I completely missed a quiz), Professor Cizsek had such great lectures that really helped with understanding the field of advertising and it was a really easy class

Love love loved this class. Super easy with fun lectures and collaborative discussions. Dr.Cizek is clearly passionate about their profession and does their best to ensure their students are being educated about important current issues. Lots of extra credit and exams were stress free with no final
MY FAVORITE TEACHER AT UT!!!! Genuinely cares about her students and the material. Great and engaging lecture! Take her class, you will not regret it!!! Loved every minute of her lectures!

analysis.name: Cindy McCreery
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I promise you need to take this class! It's so fun and interesting! She's very helpful with all your work and always open for questions. She cares so much about all her students and if you just do your work which is pretty easy you will get an A. It's literally impossible to not unless you just don't do the work!

Ask questions anytime Cindy is super chill and is always available and gets back to you, I've never had a teacher/professor care this much about their students :) the work is super easy and fun and it really helped me for my future of wanting to be a writer especially TV writing if that interests you!
This is a great class if you love to write and be creative! This class 100% made me a better writer! Cindy is the NICEST women you will ever meet.
Although there's a lot of participation I feel like this class really created a community for RTF majors and I'm thankful for this class:)

Cindy is a very nice person but there were many things that made the class frustrating. The class was disorganized and assignments could be confusing at times. I felt I was teaching myself most of the time and had to learn how to do something in the span of a week. Also, we don't know what our grades are two weeks before the end of the semester.

analysis.name: Mirela Ciperiani
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Condescending professor. She was/is a mathematical prodigy without humbleness and this didn't translate to excellent teaching. HARSH grader on exams but HW's are always full credit with little feedback. I walked out of the class with a 100 on the final, an A, and a lot of resentment for making algebra not fun. Just save yourself and take Keel.

Lectures are unbelievably dry and suck the life out of the subject that is group theory. Pretty much follows the definition->theorem->proof cycle you would find in any old textbook, except in lecture form. Provides essentially 0 intuition and is pretty much all about deduction and symbolic manipulation. Exam problems sampled from homeworks.

The HW is the exam with the caveat that she expects you to be perfect on the exams. Most of your grade comes from exams but she replaces one and also 2 out of the 11 HWs. Presentations of HW are a big part of this class so expect to present math. She is a phenomenal professor if you expect to take algebraic structures 2 with Sean.

Not the worst but also not great. The homeworks were long and while the tests were based on them, she chooses the hardest/trickiest problems from each assignment, and it feels like there's not enough time to finish the exams. She's not a great lecturer; I just read the textbook or watched YT videos since I got nothing from her lectures.

Super knowledgeable & gives you everything you need to do well. Homework is difficult but exams are pulled from the homework so it's clear what you need to know for exams & exams are easy as a result. Lectures are really informative without being overly dense. Overall a really solid choice for number theory.

analysis.name: Cinzia Russi
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Awful professor. She's hysterical and confusing. Makes a fairly easy subject matter very difficult to understand. She also giggles when she gives you bad grades. I would never recommend her to anyone.

Textbook readings can be long. Quizzes were either very easy or very hard. You don't learn much Italian in the course; it's a regular course taught in 70% Italian. Very open to working with the class on what material is difficult and changing the course structure during the semester. Friendly professor, encourages participation.
Lang Truths, Myths, Mysteries was a very interesting class! We covered many different topics and had fun working together in class. Take this class for upper div LAH!

I actually took LAH 352E, Language Myths, Mysteries, and Truths. Great class. Work was straightforward. Class was mostly relaxed group discussion. Dr. Russi was great! Easy grader and class was really interesting. She was really funny and nice!
Very nice, knowledgeable and helpful. Not sure why some other students are whining. I had zero problems with her.

analysis.name: Jessica Ciarla
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Great Professor!! Very Knowledgable!  Very fair, if something is unclear she does not penalize you for it. It's nice to hear about her personal experience in the fashion industry as she is very credible having years of experience in New York and owning her bridal shop in Austin. Makes class interesting with relevant fashion clips from youtube.

She understood you're new to the software and will give critiques and guidance if you ask. She doesn't bite. Grades pretty easily just do the work. Class takes a lot of time outside of hybrid meetings.

Very straight-forward classes. Lectures are usually always the same - her giving a powerpoint presentation, with some relevant video clips every few slides. It gets a little boring but she gives you everything you need for the test. VERY friendly and answers all questions. The only thing I didn't like was that class got repetitive.

One of the worst lecturers I have had at UT, un-engaging. Copies her powerpoint slides from the book and read them to us while standing in the same place. Assigns 5 point assignments in class which are a total waste of time. Constantly asks the class inane questions of obvious definitions.

analysis.name: Circe Sturm
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 64 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Sturm is clearly knowledgeable in her subject. But, she needs to explain things slower and more interestingly, keeping in mind that it's an online class and people can't reach her as easily. She tries to keep people in the loop by engaging in group chats and instapolls. The quizzes are easy.

This is a great course. Dr. Sturm is very organized, and the TAs are helpful. You'll need to study for the three midterms, and there's a project too. Keep up with Instapolls, and you can easily earn an A. The only reason I didn't earn an A is because of the midterms, so watch out!

Professor Sturm is really nice and takes the time to explain vague concepts thoroughly which shows how genuinely interested she is in her field of work. There isn't too much work in the class right now and you basically only have to keep up with readings. Tests are manageable, but not as easy as you'd expect them to be. All multiple choice tests.

Lectures are boring --- she just talks in circles and TA's are pretty bad (lacking basic canvas skills). Class is easy, all online prerecorded lectures with occasional instapolls. One project with a 2 page paper. There is extra credit opportunities (~2 points on final grade). Overall --- good class if you just need the credit and an easy A.

Dr. Strum talks in circles, her lectures tend to be boring and not coherent. They also used recycled lecture segments from a previous semester which was frankly negligent. This class is very content heavy, so only take it if you absolutely need it. One of her textbooks is completely irrelevant to the content of the class, which was vexing.

analysis.name: Cameron  Cler
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She had mediocre lectures and loved explaining random Chinese things wrong. Doesn't grade until finals week even though class ends in like October, and even then the grading feels arbitrary. Never gave out a single 100 on an assignment, mostly gives 85s-90s. Attendance is a grade, even if you have an exam that falls during class hours. Mid.

Loved this professor! Even though the class was late in the day, it always flew by because she made the material so engaging. The assignments were straightforward and manageable, and I still walked away learning so much valuable information. Would definitely recommend taking this class with her if you get the chance!

I took Cameron for MKT 174 and she is such an amazing lecturer. She's one of the nicest people I've met at UT, so if you need a 1 hour course take this one!! participation is crucial to passing, but she tries to make each class enjoyable! Loved her!
Very good professor. Explains everything very well, would recommend the class. Also provides very good feedback.

analysis.name: John Clarke
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data
