review_highlights.comment: An utterly unpleasant man.  He has no quealms about treating you as though you don't deserve to be in the art history program.  So dictatorial that you wind up not being inspired enough to take anything away from what would otherwise be a compelling and useful class.

I enjoyed the subject matter and was very excited to give my own interpretation guided by the textbooks and readings. Unfortunately Clarke is the kind of professor who prefers that you regurgitate back to him exactly what he has written in his own books and anything that strays from that is considered highly subjective and wrong.

Professor John Clarke teaches a performance work in his Modern American Art course that contains sexual assault, and he presented it without warning. When I emailed him that I was triggered by this piece, he asked me to tell him in person why it was triggering for me. I declined, and he put the piece on our midterm.

If you're taking this for a VAPA or upper division elective, do something else. He is rude and condescending, and makes little to no accommodations for ANY situation. His sensitive lecture topics (sex, gender, etc) were talked about as if they were a joke. If we didn't remember a specific thing from the reading he'd get angry and say we don't try.

Clarke is such a sweet guy! Not the most tech savvy. Clear lectures that go right along with the exams. Exams aren't hard at all, just need to watch the lectures and memorize the pieces. I never did the readings and got 96+ on all exams. Also some small writing assignments, but they're easy 100s. Go to class to succeed. Would love to take again.

analysis.name: Alexandra Clark
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I loved Dr. Clark's lecturing style and I can say that I learned quite a lot from her! I love that she is passionate about what she teaches and stands for what she believes in. However, I will say that the 3 exams are quite tricky, as they are long free responses. There is a lot of content discussed and no study guide/vague ideas of what to expect.

Dr. Clark is very condescending - when people ask questions in class she acts frustrated and as if the answer should be the most obvious thing in the world. I went to office hours once (Friday 8 AM only) to go over a test and ask for advice and she complained that students "just want to be spoon fed". The TAs were much more helpful.

The 3 exams that make up the majority of your grade require lots of studying, but are doable. She may seem intimidating, but is incredibly engaging and refreshingly honest about her views on what's happening in the US right now in relation to the course content. I learned so much and highly recommend her as a professor.

Dr. Clark's class is very informative. I learned so much about dementia and Alzheimer's. The lectures can be science heavy but she does a great job of explaining it so you shouldn't feel lost. There are 4 free response quizzes that can be a bit tricky so make sure to study ahead. But as long as you put in the work it's totally doable.

I enjoyed Professor Clark's class and learned a lot, and she can answer any question. She does present a lot of information but the way she lectures makes it easier to remember. Quizzes are doable if you keep up with lecture material.

analysis.name: Kevin Clarno
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Clarno is a groovy guy. He is very knowledgeable about what he teaches. Concerning the class, if this is your first class on nuclear, it might be rough as there is a learning curve. Exams also are difficult but are graded on a curve so there is less pressure. Reason I am giving a four is because the class was too disorganized. Very swag beard.
Great guy, great class. Study with the slides... Tests are a challenge, but meant to stretch you

analysis.name: Gregory Clark
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I highly recommend taking this course for the UGS requirement. Dr. Clark is super cool and into what he is teaching. The course has some reading reflections, three essays, a group presentation, and an individual presentation. It is very interesting to learn about different plants and what they do. Compared to other UGS's this one is much better.

Dr. Clark is so chill and very understanding! He truly helps every student succeed in his lab, and he doesn't force anybody to do too much work each week! However, the partner system during first semester can get a little frustrating if you're stuck with a bad one, and he doesn't really use canvas, so it is hard to determine your grade!

Awesome professor. So nice and understanding, easy to talk to, cares about your learning while also making sure not to stress you out. His FRI stream is great and provides a great exposure to the basics of research.

Dr. Clark was absolutely amazing! His Hidden Treasures of Plants UGS was really eye-opening and a great learning experience. Discussions were very chill and essay assignments were not too much of a challenge. Dr. Clark was super understanding and spent time learning about his students. I enjoyed his class and learned a lot!

Dr. Clark is THE BEST! Such a sweet guy and is extremely passionate about his research! His lab is interesting but pretty laid back! Not work heavy and he's so forgiving and approachable! LOVE DR.CLARK AND HIS LAB!!!

analysis.name: Corinne Jones
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Honestly, what kind of professor does not post their lecture recordings for such a lecture heavy class. We already have 10 polls per class, which questions are only shown in class. She also does not really lecture and just reads from slides, which questions her credibility as a professor. Seems like she cares more ab attendance and not teaching.

Never read the textbook and still ended up with 100 in the class. However, I did not truly learn anything from this class, except the information that I already knew about speech, as a SLH major. She taught very quickly with little to no additional explanation even when asked, but compensates by giving extra credit opportunities.

This class was so hard to keep up with, I feel like it was heavily catered to neuro students. Although attendance isn't mandatory, you have to go or you'll be totally lost. There's few grades and the 2 tests were so hard. Heavy material and no study guides for the tests.

Truly shocked by how little I learned in this class considering I studied weeks for the tests. She would lecture over a million things and then she would test you on the most useless things in the hundreds of slides. Expect to study for hours and still know nothing on the test.

Exams are pretty tough, but you get a cheat sheet. One exam got curved. Content is interesting. Lots of it, but cheat sheets on exam really help. Dr. Jones is not always responsive. Takes days to respond to email but usually helpful.

analysis.name: Desmond Coles
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Chill guy, good teacher. Hw typically takes anywhere between 0.5-3 hrs per week, don't procrastinate. Show up to lectures even if you took AP, b/c theres content not taught in AP thats taught here.(I'm not talking about multivariable). 65% of your grade comes from the exams. Feel free to ask questions, although he can ramble on a bit when answering

My favorite professor during Fall '25. He really knows his subject and can teach it well. He answers questions thoughtfully and explains concepts thoroughly (how particular formulas are derived) so that we understand better. Gave useful homework problems, practice exams, straightforward quizzes/exams, and had a bonus question on exams. 10/10 prof.

Amazing Calc Professor. Homework and quizzes are similar to tests. Tests aren't hard if you truly know the material. Lectures move fast but are insightful. He knows SO much about the field and is genuinely interested. 65% of grade based on tests. Quizzes in discussion. DO THE HOMEWORK! He really emphasizes it for good reason. Amazing professor!

Desmond Coles is an excellent professor with lots of knowledge about his course. It's not absolutely necessary to read the textbook before the lecture, because he will explain EVERYTHING in the lecture. 
However, it is crucial to not skip classes. Also just a chill guy, he's always wearing hats.

TLDR: don't skip class, do half the homework before

Tests are similar to the hw, albeit a little bit longer and more difficult. He was a great lecturer as well, and  even though I find calc 2 to be incredibly boring, he did an awesome job of teaching it. The multivar section was the highlight of the class, so if you're scared of calc 3, take him! He's great at explaining calc in 3D.

analysis.name: Caryn Conley
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Worst class I've ever taken. It was immensely difficult, and each weekly homework assignment increases in scope and complexity. By the end of the semester, it was taking me 10+ hours per homework (she seems to think it's funny, too). Tests aren't any easier, and the examples in class are elementary compared to what you are asked to learn yourself.

Worst professor I've ever had. She doesn't know Python. Every week you have homework and because it's so difficult you have to start the day it gets assigned otherwise you wont finish. Her lectures don't help because they're very simplistic when compared to her assignments. It's like having a project every week. Reading the book helps a bit.

UT fired Dantu because he was bad at teaching, and they brought in someone worse. Conley is a poor hire who needs to be fired ASAP. She is horrible at teaching, awkward at interacting, and incredibly unhelpful at answering questions. Tests were insanely hard, while examples were elementary in class, and appeals were not  accepted.

Dr. Conley seems nice, but she is not a very interesting or inspiring professor at all. The average class day in MIS 304 consists of Dr. Conley reading a 10-20 slide PowerPoint as lecture, and giving one or two in-class practice problems at the end of class. Expect to devote 10-12h/week on homework assignments. Wish I chosen a different professor..

McCombs is a coveted institution with amazing professors. The best professors I've had lived prosperous careers with meaningful work. This lady is nothing of the sort. The lectures are boring and she teaches concepts she hasn't applied. She lacks real-world insight and speaks like an elementary teacher, making for a crude, uninspiring experience.

analysis.name: Thomas Connolly
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 54 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Beware of trolls rating this professor; he is not that great. For a Dynamics Physics course, a 95 and above is an A! (For reference, his test average was a 68, and no curve was given). In other words, it's extremely difficult to earn an A in the class. A 90 is a B+! He doesn't even teach well and will not post any notes (so you're on your own).

If you have ADHD prepare to self teach. All he does for lecture is give in class exercises with minimal instruction, let us work on it, then explain the solution. Least engaging lecture I've ever had. Tests (2 mid 1 final) are 25% each, no curve, took over a month to return 1st midterm. +1 to the other recent reviews; don't trust the positive ones

His lecturing style is one of the worst out there. He does not explain things well & relies on his students learning from "in-class exercises." The TAs were also so unhelpful. Most questions were answered as "I don't know, to be honest." The exams were nothing like what we had during quizzes, and they were super late at 8-10 pm on Thursday nights.

Difficult but caring professor. He is very sweet but I found it hard to take what I learnt in the lecture to an exam. I often had to look for other practice problems apart from his own to feel prepared. His extra credit is ~1 % added to your final grade (5 pts bonus for course evals) so dont be counting on it for anything.

95 for an A. The 'curve' you get is 4-8 bonus points added to your lowest exam (which all weigh the same) meaning a 1-2% grade boost. Kind Professor, but avoid. Stopped uploading solutions to his work after a few weeks in. Never have felt so unprepared going into exams, which the worst is NOT dropped despite the 95+ for an A. Non-cumulative final.

analysis.name: Renita Coleman
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 48 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor is very familiar and passionate about the subject, which makes lessons interesting. The exams make up 60%, but most questions are common sense aside from some hyper-specific examples, which test reviews from professor and TA's mention. Not an extremely easy UGS and had to spend hours studying/doing homework. TA's grade the 6 essays hard.

This class was really easy, most of your grade comes from 3 tests that were all super easy if you went to the discussion test reviews. There were also six one page papers throughout the semester, but were honestly all fun to write (also two got dropped so you only have to do 4). The lectures were probably fun if you are interested in pop culture

Part I. First of all, I hated this class. As a pop culture enthusiast who was raised into this field and developed my identity though it, the curriculum satisfied me and accurately portrayed every single pop culture event which filled me with nostalgia but boredom. Professor Coleman is well-spoken but often stutters and loses her train of thought.

Absolutely loved Dr. Coleman! She's very passionate and funny. This class is very interesting and in my opinion pretty chill. Class is TA heavy, and your grade depends heavily on your TA. Shout out to my TA Carlos Byrd! He was the best, and made me enjoy the class and subject more. Would 100% take again.

Coleman tries her best to set you up for success - she gives you all the materials you need to do well. Who your TA is matters alot - they are the ones giving you reviews before the tests and grading your discussion papers. There are definitely other better UGS courses than this one - don't make this your first choice.

analysis.name: Jason Cons
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Cons is a great professor! He is a nice guy and really wants his students to do well. That being said, he does require a lot of papers so be prepared for some intensive writing. There is a lot of (sometimes very nuanced and thick) reading involved, but he always explains them perfectly in lecture. He is one of the best professors I've had!

His environmental anthropology class was extremely interesting for someone with no knowledge prior to this class. He is very nice and encourages engagement with the class. You must read and understand concepts, as you will have to write about them for your midterm. The final is a fun group project! Mainly graded by TAs

This class is the intersection of environmental science and philosophy. Dr. Cons presents logical and insightful ideas about how to think critically about environmental ideologies. The class itself is very manageable, and will be beneficial it you attend lectures and discussion sections. Grading is TA dependent though, so good luck.

Dr. Cons was a wonderful lecturer and prof! The grade for the class was based on attendance, a midterm, a final group project, and short writing assignments. The class itself was very very interesting and I learned a lot that I never would have known had I not taken the class. Take this class!
Literally the best professor I've ever had. Fascinating lectures, caring guy, and super funny.

analysis.name: Olivier Coibion
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: One of the most interesting upper econ classes! 3 exams, nothing else. The 1st 2 are optional with the final being the full weight (30 30 40 if you take all). As he explains, taking all 3 essentially passes you as about 40% of the class will opt to only take the final and of those about 15% will be the failing cohort. Can be stressful as 100% exams

GREAT professor and great guy overall. The whole class is 3 exams. The content is challenging at times, but as long as you pay attention, take notes, and understand the practice exams, you will do fine. The curve was significant, but it's based on class performance. Take all three exams even if you are not confident!! It will help you statistically

only graded by two midterms and a final. the content in the class is really dense, like i felt like i was learning so much just for one midterm. professor is cool, he knows his stuff but yaps a lot and we only got through like 75% of the content for the year. i think the best option for macro theory
His lectures are decent, and he doesn't assign homework for practice. However, the practice exams are extremely useful. The exams are challenging. All grades are based solely on exam performance.

Good professor and class is manageable if you stay on top of things. Class is graded entirely on two midterms (30% each) and a final (40%). The catch is that if you chose to skip a midterm, the weight of that midterm gets shifted to the final. If you're a good test taker, then definately take this class and lecture attendance is not mandatory.

analysis.name: Clint Tuttle
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 190 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Have you ever watched a Kia or Hyundai commercial and think to yourself "Oh Wow amazing car!" Then after owning it for a few weeks realize a few things? Let me save you some time. Really, would not take again.
Brilliant Entertaining lectures. Horrible, infuriating assignments. 5-mile treadmill-boring articles.

HANDS DOWN one of the best professors at UT. The readings aren't that bad as some make it out to be. Tuttle has a panache for story telling and keeps lectures fresh and exciting. He teaches applications of excel and makes the material easy to understand and keeps you interested. I definitely left Tuttle's class feeling prepared for the real world.

Great guy 10/10. If you get the chance to take professor Tuttle you definitely should! He wants his students to do well. Seriously, he is very fair and helpful with all the material. He knows some students might struggle with excel but trust me when I say he knows you'll use it in the future. You will! Fun class and this is one class you'll want!

Clint Tuttle is a UT LEGEND!!! This guy is freaking awesome and if you don't take him, you're missing out on one of the best classes UT has to offer. You'll hear fantastic stories during class and his presentations is something all professors should learn from. He prepares you for the real world with excel. HW isn't bad and its doable. TAKE HIM!

analysis.name: Cary Cordova
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 52 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Do the disco a 1.5 weeks before its due or you're really going to suffer. Just suck it up and DO IT! Lectures are good and the textbook/reader is only "buffer" info. Exams have a long list of keywords but you'll get at least one from each "unit." The readings helped bc they were used on the exams.

Not a big fan of this class at all. The biweekly readings were incredibly long and every major assignment is written. The TA's and Cordova are very vague in their feedback and make it difficult to get an A. I wouldn't take this class unless you have incredibly strong writing skills.

Got stuck in this class from my FIG and regretted it within the first week. There's so much reading you have to do for every class and the lectures are really boring. I changed the class to pass/fail halfway through the semester. Don't take this class unless you love history. And your grade is highly dependent on how your TA grades.

If you want to have ultra liberal ideology shoved down your throat, then take this class. The TA's will disagree with you on anything that does not fit with their agenda. Your grade will suffer for speaking up.
Although the class is pretty interesting, the TAs do grade very harshly.

analysis.name: Conrad Fjetland
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 137 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Going to lecture is actually not mandatory. Obvi going to lab is, but if you miss it you will be able to make it up. It's way easier to get the grade you want than he makes it seem tbh it's obvious he just wants ppl to work hard.
Requires time but it's not at all as bad as people make it out to be. The labs themselves are actually fun unlike the other lab courses at UT

Your D2D experience comes down to your TA, mine was very nice. Professor gets a poor rating due to what seems like him purposely trying to make the lab hard. TAs are FORCED to grade harshly due to prof. Nitpicky quizzes, and enforcement of harsher grading by prof when averages are too high. Lab material not hard, artificially made difficult by prof

This guy is terrible. Why are multiple lab reports assigned and due in the same week? Why does he arbitrarily decide grade cutoffs based on your lab section? Why are his quizzes over nothing important and relevant? Worst class at UT by far.

this is a terribly designed class and CNS needs to reevaluate this lab. There's a reason why students are trying to push it to senior year because of how incredibly difficult this class is 

DO BETTER

analysis.name: Michelle Crabtree
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Michelle was great for an entry-level class. I had her 4-6 pm, and for being such a late and long class, she kept us actively engaged. She taught us a lot of dialectical differences and has a lot of experience teaching languages. I struggle a lot in school and she helped me feel more confident.

Prof Crabtree does very well at managing her personal life with her graduate studies and the classes she teaches! She goes above and beyond teaching wise and offers some immersion experiences (ie brought gazpacho to class)! I hate the Spanish dept at UT, but she made this class more than tolerable and goes the extra mile to make up for its faults.

Michelle cares for her students and goes above and beyond to ensure everyone is understanding the content. She answers questions without condescension and enthusiastically. If you have never taken Spanish before, the content will be difficult with any professor, but I wholeheartedly recommend Michelle.

analysis.name: Kelley Crews
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 50 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: do NOT take this class. the assignments are super easy but they are graded incredibly hard by the professor and the TAs. The professor is super judgemental and tries to justify the horrible grades for the easy assignments and also does not have neutral political views, which even if you agree with you still get a bad vibe about her attitude.

This class really just frustrates me. Never give a rubric for our quizzes and don't really know what to expect for them. TAs and professor is really unclear and claim for it to be super easy but the tests get really specific things gone over in lecture.

This class was an EXTREMELY easy A. You just have to show up for the super random attendance checks and write one essay a week (500 words) which is graded so easily I would write the morning they were due and get a 100. However, Dr. Crews is very zany and scatterbrained. She goes off on massive tangents and class can be exhausting to sit through.

The class as a whole was the easiest thing ever. You have to go to class for the random attendance checks and the only other grades are weekly 500 word essays that take like 10 minutes to write. Overall, super easy A. However, I hated Professor Crews with a passion. She is condescending and impresses her beliefs upon students which IS NOT okay.

she missed 2 weeks which made the course very unorganized. your grade literally depends on your TA's grading and its very inconsistent. you never get feedback so you never know what you did wrong. quizzes(4) were short confusing. she dropped the lowest quiz for us but honestly take another class. it wasnt worth it. we watched like 10 movies overall

analysis.name: Megan Crowhurst
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This prof isn't the worst but complicated. At first she is nice, but then I realized she uses rhetorical devices to single out people she didn't like. It made it tough to learn anything, trying to constantly sift through her maze of points to figure out what was important or not. Her grading reflects a corporate agenda not correctness. I'd avoid.

She really knew her stuff about everything that she taught, didn't use notes at all. Super interested in the topic, and had a clear and effective learning plan for the class. It was definitely worth the time.

This class is not that hard but is still harder than most other UGS classes. I don't think it's worth it to take this class. Dr. Crowhurst is nice but unclear with her grading scale and lectures are interesting at times (and on zoom) but not enough to outweigh the negatives. If you end up taking the class, make sure you talk in class to get an A.

This class was pretty interesting, Dr. Crowhurst is really passionate about what she is teaching. You do have a term paper and a group presentation, but they aren't really all that bad, you do have a lot of time for them. Overall this class wasn't all that difficult.
She's pretty nice, but honestly, I was bored in the lectures. It's kind of a tedious course, but the material is fairly easy to master. Homework was imo much harder than tests.

analysis.name: Alison Craig
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: funny and overall sweet professor but can be disorganized at times. that issue sort of goes away once you enter the simulation. TAs can be nitpicky with grading but that is usually offset by EC points offered during the simulation; go for a leadership position!

Dr Craig is a GEM. The mock senate simulation may seem daunting but it is actually easy to earn participation points. I had a health crisis and she was very understanding and worked out a way for me to get more credit to make up for what I missed. Okay so she may not be the most organized person lol but she's so funny and fantastic. Take her class!

Lectures first half of semester and then attendance matters for second half (the simulation). Lectures are common sense, and she just rambles, so not really necessary to show up. Simulation is fun and attendance goes toward your participation grade for these days. Extra credit offered. If you don't end this class with an A+, that's your fault.

Dr. Craig is awesome! Her class is taught as a senate simulation, but she takes from her immense knowledge to support students in the class. There are 6 total assignments, one of which is an exam that's based on her lectures - which are funny and helpful. You'll want to attend class, especially in the simulation, but the classes are lots of fun!

Took US Congress with Prof. Craig. Class is largely based off of a senate simulation, where participation is important. She gives lectures that are funny but also can seem somewhat unorganized. There are 6 assignments including 1 exam, all of which are easy to do well on if you pay attention in class. Overall a fun and easy class and professor.

analysis.name: Cristine Legare
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 37 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: The lectures are an open discussion with the class; there are no lecture slides. The lectures did not have relevance to the exam, we had to learn everything on our own. There are a total of 6 essay exams and a final essay exam all in person without notes. There would randomly be group projects that were not on the syllabus. Class was not organized.

There are 6 exams 3-4 questions each: 1 pg essay per. Questions release 2-3 days before. Exam time was shortened from 90 to 75 mins 
This class killed any interest in the subject. The textbook is disorganized, the professor doesn't lecture, and exams are impossible to write to the prof's standards for all 4 questions in the given time.

Lectures are almost completely unrelated to exams, but attendance is mandatory. She never gave a rubric for essay exams, and for our 15-page term paper, the format requirements (changed margins and we all lost 1-2 pages) were changed a week before the due date. Nice woman and seemed to care about the course topic, just a little lazy unfortunately.

Don't get me wrong, Dr. Legare is a very nice person and she's very highly educated in her field, however attendance was mandatory so if you took one day off your grade would go down, she threw random assignments at us then later told us it was for extra credit, and the TA grades the exams harshly. Very insightful class but not the best I'd say.

Do not take this class. 6 exams, and you will literally never get comments on your exams or how to improve on your essays.  You wont even get your last exam grade back until you are already taking the next exam.  TA is a horrible and harsh grader for no reason.  You are never told what they are expecting for the exams so it is impossible to do well

analysis.name: Craig Campbell
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The class I took isn't on the list here. Dr. Campbell is one of my favorite professors. He cares deeply about the students and the course material. The class was more-discussion based, and he gave really insightful input. There are a lot of readings, but they're manageable, interesting, and very helpful to the big final project. Really cool class.

the professor would also always talk in circles and the pop quizzes were torture because even though I did all the required reading, the questions were always the most obscure random quote from page 3 line 4 from some book about some white guy studying people of color and then going and publishing a book about it for more white people to read

Professor Campbell is a wonderful and smart professor.  His lectures are pretty fun, he likes using technology.  Be prepared to talk a lot, he encourages students to be active talkers.  Be prepared to spent around $100 in his "the photographic image class" you will need to print a lot.  Grades are based on 2 presentations, 7 projects, participation

Honestly, I found his lectures to be boring. He would read material straight from the textbook. The videos that he played were cool, though. Attendance was mandatory due to the in-person quizzes. The discussion section was the only interesting part of the class, and my TA was more engaging than this professor.

Professor Campbell's ANT302 class was not difficult. He is super chill and a really cool professor, but his lectures are very wordy and theoretical. Someone said the same thing below but if you're not on the same wavelength as him, lectures are a bit hard to follow sometimes. Interesting class

analysis.name: Rowena Crabbe
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Great professor, she is extremely thorough with lectures and truly cares about the subject. HOWEVER, I would not recommend this as a UGS course simply because it requires SO MUCH WORK and you are better off in an easier one. We had reflections due weekly, all requiring a ton of reading (mainly academic articles that were hard to understand).

I LOVE DR. CRABBE!!! Yes, there is some reading and weekly reflections. However, Dr. Crabbe does her best to make it accesible and there's plenty of time to complete. She is genuinely so knowledgeable, and you'll leave with such a rich understanding and curiosity of marketing. TAKE THIS CLASS- you won't regret it.

Dr. Crabbe is an excellent professor, she explains things in such a clear way and makes you feel like your opinion matters. This isn't a blow off UGS, but still light work. It was genuinely one of my favorite courses this year because the content you learn and talk about matters. Highly recommend

Dr. Crabbe's Influence of Marketing in Society course was one of the most thought-provoking, enlightening, and engaging classes I've taken at UT. Each lecture functions as a time to discuss readings, and participation is a big part of your grade, but Dr. Crabbe makes it easy to do so! The amount of reading also lightens up throughout the semester.

Dr. Crabbe was the best professor I could've asked for. Her assignments were challenging but impactful, especially with the amount of time to submit each paper. It may feel like a lot of writing and reading at times, but her care and knowledge for what it's like to be a student makes her 1 of 1. Would definitely recommend, just be ready to read!

analysis.name: Robert Crosnoe
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 25 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Pretty easy and something you can put on the side. Discussion post every week and a short quiz over the lecture (3-5 questions that can range from 5-15minutes). A couple of papers, but the lectures are enjoyable to watch, and you can find them very relatable in your day-to-day life.

Crosnoe is the GOAT. Super sweet, pretty funny, and actually wants to get to know his students despite being online. Essays are so light. Quizzes get a little challenging at times, but it's nothing crazy. Biggest advice: go to his office hours! We talked about Hobbes for like 10 minutes and it was great! + he'll help you out w/ your grade if you go

Professor Crosnoe is a nice guy and I enjoyed talking to him one-on-one. My only issue is that I found it pretty difficult for me to focus in class during the lectures (which were live streamed). There is quite a bit of reading as well as quizzes and discussions for almost every class, but nothing too hard. Not a bad class overall :)

Sweet guy. 3 big papers due throughout the semester plus quizzes at the beginning of every class, instapolls, and chats for participation. The papers are pretty easy honestly you don't really need to pay attention to be able to do them and they don't grade super hard. You have to go in person once for participation credit. Didn't need the textbook.

The class itself is completely online, there are quizzes and participation discussions every class but very easy. He also gives instapolls during class, but not for a grade, just to see if you are paying attention. There are three main assignments during the curriculum, but he grades them very easily. Overall, the guy cares about your well-being.

analysis.name: Cristina Maymí
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: of course, spanish at UT is going to be a heavy course load. maymi makes it to where you feel supported throughout the course. took her over summer and during that my father passed away. she made it to where she was flexible with not only my work during that time but always checked in to make sure my mental was good as well. take her if you can!

I cannot express enough gratitude for Señora Maymí. I took SPN 610 last semester (not listed here), and her class was super engaging. Thanks to her support and recommendation letter, I got to study abroad in Spain and traveled around Europe. She's an amazing professor who continues to support her students even after the semester ends.

She's literally the sweetest professor ever! She genuinely wants you to learn Spanish, not just pass. Yeah, the class is a LOT of work, but she's incredibly supportive, and by the end, you'll actually know Spanish. I had a tough time toward the end of the semester, but was able to pull through and pass. We seriously need more profs like her. 10/10.

This professor was kind and you could tell really wanted to see her students succeed. She was flexible with late assignments and very understanding. This class was hard, but she made it easy because she's an amazing professor. This course load is heavy, but again, she was so helpful.

analysis.name: Ann Cvetkovich
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Material and readings 4 me were very interesting so long as u care about the topics. At times lectures felt somewhat contrived, but overall they were engaging and interesting. Essays are graded somewhat harshly but the feedback provided is helpful. I wouldn't say the class is an "free" A, but if u have a passion for LGBTQ+ issues it's a great class

She wasn't a very good lecturer, so the class would just be her talking nonstop about random things, and it was super boring. She was very rude and got mad easily. Don't even try emailing her, she NEVER answers. Her TA Gabriel was very harsh in grading. It seemed like they both didn't like each other & didn't want to be there. Syllabus unclear.

Dr. Cvetkovich is very passionate about her class but it doesn't necessarily translate into having an interesting class. The graduate TA, Gabriel, is a very harsh grader with vague rubrics so it's slightly hard to make an A. The field trips are interesting but a little irrelevant to the class. The readings are long & slightly boring & repetitive.

The content was interesting, but the lectures did seem to drag on, and the TA is not very nice. The grading was a bit harsh, depending on whether you got the TA or the professor as your grader. I would recommend taking this class if you have a genuine interest in the material rather than just for the credit.

Dr. Ann is an excellent professor. She is incredibly knowledgeable in her field and provides great feedback on assignments. Many experiential learning opportunities, which is very enjoyable. She appreciates honest participation and encourages questions. Course load is easy to manage, would recommend for UGS!

analysis.name: Craig Linder
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 75 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: MANY advised against him, but he really isn't bad. To be honest, I dont think I've ever learned more, (objectives are key for exam), but still his grading is hard. Exams: 1: 83, 2: 84, 3: 81, 4: 84. So in all you can get an A- with 80s, just do every homework (not that many), do every journal entry (easy points), quiz average was about 13/15.

Don't listen to the ratings on here. Just go to class and actually pay attention. I recommend rewatching the lectures and paying attention to the examples. The learning objectives are super helpful and the exams are basically written from them. It is a lot but things make sense if you actually try to understand. He is super nice and I LOVED him.

Dr. Kirkpatrick? A literal king—clear, caring, and makes lectures enjoyable. Then there's Linder: rushed, confusing, and painfully boring. His 30-question free-response tests feel like essays, and regrades? Don't bother. The vibe switch is wild. If this class were all Kirkpatrick, it'd be elite.

Was scared bc of reviews but I've learned a lot. Super lecture heavy - its easy to see the pattern of his tests. He often asks questions about the examples he puts on the slides. My grades so far Exam 1: 82 raw, 87 curved. Exam 2: raw + curved 89. He's nice + I think the people that complain don't actually come to class. Disc attendance mandatory.

Tough grader but willing to round up my grade that's off by 0.003 to an A. His exams are quite hefty and it is so important to keep up in his class by being readily prepared with lectures he post afterwards. Love that he rounded my grade up so I have to give him a 5, but prolly won't take him again 😭

analysis.name: Henry Curtis
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I honestly think for his first time teaching it really wasn't too bad. He was kind of rude and sassy at times and the course is strictly based off of tests. The tests were worded weirdly, and though he says that attendance was required, he took it ONCE. He would go off into tangents and I would get lost, so this course is pretty much self taught.

Attendance was mandatory but never taken except on TXOU weekend. Lectures were dull, off topic, and he often sat on his phone during group work. Exams had bad multiple-choice but okay short answers. He tries to make an intro class harder than it needs to be and said, "philosophy is as hard as chemical engineering". Overall a childish professor.

This class is very interesting if you are interested in thinking about how certain political/social problems in today's world work and how different ethical theories can be applied to them. There are about 3 weekly readings. There are 3 tests and they aren't too difficult as long as you understand the readings and attend lectures.

Extremely chill, accessible outside of class, very accommodating and did a fairly decent job at explaining readings. Lectures could get a little dry. He never actually took attendance tho and it was often difficult to participate because he sometimes goes off on tangents. Do the readings, sit front row and go to office hours.

I really enjoyed having Henry as a professor. His lectures were very funny, and his office hours were quite helpful. There was a decent amount of reading, but it was never impossible to manage. Our grade was made up of 3 exams and participation, which causes some pressure, but if you attend every lecture and do the readings you'll succeed.

analysis.name: Joe Cutbirth
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 39 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Really enjoyed lying and deception with Cutbirth. Class consists of weekly quizzes over the reading and 3 easy interview projects. Material itself is really interesting and Cutbirth allows for a lot of discussion (though not required). Attendance isn't tracked but he is a knowledgeable guy with a lot of cool experience so it's worth going.

A lot of writing (no exams) and a group project at the end. Not hard and a lot of flexibility with the "hybrid." The professor went out of his way to take some unconventional approaches with readings and "leaders," and that was cool. He's good to meet up with in office hours, too.

Worst class I've taken at this University. He makes the weekly quizzes very deceptive and tricky. Lectures are vague. Honestly I didn't know how to win and make a good grade in this class. I did all the readings and went to all the classes and couldn't make a good grade.

Super nice guy very straight forward. Take him literally when he tells you how things are done. He isn't very flexible on make-ups and excused absences. Has a great career with a lot of practical experience. See him in his office. He likes knowing who you are and what your interests are. And he will go out of his way to help if you're struggling.

I took both classes. Pretty informal but his standards are high. Quizzes  mini-exams with stuff from books but not lectures. He posts slides BEFORE the lectures, lets you drop two quiz grades and gives a good midterm and final review. Go to his office hours, but beware he can be a little chatty. Fake News was my favorite course yet at UT.

analysis.name: Douglas Cushing
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 50 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Not many assignments, but the ones that we had were not too easy, and not graded too easily either. 2 exams. Weekly HW "quizzes", but aren't bad. Lectures are really long, and he does not stop talking throughout. Meet once a week w/ TA, which was nice to get to talk to people about the class. Overall, not super hard, but it is a lot of content.

Decent VAPA. Yes, some assignments can be annoying if you're just looking to get your VAPA out of the way and don't care for art history, but quizzes/tests are easy—this class is a GPA booster (not honor-locked as of this semester). He's a genuine and knowledgeable professor, and TAs are understanding. Fast-paced lectures, not required though.

Dr. Cushing is such an amazing professor! He's very caring and moves essay deadlines when he feels that students need longer to work. There's 3 research-ish assignments and 2 exams- no final. Lectures are recorded and not required, but discussion sections are required. He's super sweet and makes great cookies. As an economics major, take his class!

From a person not pursuing a field in art history, this was a tough VAPA and very demanding. I do think that Dr. Cushing would be great if you are attempting to pursue a career in art history. His grading is tough, and often backloads a lot of grades, making myself predict what my final grade for the class will be. Funny Instapoll answer choices.

Professor Cushing is great! Easy class if you want to knock out your VAPA. The class itself consists of various writing assignments, exams, quizzes, and extra credit. Lectures are online so I literally attend it in bed. Discussions are mandatory and we are only excused 3 absences, but it is not hard at all and the TAs who run it are super chill.

analysis.name: Milica Cudina
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 34 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Cudina is an amazing professor! She is very caring for her students and her lectures are very comprehensive. Her notes are also very easy to read and are posted after each lecture on her website. Her tests can be a bit tricky but very doable. She also offered extra credit this semester and the assignment was very interesting. Would take again!

One of the nicest professors that I've ever taken. Super nice with everyone and helpful beyond measure,extremely conciderative as well. The class context is very difficult though If you really want to understand the class as she sort of expects you to have a general understanding beforehand, but getting a high grade isn't hard

The class covered some good content, and the majority of our grade was made up of the 3 midterms and optional final. She provides practice tests that give you a clear indication of what to expect for the actual exams..being able to solve those is a good indicator for how well you will do on the actual exams. The homework is challenging however.
Lectures were hard to follow, homework was really difficult, projects took a while, and exams were hard to prepare for. Still, she is the sweetest person on the planet.

I took her for M 378K and M 362K, but same rating for both. Very caring and friendly professor! M 362K is good Exam P prep, too. But do note that you will need to put a lot more time into the homework assignments. Not a free A, but you learn a lot even if you walk out with an A-. P.S. Free fruit snacks at her office hours :3

analysis.name: Molly Cummings
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 31 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Discussion section attendance mandatory (otherwise, lectures are optional). Botero and Cummings were both great lecturers, although only Botero provided study guides for the exams. The TA, Brittany, was very helpful throughout the course. Tests comprise ~80% of final grade. Exams mostly short-answer and fill-in-the-blank, class avg mid- to high-B.

I do not usually review, but she was the rudest person ever for no reason. This class was SO MUCH HARDER than it had to be. Attendance was optional but not rlly. Maybe people would come in person if she wasnt so mean and passive aggressive about it and cold calling on students who look confused. She didn't accept my accommodations?? Is that legal?

Dr. Cummings is so nice and always in good spirits. I took the class online bc covid so it may have been easier than normal. Tests were open note so I barely studied and did well. 1/4 of grade is a group research project where we were not given a rubric. There was a presentation and then a paper. I despise both research and writing but was fine

I love animal behavior but Dr. Hutchins/Dr.Cummings made it extremely difficult. their tests were way too broad and detail-heavy with some of the things never even mentioned in lecture. They don't even provide practice problems or even a study guide. Also complains about people not attending lecture when they are so uninteractive. Do better.

She seems to be a well-respected expert in the fish behavior world. Her lectures aren't confusing but they are dense with content, which can be hard for non-neuro majors. The content she emphasized the most in lecture was not tested on the exam, rather it was on minor/less-focused details. She does not provide practice problems nor practice exams.

analysis.name: Erin Cunningham
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Is overall a very skilled and caring teacher. I'm not a fan of sculpture, but I enjoyed learning new techniques and hearing her opinions in crit. Her class requires participation, but has a chill atmosphere and she'll check in on you to see if she can help with anything. Would definitely recommend.

Core class taken for studio art major, no way around it, but I appreciate Erin. She's pretty chill and even when I thought a student was being very disrespectful towards her she just laughed and went along with it. I personally don't like sculpture too much but I still found enjoyment in the projects and her critique for everyone thoughtful.

Erin is the best! I took her Sculpture for Nonmajors class. There were 3 projects (found-object, wood, and metal), and Erin really wanted to help us make pieces that we liked. Overall, a very fun, engaging, and informative class. I would recommend it to anyone.

analysis.name: Cynthia Penwell
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Great prof with field experience, but totally disorganized. Extensive weekly papers and a ton of readings she never touches on during lectures. She does mix students up A LOT and does not seem to know who is who. Besides that, she is an OG who also works in the field while teaching and is a brutally honest person, which is rare, and I appreciate.

Long weekly papers with no rubric and harsh grading. Only 2 allowed absences. She is not understanding yet is literally a SW professor. She mixes up students' names of the same race. She is so hard to work with. By far my most time consuming, repetitive class. DISORGANIZED! You will have to suffer for an A. DO NOT BE FOOLED BY THE HIGH RATING!

She's very respected and knows what she's talking about because she is so experienced in the social work field. She's very funny and kind. She is willing to work with those who have personal issues, and the class is mostly based on papers and a group project as well as attendance. LOVED her! One of the best professors I've had.

Penwell is a great, very caring, compassionate professor. I recommend taking her, she is truly interested in her students. Class does have a lot of tedious assignments, though, but I do learn a lot. Weekly papers, service learning requirement, and a big dyad project, which was interesting and you learn a lot, but you roleplay in front of the class.

Penwell is incredibly passionate! I appreciated her insights on SW. There are a lot of weekly papers, and the grading criteria can be unclear. Despite this, I really enjoyed the class! There's a group project 1/4 of your grade, which includes a roleplay aspect. I personally found it fun though! She cares a lot and is very accommodating, just ask!

analysis.name: Cynthia Marentes
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The professor is highly critical of students. While she gives feedback on all presentations (there are multiple), she always finds things to deduct points for. Her critique is subjective, even if you argue your points, she is unlikely to give you your points back. You will not receive a 100 on any presentation. Just take it online.

I took Prof. Marentes for Professional Comm. Studies in the spring semester of 2024 and she was amazing! There are quizzes after each chapter that are open notes, lots of presentations, and class participations. This class definitely helped me improve my presentation and communication skills. I thoroughly enjoyed her class and would take it again!
This class was interesting, no assignments were hard BUT she did grade hard.....

analysis.name: Cynthia Cabrera
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 73 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Cabrera is obviously very passionate about teaching. But she consistently gets practice problems wrong and explains concepts in overly complex ways. If you can do well with this teacher that means you already took calculus or you completely learned the course on your own time. AVOID AT ALL COSTS!

Just horrible at teaching, nice person and passionate at math, but she makes so many little mistakes while teaching it makes someone who already took calculus worse at calculus. Would not recommend. If you get this teacher I would recommend self teaching and tutors. Good luck.

She is a lovely person who cares about her work, however, she is not a good professor. She overcomplicates simple concepts and underexplains the more difficult ones. Exams are weighted heavily making the other assignments seem unimportant even when they take a lot of time. I would recommend avoiding her and taking calculus with another professor.

Getting in contact with her is very hard. She overcomplicates subjects, and her lectures are very hard to understand. Many of the assignments you do seem unrelated to what you are learning. In addition, on the tests, there is a lot of material that you will feel like you never learned. Take calculus with someone else.

She's incredibly sweet and you can tell she loves her job. However, she's not a good teacher. About 1/5 or of her students actually go to lectures because they're unhelpful, she's a confusing lecturer. Time is spent super inefficiently. If you reach out to her personally, she'll try her best but you'll have better luck self-teaching in this class.

analysis.name: Cynthia Talbot
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Talbot is a terrible teacher. Graded one of my assignments without her laid out rubric and instead by how much she liked the paper. The tests and quizzes have no relation to what you learn in class and requires extra prep for tests. If you're looking for an easy A, this isn't it. Too many assignments . She was often unsure on her history info

Dr. Talbot is a very good professor, the history course of the premodern world is very interesting, tests are in essay form, and both the professor and TA give good feedback. But reading, attending class, and paying attention to class and test preparation are very useful and important. Overall, very good professor.

Dr. Talbot is kind, intelligent, and she really cares about her students. She posts readings that will help you better understand, in-class review sessions before exams, extra office hours around exams, and she always helps out the best she can. Very fair. Great professor. I recommend.

analysis.name: Gabrielle Davis
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: After taking Dr. Davis' class I felt like I understood why I needed to be a nurse. learning how to communicate with patients helped so much in clinicals. it was hard at first but now I'm a UT BSN

Dr Davis is a great professor. Eventhough she didn't take attendace she knew our names. Some of the subject matter is boring, but Dr. Davis helped us understand why it is important to future nurses. She had great real world stories and sometimes she was even funny.

The teacher was very heavy grader on papers assigned and weekly quizzes, did not give any actual format or guides for students to look at, teacher claimed to want participation in the class however teacher was very prone to interrupting students during thoughts or discussions or would add on her own commentary.

Dr. Davis is one of the best professors I've ever had! She is such a caring and understanding professor. The course is organized extremely well and you know what to expect from day 1. There are two assignments, a group project, 4 quizzes (asynch), and 2 exams. This class was enjoyable and not a lot of work at all. Take her if you can!

analysis.name: David Mitlin
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The professor is disorganized and doesnt teach the material. He wastes class time doing his own assignments/literature reviews using Grok and ChatGPT, waiting several minutes for AI responses while the class sits idle, mumbling to himself through the 1.5-hour lecture w/out engaging students. I was excited for this course but left very disappointed.

ME 359 Materials Selection - Professor doesn't show up for office hours, late to class, poor assignments and lackluster content. Easy class, couple presentations, not too bad, just so extremely poorly executed.

His class should not be difficult but it is because of how nontransparent he is about everything. His lectures don't make any sense and he routinely cancels his office hours. Homework will not be over topics discussed in class and he never handed our tests back so I never knew my grade until after I took the final. Absolutely terrible.

This review is for ME359- Materials Selection. Other reviews are somewhat accurate: always travelling, but still made availability to help students outside class. Kind, goofy guy, very knowledgeable. Yes, there were only 3 assignments/projects, but I found them very interesting and not that bad.

Never available, always traveling, Only 5 total homework assignments with unclear solutions. Exams were straightforward and representative of the homework. Class was only graded on 5 homework, two exams, and the final. FINAL WAS WORTH 40%.

analysis.name: David Searle
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: genuinely one of the best professors I have ever had + he obv WANTS his students to succeed. I was worried about my grade going into this class since the reviews said that his class was hard, but as long as you go to class somewhat consistently and look over the slides for whatever you miss you will be fine. funny understanding & caring professor!

I was honestly really scared about my grade in this class after the first exam because it was hard. But, all the extra credit at the end raised my grade 4 points. Take advantage of the participation points you can get in class, they really helped my grade! Exams are curved well. Lectures are interesting and not too much work outside of class.

TOOK FOR BGS!! David Searle is genuinely THE best professor that I have had the privilege to experience here at McCombs! He genuinely cares about his students so much and about actually learning instead of just memorizing facts and information. He is such a genuinely good person and I highly suggest taking this course!

Searle was amazing and so kind! He made what could've been boring content fun because he includes the class and tells about his experiences. 

Tests were difficult but he gives a big curve luckily. For participation points, start them early so you get more extra credit. 

Side note but he kinda looks like Jim Carrey

took for BGS- genuinely one of the best profs ive had. Searle is just such a great human which i feel like is hard to come by these days. He cares for his students and you can tell he enjoys what he does. Searle is the GOAT and more profs need to be like him :)

analysis.name: Hugh Daigle
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Sweet guy and never gave us a lot of homework. He allows 1 page for cheat sheets and midterms weren't hard to get an A. Just review his slides and put everything on your cheat sheet. He also gave a super easy 10 point bonus question on a midterm once, so the average was like a 103. I am definitely going to take his sustainability course too.

Dr Daigle is awesome! Exams are very similar to homework and lectures and you get a cheat sheet. He curves HEAVILY. Lab reports are long and tedious (like 30 pages...), but you only have to do 3 ish and he is a light grader. He also pushes due dates if he feels there is too much on his students' plates. Very passionate about rocks!

Dr. Daigle is very wholesome. He is clear he is very passionate about teaching. Even though the topic is mostly boring, it is nice listening to his lecture. A single pop quiz in the semester. Homeworks were easy/graded generously. TAs were nice. Open note exams. The exams were straightforward, some math, some T/F. 3 lab reports were written.

Dr. Daigle's course is a great introduction to the many challenges that come with using more renewables. Assignments and presentations were straightforward, and the content was interesting. I would recommend this class to anyone who meets the prerequisites. Virtually all of the open note final could be completed by referencing the slides.
Great Professor, very easy class. Labs take a lot of time.

analysis.name: Eric Dewaal
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 55 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: This class took me through the 5 stages of grief and is the most difficult class I've taken. De Waal is a good lecturer but expects you to know A LOT and intentionally words his questions to be tricky. He also grades the free response extremely harshly so you lose points on little things. I managed to get an A by studying ~25 hours for the final...

This class was very difficult from the beginning. Exams are very specific and he expects you to know all of it. He gives a lot of study materials though, but just a lot of material on the exam, and very very oddly worded questions that are difficult to understand.

I really liked Dr. De waal even tho I dropped. He cares a lot about his students, but the exams killed me. I studied multiple days before each exam and didn't pass a single one. Content is interesting but very complex and memorization heavy. Taking with a diff prof next semester.

The exams were insanely hard. Sure, there was a lot of material, but he will nitpick on the specific criteria he determines for points for FRQs even though other open-ended answers are correct. He will take away any information that is 'incorrect'. The high school was not even a 100 for any of the exams except the easiest one (exam 4).

So much content and memorization, but he explained everything really really well which makes the content so much more digestable. Very organized professor and clear expectations. Quizzes come straight from homework and lecture questions, exams are a bit harder since they're longer and you really need to understand everything to do well.

analysis.name: Cynthia Labrake
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 129 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Basically, if you do homework on Canvas and go to class, this class isn't that hard. There is online polling that happens during class, but you can do that at home if you need to. Because of this, technically you don't need to go to class but I would suggest it. She's a pretty good teacher, even with the 200+ students class.

The structure of the course was changed this year to 8 exams, which causes you to spend more time studying throughout the entire semester. There is work for essentially every class. Labrake herself is quite scattered, requiring you to learn outside of class. However, her and especially Albert's reviews are worth going to and will help you on exams.

LaBrake is one of the best chem professors in the department. Her lectures are super engaging and she knows what she's talking about. She goes a little fast so you really have to do the homework ahead of time, otherwise you won't understand what's going on. She has a few options for bonus points on tests, so look out for those opportunities.

To even call her a professor I've had is a bit much since she used videos over a year old full of errors recorded at odd hours and videos she liked from youtube that replaced her lectures. I feel she tries to claim this is part of 'self-directed learning', but I feel there's a difference between encouraging learning and not teaching.

I learn by seeing the problem done step by step and explained why things are a certain way, but she does the problem on her own and I never know what I am doing. The textbook to me was not helpful at all. Goes too fast on the powerpoint and barley goes on a topic when all of a sudden she's on another.

analysis.name: Douglas Dempster
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This class was amazing! Coming in, I thought I knew what creativity was, but this class allowed me to reflect on and challenge my views. Prof Dempster taught us through a lot of fun activities, from scavenger hunts to movement labs. There are 10-minute talks that require you to give a presentation during your lab section, but they're not too hard.

The class was decent enough, though I feel the grading criteria is somewhat unclear. Once, I received a B on one of my assignments for “appearing to be stressed”. Additionally, Professor Dempster rarely got back to me when I asked for feedback. The course is simple enough, however, if you're in need of a UGS, I wouldn't take it with him.

His lectures are engaging, and he incorporates many interesting activities. However, he couldn't understand my paper, and the A threshold is 95, not 93. Ultimately, due to my final paper, I received an A- with a final grade of 94.7.

such a good professor. cancelled friday lectures for the last two months of class. easy readings and fun labs. great professor literally nothing bad to say. the creative notebooks are fun and easy to do and count as a big portion of the grade- he also encourages students to work on them during class. super interesting and engaging. HIGHLY RECOMMEND
Could not recommend more. Work can be pretty intensive, but stay on top of it, and you're in for an incredible experience.

analysis.name: Erik Dempsey
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 40 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: While I don't love philosophy, Professor Dempsey still made sure that the texts we read were interesting and relevant to a common theme. Class grades came through in-class essays and pop-quizzes which challenged you and forced you to study but were still very manageable. Lectures were not very engaging, but the discussion sessions made up for it.

Dempsey is fantastic. This was my first time taking a class with him, and he can be a harsh grader, but you really improve over the semester. Expectations are clearly laid out. Lectures were mandatory but always interesting. There are insane amounts of reading that you must keep up with to understand lectures. DO THEM. And talk to him out of class!

I have never taken any philosophy classes before this one and Professor Dempsey made the subject very approachable! Highly recommend him for CTI courses, he is a great speaker and is very knowledgeable. As long as you do the readings, take notes, and ask questions, you will be successful. Course is well-organized with clear expectations.

Dempsey is an amazing lecturer. I was introduced to so many new concepts through his lectures, and they genuinely made me think about the nature of the world. Definitely encourage speaking in class, as attendance/participation is graded, but he also has very interesting answers to questions. The readings are tough, but he explains them in class.

Passionate about Shakespeare, but format of  class is like  a remedial English class in HS because you are basically rereading your reading assignment in class with him. Because no one would willingly go to class knowing this, he makes attendance mandatory and takes off one point of your final grade per day missed. Notes required for absences.

analysis.name: Denne Reed
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 28 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Never take this class. Avoid it as much as you can. The professor is great, no issue with him. The class is boring, lectures are all 1hr long and there's almost more than 10 of them for each unit, the readings are extremely long and it is really hard to get a good grade on the exam because it asks for specific information. Avoid it.

WARNING! This class requires a lot of work, exams are based mostly on lectures, which are hours long and kind of boring...Don't take unless you know how to pace yourself and are ready for a lot of effort. Assignments and readings are easy enough tho.

The exams are proctored via Honorlock but open-note. If you actually watch the lectures, you'll get through. However, the lectures felt somewhat boring and they were 55-1 hour long each video. There were about 8-11 videos per unit (x5). There are several readings to do when taking the InQuizitives (homework), but they are not particularly too bad!

Even though exams are online and open note, they are proctored via Honorlock and are not open resource. The questions are so specific in these exams you pretty much need a word-for-word transcript of ever lecture, which is not allowed. This course takes way too much time for what it is. Would not recommend, especially as a science elective.

Professor Reed is a great guy who is passionate and caring. This course, however, was incredibly boring and frankly unnecessary. If you want to debate science, ethics, and philosophy, this class is definitely for you. Otherwise, I would not recommend it. It is incredibly reading and discussion-heavy.

analysis.name: Derek Davies
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: It was his first semester teaching and from what I can tell he has a lot of work to do if he wants to become a good professor. Exams gradually got more reasonable as the course progressed but the first one was horribly designed and it showed from the results. The workload was too much considering we had a project to design and create a RC car.

1st semester teaching course and it showed. Assumed class had way more knowledge from Solids and Statics. Lectures are just fully filled out slides. Unless you know exactly what to do at every step, exams are hard to finish. RC car project is ok, but the actual class work made it hard to focus on the project

Expects that we fully understand previous concepts from Statics and Solids with little to no review. Covered LOTS of material with not enough. On Exam 1 the average was still a failing grade after the 25 point curve. 1st semester teaching so somewhat understandable. Also had to build an RC car.

fairly boring if you aren't interested in the intricate specifics of engineering (coming from an engineering major), but if you just want to complete your UGS, this is great. Attendance is mandatory, but it's just a quiz posted online. There is one annoying group project building a Rube Goldberg machine, but other than that a pretty free class.

Prof Davies is so nice and obviously passionate about what he teaches. Assignments are short and easy writing explanations, 3 quizzes, and group projects. Grading criteria is super clear so follow what it says and u will get an A no questions asked. Attendance is taken at the end of class though so you do have to come and stay in class.

analysis.name: Dragan Djurdjanovic
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment:
Professor Djurdjanovic makes this class very accessible to someone with no background in programming. The class starts out quite slow, but about halfway through the semester difficulty skyrockets and you'll need to put in 10 hours of homework/labs a week.

It isn't hard, though—and extra credit makes the class an easy A.

Lectures really only explained the theory of what you do, not actually coding it, which made the homework tedious and reliant on self-teaching. The homework/lab assignments are fine, just long in the middle units of the course. Take-home tests are a blessing, though, so keep up with the class, and an A is very possible.

Phenomenal professor with some of the best lectures I've ever seen at UT. He is truly passionate about numerical methods and isn't afraid to show that. It's a shame that his TAs are among the harshest graders I have ever witnessed. One of his TAs reeked of sanctimony whenever she graded my assignments (ex. losing 5+ pts for wrong plot color/marker)

Dr. Djurdjanovic was incredibly helpful in and out of class. He answered questions well, and provided a lot of assistance understanding the material. He also offered a ton of extra credit. The material isn't very difficult, and all formulas are outlined clearly in the lecture notes posted to canvas. If you're stuck, go to office hours.
He likes to go on about his own research, but you can tell he loves the subject. He cares a lot about his students, especially if you go to office hours. Take him if you can

analysis.name: Dhiraj Murthy
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Great course & fantastic professor! He cares and is truly invested. All students should take his class because data privacy is becoming so important. Recommend getting txtbk online, hw is easy if you go to lab, and tests are tricky if you don't do optional quizzes. ATTENDANCE MANDATORY and can help push your grade if needed.

Every week we had to read about 30-50 pages of the textbook and take a quiz. There were two exams which covered very knit-picky details from the textbook so you had to take very good notes and study well to do okay. Professor was available. Wasn't prepared to have to do so much work for a class outside of my major.

Professor wanted students to recite textbook info through quizzes rather than learn course concepts and hardly provided genuine engagement. For this online course, he didn't provide video lectures or assignments outside of what came with the book ($135 and required). The course covered basic computer concepts and was not what was advertised.

analysis.name: Todd Ditmire
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
